questions.q: Essentially, this work is a play whose dialogue is sung instead of spoken. The performers act out the story onstage as an orchestra accompanies them from a pit. What is this drama set to music, examples of which are The Magic Flute and Carmen?

This man's Second Inaugural Address urged U.S. citizens to act, quote, "with malice toward none [and] with charity for all." At Illinois's Republican State Convention, he cautioned, quote, "A house divided against itself cannot stand." Identify this 16th U.S. president, who also wrote and delivered the "Gettysburg Address."
Use your knowledge of negative numbers to answer this question. Consider the number negative 5 and 632 thousandths (-5.632). What is the next integer smaller than negative 5 and 632 thousandths?

Applying force to an object will often produce a stress response in the form of a fracture or a break. What is the scientific term for the force required to stretch, pull or stress a substance or object to the point to just before it breaks?
This Kentucky college was founded in 1855 by a minister. It was the first integrated college in the South. What college is the site of the KAAC summer camps?

This musical element is the reason two different instruments playing the same note still sound different. Listeners may describe it as "mellow," "reedy," or "brassy." What is this characteristic sound of a particular voice or instrument?
How many words should be capitalized in the following sentence? Do you want to go to the movies on Saturday?

Happy Wheels Bike shop donated 36 tricycle wheels to the Wheels for Fun. Wheels for Fun needs two wheels for each tricycle that they repair. How many tricycles can be repaired with the donated wheels?

First proposed by Gallileo, this property of matter was used to describe horizontal motion. In simplest terms, it suggests that an object in motion will stay in motion and an object at rest will stay at rest unless it encounters another object or force. Name this property of matter.
Ten pre-state conventions were held in this city between 1784 and 1792. What Boyle County city hosted Kentucky's Constitutional Convention in April 1792?
This broad musical grouping includes pop, metal, jazz, and hip-hop. It applies to any music not meant for religious use. What is this opposite of sacred music?

This Newbery-winning novel blends science fiction with Mexican folklore. In it, Petra Peña becomes the only comet strike survivor who can remember what life was like on Earth. Name this novel by Donna Barba Higuera [hee-GAIR-uh].
This question requires multiple answers. Compute the first three positive multiples of 12.
Electromagnetic radiation is typically invisible without specialized instruments. What can be described as any sort of electromagnetic radiation that can be detected by our eyes?
This is the longest mountain system in the United States. What mountains located in the western United States contains several mountain ranges?

In appearance and construction, this instrument resembles the euphonium and the helicon. John Philip Sousa modified the instrument's design to create the sousaphone for marching bands. Identify this largest and lowest-pitched brass instrument.

This character is born on an island full of other so-called "unimaginary friends." He leaves for the real world, where he meets his human child Alice. Name this protagonist of a Caldecott-winning picture book by Dan Santat [SAN-tat].
This answer must be a mixed number in lowest terms. Determine the difference between ten and two-thirds and eight and one-sixth.

Oftentimes, people searching for precious minerals will come across a deceptive material that shines like metal in the sun. With a name that comes from the Latin pyr meaning fire, what is the scientific name of fool's gold?
Over 34% of the U.S. population is older than this age. What age people are a half-century old?

Dancer Martha Graham commissioned this ballet, which earned the Pulitzer Prize for Music in 1945. It dramatizes a 19th-century Pennsylvania pioneer celebration. Give the name of this Aaron Copland ballet.
This poet captured a child's perceptions in "My Shadow." He published that poem with more than 60 others in A Child's Garden of Verses. Name this author, who also wrote the novel Treasure Island.
The paper weighed 300 grams. What is the weight in grams of six percent of the paper?
Robert Dietz and Harry Hess developed a theory about the Earth's crust that involves crustal plates. What is the name of this theory that explains the why and how of volcanoes and mountains?
This group of Native Americans called themselves the Real People. They were also called cave people by the Mohawks. Who were these Native American people who used Mammoth Cave for shelter?

This element determines the sequence of a dance's events. Rhythm, tempo, beat, accent, and patterns all fall under this heading. Name this element that may be felt or may be strictly measured by a clock.

At the beginning of this novel, a 7-year-old plants a bag of magical crocodile tongues. The resulting tree bears fruit so massive that the boy crawls into it and floats from England to America. This is the plot of which Roald Dahl [ROO-all DOLL] book?
You must move your piece in 25 seconds in the game Faster is Better. Elijah moves his piece in one-fourth of a minute. How many more seconds could he have taken to move?

The solar system is made up of many moving bodies of various shapes and sizes. In ancient Greece, those who studied the night sky called one such group of bodies "wanderers". Which heavenly bodies change their position relative to the stars?
This colony was founded for religious freedom. What colony founded by Lord Baltimore provided a place for Catholics to worship?

This man earned Best Director and Best Choreographer Tony Awards for Fiddler on the Roof. He also choreographed High Button Shoes, On the Town, and Wonderful Town. Who was this choreographer of both the film and stage versions of West Side Story?

In some poems, this sound device has a so-called "scheme." Limericks and nursery rhymes have this element, but blank verse doesn't. What is this crafting of identical end sounds, as in "dog" and "frog"?
This convex polygon has ten vertices. It has ten interior angles. Which polygon has ten sides?

Cells are organized with small, working parts that work as a team to perform all of the functions of the cell. What is the name for these small components, examples of which are the nucleus, mitochondria, and lysosomes?
Kentucky was one of these states during the Civil War. What were slave states called that did not secede from the Union?

It took over 37,000 hours to create this musical's masks, puppets, and costumes. It features the songs "I Just Can't Wait to Be King," "Can You Feel the Love Tonight," and "Circle of Life." Identify this Disney musical in which Timon [tih-MOHN] and Pumbaa teach Simba the phrase "Hakuna Matata" [uh-KOO-nuh muh-TAH-tuh].

This tall tale man's younger--and much smaller--brother was Cordwood Pete. He set off from Maine and crossed the upper U.S., where he felled trees from the Midwest to the Pacific. Name this lumberjack owner of Babe the Blue Ox.
A triangle has one angle larger than 90 degrees. It has two angles that are each smaller than 90 degrees. Based on the size of the angles, what name is given to this triangle?
This type of grass is of the genus Poa and is native to Europe, Asia, Africa, and North America. What is the common name for this type of grass, most well-known for being abundant in Kentucky?
This civil rights activist's actions started the Montgomery bus boycott. What seamstress refused to give up her seat to white passengers on a city bus in 1955?

Encaustic painting mixes this heated substance with pigments. Batik [buh-TEEK] produces fabric patterns by taking advantage of this substance's resistance to dye. Identify this material made artificially from petroleum or naturally by bees.
The Latin root "aqua" is part of the words "aquarium" and "aquatic." Give its English meaning.
Mrs. Jenkins needs to buy enough quilt binding to go all the way around a quilt. She is making a quilt that is 36 inches long and 24 inches wide. How many inches of quilt binding does she need?

Zoologists use this term to describe an organism with three pairs of legs, three body divisions, and typically two pairs of wings. They also have exoskeletons. What is the general name for this group of invertebrate animals which include flies, mosquitoes, fleas and beetles, to name a few?
This national legislative body meets in the Capitol in Washington, D.C. What lawmaking body includes the U.S. House of Representatives and the Senate?
During the Renaissance, oil paints largely replaced this type of paint. It forms a film as it rapidly dries. Give the name of this paint made of pigment, water, and egg yolk.
As a verb, this word can be a synonym of "abandoned" or "departed." Identify this word that, as an adjective, is the opposite of "right."
Tommy needs to choose what he will wear to school tomorrow. He can choose from 4 shirts, 2 pairs of shorts, and 3 pairs of shoes. How many possible outfits can he choose?

This substance is considered organic because it is produced by a living thing and is formed from partly organic substances. What is this precious gemstone, often found in certain mollusks, such as oysters?
This document is issued by the U.S. government to its citizens. What document allows citizens to travel outside the country?
Multiple answer required. They created the Mona Lisa, a marble David, a bronze David, and The School of Athens. Which four Renaissance artists lent their names to the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles?
Identify the complete subject of the following sentence: The talented, graceful ballerinas twirled across the stage.
A number sequence begins 1, 2, 5, 10, 17 Find the next number in the sequence.

The human body is comprised of multiple systems working together. The cardiovascular system, for example, is responsible for transporting nutrients throughout the body. What major system of the human body provides support and protection?
This tax is usually due on April 15th. What tax is collected by the IRS?

This painting premiered at the Spanish Republican Pavilion during the 1937 World's Fair in Paris. In black, white, and grey tones, it shows a bull, a horse, and anguished people. What was this protest of a Basque village's bombing, created by Pablo Picasso?
How many prepositional phrases are part of the following sentence? The puppy at the park ran around the tree and down to the pond.
This question requires multiple answers. Identify the constants in this equation, "x plus 3 equals 23"?
Literally translated, this term means the study of things high in the air. What is the term for the study weather?
This speech was delivered at the dedication of a cemetery. What speech by Abraham Lincoln begins "Fourscore and seven years ago"?

Some Native American tribes in California traditionally built this vessel out of reeds. More common examples were the dugout and birch bark varieties. Identify this slender, open boat that made war, trade, and transport easier.
Spelling required. A new bicycle was my reward for earning straight A's. Spell the word in the preceding sentence that is a synonym of "prize."
Multiple answers. Consider the equation: 4x plus 3y equals 24. What are the variables in the equation?

This 19th century Swedish scientist worked in a military equipment factory during the Crimean War. During this time, he began experimenting with explosives. Name this scientist, the inventor of dynamite, for whom yearly prizes for physics, medicine, and chemistry are named.
This funeral was attended by royals, world leaders, and other dignitaries. It was watched by millions over live television. What monarch's funeral was held on September 19, 2022?
How many apostrophes should the following sentence contain? She's going to ask her sister to clean up their brother's mess before their parents get home.
This property of real numbers combines multiplication and addition. What property allows you to multiply a number by each of the addends inside the parentheses before adding the addends?
Symbols in this musical category may look like a hole, a top hat, a chicken's beak, or the number 7. Name these symbols that call for a period of silence.
This geographical region borders the Cumberland Mountains and the Eastern Knobs. What region includes most of what people call Eastern Kentucky?

A sample of a material can be molded or shaped into many forms due to its malleability. What is the term for the physical property, similar to malleability, for a material's ability to be drawn or stretched into a wire?

In this novel, Star Children consume starlight before moving into the Free Cities. Xan the witch saves abandoned babies, including Luna, a girl she accidentally enmagicks with moonlight. Identify this Newbery winner by Kelly Barnhill.
Mica lives in Elizabethtown and is traveling to Frankfort which is 64.04 miles away. How many miles will Mica travel for the round trip?
This musical word comes from the Italian for "tied together." It means notes should be played or sung in a smooth, connected way. State this opposite of staccato [stuh-KAH-toh].
All of this man's sons fought in the War of 1812 and served in the Kentucky General Assembly. After helping write Kentucky's Constitution, what man became the second Governor of the Commonwealth?
A car is traveling sixty miles per hour. At this speed, how long would it take in minutes for the car to travel 45 miles?

This picture book was based on the life of its author's great-grandfather. Subtitled The True Story of the World's Most Famous Bear, it recounts how a cub moved from Canada to the London Zoo. What is this Caldecott winner written by Lindsay Mattick and illustrated by Sophie Blackall?
Samson's teacher said that he could solve the problem if he knew the number of factors of 24. How many factors does Samson find in the number 24?

Before the Kentucky Derby, a trumpet plays one of these compositions. French horns and drums can also perform these short, showy pieces created for special events. Identify this brief musical formula heard during battles, hunts, and presidential or royal ceremonies.
Four great Americans are commemorated in this sculpture. It is located in South Dakota. What colossal sculpture was created by Gutzon Borglum?

This device stimulates atoms and molecules to produce light of a certain wavelength. It then takes the light energy and focuses it into a single beam with a very high amount of energy. What is the name of this kind of light device that, when high powered, can cut through metal or, when lower powered, is used in pointers and light shows?
This short poetic form creates strong natural imagery. Its 17 syllables are divided into lines of 5, 7, and 5. Identify this 3-line Japanese poem.
In order to solve this problem, you must convert a mixed number to an improper fraction. What improper fraction is equal to 21 and one-half?

This four-stringed instrument comes in soprano, concert, tenor, and baritone sizes. A member of the lute family, it descends from the Portuguese machada. What is this chordophone associated with Hawaii?
This travel can cause positive and negative effects on the environment. What is travel for pleasure that can help improve an area's economy?

Volcanic eruptions have been a source of geologic change throughout the history of Earth. As magma erupts through the surface and flows onto the crust as lava, it begins to cool, leaving new rock behind. Which type of rock is formed by lava and the remains of volcanic eruptions?

In this novel, the title character competes against Veruca Salt, Violet Beauregarde, Mike Teavee, and Augustus Gloop. By being the best-behaved child, he inherits the title business from its owner, Willy Wonka. Name this Roald Dahl [ROO-all DOLL] work.
Happy Elementary has an enrollment of 65 percent females. What percent of the school is male?

This man included "Gun Battle" and "The Open Prairie" in his ballet Billy the Kid. "Saturday Night Waltz" and "Buckaroo Holiday" are part of his ballet Rodeo. Identify this 20th-century composer of Fanfare for the Common Man.
People of this nationality explored and settled Canada. They established many fur trading posts in the Northeast. What people settled Quebec?

This element is found in large supply in the Earth's crust. It is a major building block of ceramics and bricks, but its conductivity makes it a key component of transistors. Name this element, second only to oxygen in order of abundance in the Earth's crust.

This literary element drives the plot because it gives the protagonist obstacles to overcome. It can be either external or internal. Name this element, examples of which are person versus self and person versus nature.
Peter picked a peck of 125 pickles. If Peter picked a bushel of pickles, how many pickles would he have picked?
This element of dance might be powerful or gentle, heavy or light. Tension, flow, weight, attack, and force are part of it. Which element dictates how a movement happens?
The Lords Proprietor used this tactic to convince settlers to move to Carolina. What was this method of granting 150 acres of land to each new settler of Carolina?

As the moon cycles through its phases, there are times when it seems to be getting smaller in size. What word, the lunar opposite of waxing, refers to these phases of the moon, particularly between a full moon and a third quarter moon?

This fable's title now refers to a person who raises a false alarm. It warns the reader, quote, "No one believes a liar, even when he is telling the truth." What is this Aesop fable about a young shepherd who loses his flock to a predator?
The teacher draws a triangle on the board. She draws a little square in the corner of this triangle. What type of triangle with one 90 degree angle did she draw?

This man's dance company performed world premiere works by Lester Horton, Pearl Primus, and Katherine Dunham. His works, including Blues Suite and Revelations, highlighted the experiences of African-Americans. Identify the founder of the American Dance Theater.
According to Senator James Hammond from South Carolina, this plant was King. What primary crop of Southern plantations was used in making clothes?
This cell part functions as a barrier and support for both plant AND animal cells. Name this part that is semi-permeable, allowing some substances to come in while keeping others out of the cell.

This nursery rhyme character shares his name with a character from Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass. Many illustrations show him as an egg, although the nursery rhyme only mentions his fragility. Who, after his great fall from a wall, couldn't be put back together again by the king's horses and men?
By definition, this angle has less than 90 degrees. What is an angle that measures 30 degrees?

In ancient Greece, this genre's most famous playwrights were Aeschylus [ES-kuh-luhs], Sophocles [SOF-uh-kleez], and Euripides [yoo-RIP-i-deez]. Its hero has a character flaw that causes his or her downfall. What is this opposite of comedy?
This Texan had trouble getting a job as an attorney because she was a woman. She was nominated to the Supreme Court by President Reagan. Who was the first woman to serve on the U.S. Supreme Court?
Plants typically have both male and female structures that allow for pollination. What is the collective term for the part of the flower that is made up of the stigma, style, and ovary?
This Latin prefix means "not." Identify this prefix that can precede "stop" or "fat."
A carton will hold 12 small boxes. Each small box has a volume of one-half cubic inch. What is the volume of the carton in cubic inches?
One explanation for this specific element of art is, quote, "the areas where the subjects are positioned." An artwork's background is not part of it. State this opposite of negative space.
This panel of citizens decides if there is enough evidence to charge someone with a crime. What is this special jury made up of 12 people in Kentucky?

Two word answer. This animal is the largest of the group of animals known as crustaceans. Name this animal whose typical habitat is off the coast of Japan and whose legs can measure up to 12 feet in length.

This word may refer to a large, sturdy chest for storing or transporting clothes or other belongings. In the U.S., it names the large storage space in the back of a car. Give this word for a tree's main stem or an elephant's long nose.
A spinner is divided into 4 equal sectors with each sector a different color. The colors of the sectors are red, blue, green, and purple. What is the probability of the spinner landing on purple?

Art movements that began in this country include Rococo, Pointillism, and Cubism. It was also the home of the Fontainebleau [fawn-ten-BLOH] and Barbizon [bar-bee-ZAHN] Schools. Which European nation was the site of the first Impressionist Exhibition?
The president states a pledge to defend this document in his oath of office. What document must every citizen defend?
They were the first vertebrates to fly. What is the general name for the extinct flying reptiles with an extremely long forelimb digit supporting a membrane-like wing.
What is the simple subject of the following sentence? The aluminum ladder grew slippery in the rain.
Find the next number in this sequence. The sequence begins 1, 1, 3, 7, 13… What is the next number?

This ancient statue's sculptor was Chares [KAH-reez] of Lindos. It was made of bronze and reinforced with iron, and once stood beside a Greek island's harbor. Identify this Wonder of the Ancient World.
When your parents borrow money from a bank to buy a car, they must pay the bank back. What four letter term means the money that is owed back to the bank?
Digestion in the human body is the chemical process of converting food into useable energy. What class of corrosive chemicals turn litmus paper red and work to break down food in the stomach?
The affirmative, or positive, type of this sentence is the English language's most common. It always ends with a period. Give the name for a sentence that makes a statement.
Solve this equation for x. 2x plus 6 equals 16.

This large portrait features a border of orange, red, and blue dots next to a specially-made white frame. It shows people of different social classes mingling at a park in the Seine [SEN] River. Give the name of this Georges Seurat [ZHAWRZH suh-RAH] masterpiece.
questions.a: SUNDAY AFTERNOON ON THE ISLAND OF LA GRANDE JATTE [GRAHND ZHAHT] (Accept (A) SUNDAY ON LA GRANDE JATTE (--1884))

questions.q: "We the People" begins this part of the Constitution. It ends with "establish this Constitution for the United States of America." What is this short introduction to the Constitution?
Nuclear power plants have become a powerful source of zero emission clean energy. What element is most commonly used during fission by nuclear power plants to harness energy?
Spelling required. Philosophers use logic to prove their arguments. Spell the word in the previous sentence that is a synonym of "reason" or "sense."
Gino has ten pencils and five pencil holders. He divides the pencils equally into the pencil holders. How many pencils will be in each pencil holder?

This folk character once fooled Sis Cow into giving him a drink of milk. In another story, a temper-tantrum caused his hands and feet to become stuck to a tar-baby. Give the name of this Uncle Remus trickster figure who sometimes outwitted Br'er Fox.
He founded Microsoft in 1975 with his friend. He is an American computer programmer. What wealthy entrepreneur is known for his charitable work?
In 1774, this element was discovered by Joseph Priestley. What element, atomic number 8, is necessary for animals to carry out respiration and has the chemical symbol O?
The chef cut the dessert into 24 pieces. He serves 8 pieces to the customers. In lowest terms, what fraction of the dessert was served?
This element of music might be andante, adagio [uh-DAH-zhee-oh], or allegro. What is the word for how fast or slow a piece of music is played or sung?
"I have a dream," said this man during the March on Washington in 1963. He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964. What African American civil rights leader was assassinated in Memphis, Tennessee?

In chemistry, substances can be altered in a number of ways. What is the general term for the type of change that can only be observed when the material undergoes a reaction in which it has different properties and new substances are formed?

In this Newbery-winning novel, Lily and Sam move with their mom into their Korean grandmother's house. Lily makes a deal with the title animal to save her grandmother's life by returning stories her grandmother stole. Give the title of this Tae Keller book.
A standard six-sided die has 3 odd numbers and 3 even numbers. What is the probability of rolling an even number using that die?

This American roots music with English, Scottish, and Irish roots is played on acoustic instruments. Among those instruments are the dobro, fiddle, mandolin, and banjo. Identify this Appalachian folk music native to Kentucky.
This northern region of the Commonwealth gives Kentucky its nickname. What region is named for the dark green grass that covers the pasture lands?
Mechanical energy is the sum of two different types of energy. One of these types of energy, kinetic energy is energy in motion. What is the name for the other type of energy, energy at rest?

According to this picture book's opening line, the title substance, quote, "is the first medicine." It tells of an Ojibwe girl's fight against an oil pipeline. Identify this book written by Carole Lindstrom and illustrated by Michaela Goode.
When grouping addends to compute a sum, this math property can be used. What property of addition states that the sums of 6 plus 4 added to 3 equals the sum of 6 added to the sum of 4 plus 3?

Brahms used text from the Book of Psalms for his German one of these works. Mozart's student completed his after the master composer's death. What is this music written for a Catholic service to honor the dead?
All fifty states have state birds, but this state was the first to choose one. What state chose the northern cardinal as its state bird in 1926?

The sun is the greatest source of energy on earth and most forms we see can be traced back to it. Of the two types of energy that cannot boast their origins in the sun, one, nuclear, is a product of fission or fusion of elements. Give the name for the other that derives its power from deep in the Earth.

This poet created such characters as Marvin K. Mooney, Bartholomew Cubbins, and the Lorax. Yertle the Turtle, Horton the elephant, and Fox in Socks also appear in his rhyming picture books. Who created the Grinch and the Cat in the Hat?
Your academic team is selling tubs of cookie dough for $12.00 per tub. Every member must sell $96.00 worth of cookie dough. How many tubs must each member sell?

This instrument may have originated from a keyboard attached to a psaltery. Popular in the Renaissance and Baroque Eras, it plucks strings when its keys are pressed. Give the name of this precursor to the piano.
Every meridian and the equator are examples of these circles. What circle drawn on a globe divides the globe into two equal halves?

Pressure under the surface of Earth's crust can cause cracks that allow steam and water to escape. Water can force its way through these cracks in a violent manner, erupting almost like a volcano. Give the name of these hot springs, the most famous of which is located in Yellowstone National Park.
This author of Eight Cousins called its sequel Rose in Bloom. Her best-known works are a trilogy focused on Jo March and her family. Give the name of this Little Women creator.
Twenty-four swimmers were practicing for their swim meet. Eight swimmers left the pool for a break. What fraction of the swimmers remained in the pool?

This so-called "father of the string quartet" was, with Mozart, a leading Classical Era composer. He pleased his hometown of Vienna with the oratorios The Creation and The Seasons. Name this composer of over 100 symphonies, including Clock and Surprise.
This state is the most visited state in the U.S. It has big cities, large amusement parks, and many beaches. What state's most famous tourist spots include Disneyland and Hollywood?

When the air temperature and dew point are within three degrees of one another, a common weather phenomenon occurs. Name this phenomenon, typically seen early in the morning, that is notable in London.

Works in this broad category include newspaper articles, diary entries, and travel writing. Biographies, histories, and essays also belong to this group. What is the word for writing that is about true people and events?
The math exam has 50 questions. Leonard answered 15 questions correctly. What percent of the exam did Leonard answer correctly?
This movement category encompasses crawling, climbing, and sliding. Jumping, hopping, and leaping are also examples. Give the word for movements that transport the body from one place to another.
The first settlements in this U.S. state appeared around 300 - 600 AD. Polynesians were the first to settle on this island state. What state did James Cook explore in the 1700s?
Not counting the dwarf planets, it is the smallest planet in the solar system. Having an average orbit of 88 days and a composition of mostly iron, name this planet, the closest to the sun.
This folk hero's real name was John Reid. He wore a black mask, rode the horse Silver, and called his sidekick "kemosabe" [kee-mo-SAH-bee]. Identify this cowboy friend of Tonto.
This measurement is the standard metric measurement for length. It is equal to 1000 millimeters. What measure is equal to 100 centimeters?

While dancing as a soloist with the Kirov Ballet, this man defected to the West in 1961. He spent his last decade as artistic director and, later, chief choreographer of the Paris Opera Ballet. Name this frequent dance partner of Dame Margot Fonteyn [MAR-go fawn-TAYN].
This war was one of the bloodiest conflicts in the colonial period. What 1715 war is named for the tribe of Native Americans who lost their lands to the Carolinians?

First discovered in viewing a slice of cork through a microscope, these structures were noted to resemble the rooms of a monastery. Name these structures, the smallest units of life, that comprise every living being.

In this fairy tale, Maleficent curses a small princess to die on her 16th birthday. Instead, that girl pricks her finger on a spindle and slumbers for a century. Name this story in which a prince's kiss awakens Aurora.
A right triangle has sides of 3 inches, 4 inches, and 5 inches. Based on its side lengths what type of triangle has no equal sides?

New songs written for this musical include "These Palace Walls" and "Diamond in the Rough." Like the Disney movie on which it's based, it features sorcerer and grand vizier Jafar. Name this musical with Princess Jasmine, a flying carpet, and a wish-granting genie.
In 1861 representatives from seven seceded states formed a new constitution for a new government. What was the name of the new government of the Southern states?

In exchange for a bit of nectar, a honeybee lends aid to plants in the form of pollination. What type of relationship occurs when two organisms interact, with both receiving mutual benefit from the relationship?
This word's Greek prefix means "three." Its Greek root means "wheel." What is this word for a three-wheeled form of transportation?
This quadrilateral has two pairs of equal sides. A rhombus is a special type of this quadrilateral. What type of quadrilateral has the equal sides next to each other?

This art medium comes in compressed, vine, and powdered varieties. Painters use it for rough sketches, but artists also spray fixative on it to preserve finished drawings. Name this carbon derived from heated wood, which is also used for grilling food.
This Henry Clay High School graduate is the son of a past Kentucky governor. What man is the 63rd governor of Kentucky?

During pollinations, honey bees gather nectar for energy and storage. Once the bees return to the hive, they deposit the gathered nectar and it is broken down into simple sugars for storage. What is the name of the structure of wax containing rows of 6-sided cells made by bees to store their honey?
The first half of this word names our planet. The second half is a synonym of "tremble" or "shake." Name this type of natural disaster.
A bag of mulch will cover 5 square feet. Sally has a flower garden that is 5 feet on each side. How many bags of mulch will she need?

This movement's artists included Jasper Johns, Roy Lichtenstein, and David Hockney. Centered in New York, it used comic books, street signs, celebrities, and consumer products as subjects. Identify this 1950s and '60s movement associated with Andy Warhol.
Every citizen of the U.S. must pay his share of this money to run the country. What is the money citizens pay to the government to help support the country?
While this animal is a bear, it closely resembles a raccoon and has similar characteristics. Identify this large mammal, native to Asia, whose diet consists mainly of bamboo.
Which words in the following sentence need to be capitalized? Rome is the capital of Italy, a country in Europe.
A geometric sequence begins 1, 3, 9 … Determine the next number in the sequence.

Like perspective, this art technique can make two-dimensional paintings and drawings seem three-dimensional. It heightens the drama of works like Caravaggio's The Calling of St. Matthew and Rembrandt's The Night Watch. Leonardo's Lady with an Ermine uses what strong contrast between light and darkness?
This is the central bank of the United States. What central banking system has twelve regional banks?

The skin, the largest organ of the human body is responsible for protecting us from infection and disease. What body system is our first line of defense against our external environment and includes the skin, glands, hair and nails.
State the following sentence's complete predicate: The newest Lego set is complicated to assemble.
Solve this equation for x. X plus 0 equals 17.

By the late 1940s, this artist was laying canvases on the floor as he poured enamel or aluminum paint on them. This technique earned him the nickname "Jack the Dripper." Name the Abstract Expressionist painter of Autumn Rhythm and Lavender Mist.
Three word answer please. The American flag has this nickname. What nickname describes the design of the red, white, and blue flag?
Solving problems through inquiry is an important part of the scientific process. What step in the scientific method includes making an educated guess about the outcome of an experiment?

The English language's shortest grammatically correct sentence is this type. Depending on the severity of its tone, this kind of sentence can end with either a period or an exclamation point. What is this sentence that gives a command?
Using mental math is often faster than using pencils and paper. Use mental math to determine what number must be divided by nine to equal 8.

This Native American ceremony's name comes from the Algonquin word meaning "he dreams." During part of it, tribe members in animal skins, feathers, and beads dance to drum music. What is this communal celebration of one or many Native American cultures?
U.S. Forces killed this most wanted terrorist on earth in 2011. What al-Qaeda leader was responsible for the 9/11 attacks?

This scientist was so intrigued by the work on early telescopes that he began experimenting with ways to prevent the light distortions that were typical. Instead of using prisms as other scientists had at the time, he began using different mirrors. Name this scientist, who developed the reflecting telescope, and who is widely credited with discovering gravity after observing a falling apple.
Spelling required. Pardon me for disturbing your meditation. Spell the word from the preceding sentence that is a synonym of "forgive."
This type of note has a solid head and a stem with no flags. Identify this note that receives one beat in 4/4 time.
This man linked virtue with happiness in his First Inaugural Address, delivered in 1789. He warned against political parties in his 1796 Farewell Address. Identify the United States' first president.
Cici and Jeremy are flipping a penny to decide who will be captain of the team. Cici likes tails and calls tails as the coin is flipped. What is the probability that the coin will land on tails?

In science, physical properties can be observed through the natural observation of matter. One of these physical phenomenon is produced by the motion of electric charge. Which property of matter varies depending on the attraction of unlike poles?

Butler, Union, and Daviess counties are found in this geographical region. Most of the surface mines in this area are located in Hopkins, Muhlenberg, and Ohio counties. What is this area of Kentucky known for its coal production?

This sacred music style gave rise to both soul and rhythm and blues. Rooted in call-and-response, it developed from hymns, spirituals, and slave work songs. What is this African-American Christian music?

To date, this book is the only graphic novel to win the Newbery Medal. In it, aspiring artist Jordan Banks adjusts to the culture of his private school, Riverdale Academy Day School. Name this book written and illustrated by Jerry Craft.
This question requires multiple responses in correct order. Place these numbers in descending order: 63, 27, 57.
questions.a: 63, 57, 27 (NOTE: MUST BE GIVEN IN THIS ORDER)

questions.q: A ball placed on an incline will not simply slide down the ramp due to an opposite force. What is this force that causes a ball to roll instead of simply sliding down the ramp?
Kentucky's state seal contains these six words. What is the state motto of Kentucky?
questions.a: UNITED WE STAND, DIVIDED WE FALL

questions.q: Performers of this traditional music genre wear short jackets, wide bow ties, boots, and sombreros. They play brass instruments, violins, and guitars as they stroll around. Name this music genre native to Mexico.

This Caldecott-winning picture book retells a Brothers Grimm fairy tale. In it, a witch locks a young girl in a tower with no stairs or ladder. The heroine lets down her long hair in what Paul O. Zelinsky book?
Respond with a decimal. Jeremy ate one-half of the pizza and Joey ate one-fourth of the pizza. In decimal numbers, how much of the pizza was eaten?
questions.a: 0.75 (OF THE PIZZA) (ACCEPT: 75 HUNDREDTHS OR POINT SEVEN FIVE)

questions.q: In electricity, wires often have the ability to resist current. When current cannot move through a wire due to high resistance, what net effect will be observed on conductivity?
This lake is one of the Great Lakes. It is the second largest by volume. Which Great Lake is the earth's largest lake by area in one country?

This instrument's name is Italian for "little goose." It is a globular flute shaped like an egg or sweet potato and features finger- and thumb holes. Identify this folk instrument, whose name appears in a Legend of Zelda video game.
A special type of this poem is the abecedarius [ay-bee-cee-DARE-ee-us]. In what kind of poem do the first letters of each line spell out a word when read vertically?

Only one-fifth of the theater was filled before the play began. When the curtain rose, two-thirds of the theater was filled. As a fraction, in lowest terms, how much more of the theater was filled when the curtain rose?

The theory of plate tectonics suggests that the crust of the earth is made of plates that float along the surface beneath and are constantly moving. What is the name for the layer, located just below Earth's crust, that allows plates to drift and from which magma originates?
This state encourages a type of tourism to visit its natural environments. What state's ecotourism includes cruises to Kenai Fjords National Park?

Like Beethoven, this man's music bridged the Classical and Romantic Eras. He called for a violin, viola, cello, double bass, and piano in his Trout Quintet. Whose more than 600 songs included "Gretchen at the Spinning Wheel" and "The Erl King"?
This author's works for children include The Witches, Fantastic Mr. Fox, and The BFG. He also created a highly intelligent six-year-old girl with telekinetic powers. Identify the writer of Matilda.
Mini-Donuts sold 25 baskets of donuts. Sarah bought two-fifths of the baskets. How many baskets of donuts did Sarah buy?

Two word answer. Disturbances in the magnetosphere caused by solar winds create lights that appear as curtains, rays, spirals, or flickers. Usually seen close to the Earth's North Pole, give the name of this phenomenon in the northern hemisphere known as the Northern Lights.

These explorer/hunters traveled in groups of two or three. They were hired by land surveyors to guide people into Kentucky and Tennessee. What are these hunters who included Daniel Boone and James Harrod?

Movements of this type include bending, stretching, twisting, and rocking. By definition, at least one body part always remains in contact with the floor. What kind of movement doesn't transport the entire body through space?

A person in this literary role may have a limited or an omniscient [ahm-NISH-unt]--that is, all-knowing--point of view. They can speak in the first, second, or third person. What do we call the voice that tells a story?
There are 80 students in the fall enrichment class. Seventy-five percent of the students chose to study origami in their art class. How many students chose origami for their art class?
In 1990, the space shuttle Discovery released a satellite of sorts into space. Identify this orbiting, reflecting telescope that was built to send data from space to Earth using radio waves.
This American patriot was a journalist and scientist. He became wealthy after starting a printing business in Philadelphia. What statesman published Poor Richard's Almanack?

This performer of both classical ballet and modern dance had the leads in the ballets Vestris and Gorianka. He shocked the world by defecting to the West while dancing in Toronto in 1974. Give the name of this man, who spent most of the '80s as artistic director of the American Ballet Theatre.

This tall tale character was based on a real man who supposedly wore a coffee sack cloak, a tin can hat, and no shoes. In 1802, he set off in a canoe to give fruit seeds to Wild West settlers. Name this man remembered for the orchards he planted.
The hallway is 300 centimeters longer than the library. The library is 8 meters long. How many meters long is the hallway?
These one-celled organisms produce carbon dioxide through fermentation. Give the name of these simple organisms that are responsible for bread rising.
A group of Texans fought a battle for their independence here. What is the name of the mission in San Antonio that you should "remember"?

Among this musical's songs are "Little Girls," "It's the Hard Knock Life," and "Tomorrow." Miss Hannigan and her brother Rooster try to get rich using the title red-headed girl. Daddy Warbucks adopts a spunky orphan in what musical based on a comic strip?
This Latin prefix can come before "pone," "mark," or "card." Identify this prefix meaning "following" or "after."
Every triangle contains three angles that add up to this sum. What is the sum of all three angles of a triangle in degrees?
It is the compartment of a flower where a sugary substance is held to attract insects. What name is given to this glandular part of a flower, similar to the name of the substance it holds?
President Johnson signed this act into law in 1965. What act banned literacy tests as a barrier for voting for African Americans?
This element of art plays a large role in impasto paintings. The visual kind is simulated, while the physical kind is tactile. Which element controls how an artwork feels or looks like it would feel?
The first half of this word is an antonym of "dark." The second half is a synonym of "residence." Identify this word for a tall tower that shines brightly to guide ships into port.
A rectangular rug measures 12 feet by 10 feet. What is the area of the rug in square feet?

One of the most well-known examples of this process is in caterpillars. Caterpillars wrap themselves in a cocoon spun of a silky web in order to transform into a butterfly. What is the scientific term for this process by which one organism completely changes in form and function?
Kentucky ranks fourth in the nation for the number of these land divisions. What 120 local governments in Kentucky include Fayette and Jefferson?

Filippo Brunelleschi [fee-LEEP-oh broo-nel-LES-kee] designed this architectural feature for Florence Cathedral. The Taj Mahal [TAZH muh-HALL], Pantheon, and U.S. Capitol also have this element. Give the word for part of a roof shaped like an overturned bowl.
How many commas should appear in the following sentence? She loves purple nail polish, but her mom prefers pink.
Bob the Builder wants to build a raised garden. The garden plot measures 4 feet by 6 feet. In square feet, determine the area of the raised garden.
A human has a gestation period of about 280 days. The giraffe has a gestation period of close to 450 days. What land mammal has the longest gestation period at around 660 days?
This important duty of citizenship must be obeyed. What regulations should every citizen obey and respect?

This fresco decorates the wall of a convent's dining room in Milan, Italy. It shows Jesus seated at the center of a long table with his disciples on either side of Him. Give the title of this mealtime group portrait, created by Leonardo da Vinci.
Give the following sentence's simple predicate: Petra returned early from her trip to China.
A certain geometric sequence begins with 2 and the second number is 4. The fourth number is 16. What is the third number in the sequence?

Healthy individuals experience cell growth and division at a continual rate in order to maintain good health. When cells do not divide properly, many different diseases and conditions can occur as a result. What is the term for the life-threatening condition in which cells within the body replicate irregularly and/or uncontrollably?
This government agency makes money. What agency makes coins used for spending?

This Renaissance artist's adopted last name translates as "little barrel" in Italian. He illustrated a biblical scene in The Madonna of the Pomegranate, but also painted Greek and Roman myths. Who created La Primavera and The Birth of Venus?

Teachers warn students not to use this kind of sentence in academic writing. It can express anger, frustration, excitement, or other strong emotions. Identify this sentence that ends with an exclamation point.
This question requires multiple answers. What are the coefficients in the mathematical expression: 15x minus 3x?
The head of an axe is a wedge while the handle is a lever. Give the name for this type of machine made up of two or more simple machines.
This national treasure symbolizes freedom, inspiration, and hope. France gave this statue to America. What statue welcomed immigrants to America for many years?
questions.a: STATUE OF LIBERTY (ACCEPT: LIBERTY ENLIGHTENING THE WORLD)

questions.q: This god's sons are named See-Trouble, Road-Builder, River-Drinker, Game-Skinner, Stone-Thrower, and Cushion. He is a shape-shifting trickster who migrated from West Africa to the Caribbean and the American South. Name this keeper of stories, who often resembles a spider.
Spelling required. If you walk too quickly on slick pavement, you may take a tumble. Spell the word in the previous sentence meaning "fall down."
Please Excuse My Dear Aunt Sally. This mnemonic will help you solve math problems. According to the mnemonic what should you look at first to solve an equation?
questions.a: PARENTHESES (ACCEPT: SIMILAR RESPONSE USING THE WORD PARENTHESES OR PARENTHESIS)

questions.q: First and last name required. This Los Angeles native became an author of children's science books upon her retirement. As the only person to serve on the panels that investigated both the Challenger and Columbia Space Shuttle accidents, she was integral in determining the cause and effect of both. Name this NASA retiree, the first American woman to go into space.
This Russian president declared a military offensive on the Ukraine. Who is the current president of Russia as of September 2022?

This novel's heroine is a Cuban-American rising sixth grader at Seaward Pines Academy. She deals with class bully Edna Santos, mentors her Sunshine Buddy, and learns that her grandfather Lolo has dementia. What is this Newbery Medal-winning novel by Meg Medina?
A spinner is divided into six equal sectors. There are two orange sectors and one sector each of red, green, white, and blue. What is the probability that the spinner will land on pink?
This musical element is measured in Hertz. Some musicians have an "absolute" or "perfect" sense of this element. Name this word for how high or low a note is.
This large geographical region stretches across the southern border of Kentucky. What geographical area is named for the small purple plant that grows there?
An example of these observeable changes is watching ice melt into water. What sort of change occurs when a material retains its composition but changes in appearance.

In this picture book, the title characters rescue dragons that are about to be slayed and lure the cat and the fiddle out of their nursery rhyme. They leave their own fairy tale, thereby escaping the Big Bad Wolf. Straw, stick, and brick houses play a role in what Caldecott winner by David Wiesner [WEEZ-nur]?
This question requires multiple answers in correct order. Place these whole numbers in ascending order: 101, 100, 111
questions.a: 100, 101, 111 (NOTE: MUST BE GIVEN IN THIS ORDER)

questions.q: In the 1970s and '80s, fusion musicians combined this genre with rock and Latin music. Swing, big band, and Dixieland were styles in this genre, which grew from spirituals, blues, and ragtime. Name this genre of Miles Davis and Louis Armstrong.
This governor started Governor's Cup with her executive order. Who was the only female governor of Kentucky?

If you tie a bolt to the end of a string and whip it around your head, the bolt will not drop out of nowhere to hit you as long as it is in constant motion. What force prevents the bolt from continuing in a straight line away from your head, or likewise hitting you?
This poet probably wrote "Annabel Lee" as a memorial to his wife Virginia Clemm. In another work, the speaker spends a bleak December night talking to a bird. Identify this poet of "The Raven."
The beaker in the science lab holds 1 liter. Sharon's teacher added 0.38 liters of water to the beaker to fill it. How many liters of water were in the beaker before the teacher added the water?

This single- or double-reed instrument has a chanter and, in most cases, at least one drone. Bellows or a tube push air into a sac that the player then squeezes. Identify this instrument from the Scottish Highlands.
This land feature is formed by mud and sediment. What is the region where the continental shelf slants down to meet the ocean floor?

The sun produces energy that travels to Earth as electromagnetic waves. Unlike sound waves, waves from the sun can transfer through a vacuum. Give the collective name for the sun's energy type that includes microwaves, radiowaves, and light energy.

This author's Chronos series is also known as The Austin Family Chronicles. Likewise, her Kairos series is sometimes called The Murry-O'Keefe Family Chronicles. Name this science fiction and fantasy author of A Wrinkle in Time.
Old McDonald's farm is divided into 15 fields. He plants corn in two-thirds of the fields. How many fields are planted in corn?

One kind of this percussion instrument, the bell lyre, is used in marching bands. Like the xylophone, it contains rows of tuned bars that are played with mallets. What is this high-pitched, German-named instrument with metal bars?
This factor can increase population size. What is the movement of individuals from another country into the United States?

As a river flows into slower moving, shallow bodies, sediment is churned up and deposited into areas where they join. What is the name for these triangular-shaped wetlands that form at the mouths of rivers?

This literary element can be illustrated by Freytag's [FRY-togz] Pyramid. Its parts include exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, and resolution. Give the name for a story's sequence of events.
Eleven Girl Scouts attended the music jamboree. Seven of them bought souvenirs. What fraction of the Girl Scouts bought souvenirs?
In this opera, a wife dresses as a boy to free her husband from prison. Leonore's plan succeeds and Florestan escapes his death sentence. Give the title of this only Beethoven opera.
Usually, these people were of French or Spanish and African descent. They were born in the West Indies. What word beginning with "C" describes these early Latin Americans?

Catastrophic flooding is often caused by excessive rainfall over a short period of time. Another contributing factor is also the total discharge of water by surface streams. What two-syllable term refers to this phenomenon that is made worse by removal of trees through logging and strip mining?

In this Aesop fable, the Fox agrees to judge a competition between the title animals. One of those animals naps through most of the contest, letting the much slower competitor win. Which Aesop fable illustrates how, quote, "The race isn't always to the swift"?
questions.a: (THE) TORTOISE AND THE HARE (Accept (THE) HARE AND THE TORTOISE)

questions.q: The animal shelter has 48 puppies and 12 kittens. Determine the ratio of kittens to puppies.

This dance first appeared in the 1830s in the lower-class ballrooms of Paris's Montparnasse [mohn-par-NASS] district. By the 1890s, music halls like the Moulin Rouge [moo-lahn ROOZH] had popularized it. What was this high-kicking dance performed by a chorus line wearing black stockings and petticoats?
This Governor of Virginia rallied support for the Revolution with his speeches. What patriot is best known for his words, "Give me liberty or give me death!"

The Earth's atmosphere is gaseous in nature, allowing organisms to carry out respiration. The atmosphere is made up of only about 20% oxygen and 1 % trace gases. What gas makes up the other 79 percent of Earth's atmosphere?

Like Little Red Riding Hood, this fairy tale character took an unchaperoned stroll in the forest. After coming on an unoccupied house, she ate porridge, sat in chairs, and fell asleep in a bed. Name this girl who was frightened by three bears.
One bedroom is 6 meters long and the kitchen is 2 meters longer than the bedroom. The second bedroom is 3 meters shorter than the kitchen. How many meters long is the second bedroom?

This student of Martha Graham was once co-artistic director, with Mikhail Baryshnikov [buh-RISH-nuh-kawf], of the American Ballet Theatre. For Broadway, she created and choreographed the dance revues The Times They Are A-Changin' and Come Fly Away. Who set dance moves to Billy Joel's music in Movin' Out?
This lumber mill was the site of a discovery that led to a rush to move to California. What mill was the site where gold was discovered?
THis group of compounds in animals stores energy and forms most of the cell membrane. What is this class of macromolecules that includes fats, oils, and waxes?
The Greek root "therm" is part of the words "thermometer" and "thermostat." Give its English meaning.
This two-dimensional closed shape is constructed with straight line segments. Examples of these polygons include squares and rectangles. What polygon has four sides and four vertices?

People with this theatrical job description may move scenery, keep track of props, or operate lighting or sound systems. They are the stagehands and other behind-the-scenes people who keep a show running smoothly. Name this group that, together with the cast, makes up a theatrical company.
This African American was an agricultural scientist and inventor. What man became known as "The Peanut Man" for his work with peanuts?
In a flower, once this part is fertilized, a seed will be produced. What is the name of this female flower part that shares its name with a term for a human egg?
One word in this homophone pair is a synonym of "beloved." The other word names a vegetarian mammal with cloven hooves and, in males, antlers. What is the shared pronunciation of these words?

Mr. Jones needs to fence his rectangular garden to keep the deer away from the vegetables. One side of the garden is 40 feet and the second side is 16 feet. What is the perimeter of the garden in feet?
Multiple answer required. Each secondary color in art is a mixture of two primary colors. Name the three secondary colors in art.
questions.a: ORANGE, GREEN, (AND) VIOLET (any order) (Accept PURPLE in place of VIOLET)

questions.q: Kentucky's legislature is this type. So is the national legislature. What is a legislature with two chambers called?

They belong to a larger group of animals known as arthropods; animals with exoskeletons and jointed legs. They have 2 pairs of appendages in front of the mouth and paired appendages near the mouth that function as jaws. Name this group of animals whose best-known members are shellfish lobsters and crabs.
This punctuation may have begun as an uppercase Q written above a lowercase O. Name this punctuation that ends an interrogative sentence.
The toy dump truck has a bed that is 5 units wide and 5 units long. Tommy filled the bed with sand to a height of 2 units. What is the volume of the sand in cubic units?

This artist used the sfumato [sfoo-MAH-toh] technique to create the smoky atmosphere in Madonna of the Rocks. He explored the human body's proportions in his pen and ink drawing Vitruvian Man. Identify the Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa.
questions.a: LEONARDO DA VINCI (Accept first, last, or both)

questions.q: Any citizen can choose to do this so they can help lead the country. What right includes being nominated and campaigning?
questions.a: RUN FOR PUBLIC OFFICE (ACCEPT: SIMILAR RESPONSES)

questions.q: Nearly all small animals in this biome are burrowers and nocturnal. Among its North America species are the creosote bush, roadrunner, and gila monster. Defined by having little vegetation as a result of low precipitation, name this biome that supports the camel and the cactus.
Identify all the predicate adjectives in the following sentence: Those high heels look expensive and uncomfortable.

Janice put 45 cupcakes on the first table, 54 on the second table, and 63 cupcakes on the third table. She continues the pattern to the next table. How many cupcakes will she place on the fourth table?

Pope Leo the Tenth commissioned this Renaissance artist to lead the building of St. Peter's Basilica. His most famous painting shows Plato, Aristotle, and other philosophers from ancient Greece. Identify the artist of The School of Athens.
This happens when prices rise across an industry. What rise in prices means a decline in purchasing power over time?
Movement of this muscle creates a pressure gradient in the abdominal cavity of humans. What is the term for the thin muscle sheet whose movement causes the lungs to expand and contract?
This type of sentence shares its name with a class of pronoun. It can be direct or indirect and requests information from the reader or listener. Name this sentence that ends with a question mark.
The value of variables in an algebraic expression can change. What is the variable in the algebraic expression 3y?

From the 16th to the 18th century, educators in both Britain and America used this type of children's primer. With a wooden frame shaped like a tennis paddle, it held vellum or paper with the alphabet and Roman numerals written on it. Identify this teaching tool named for the thin, transparent plates of animal tissue that protected it.
This document issued by Lincoln did not end slavery in the U.S. What proclamation declared "all persons held as slaves … shall be free"?

Mass is the measure of the amount of matter in an object while weight is the measure of the amount of gravity acting on an object and is measured with scales. What laboratory device is used to accurately measure the mass of an item?
Spelling required. The statue is perched on a steep mountain. Spell the word from the previous sentence that names a landform.
What number is three-fourths of 200?

This actor voiced Shaggy in Scoob! and Chase in PAW Patrol: The Movie. He earned a Young Artist Award for playing the title role in the prequel to The Big Bang Theory. Name this star of Young Sheldon.
This actress made news in 2018 when she married a prince. What wife of Prince Harry is now the Duchess of Sussex?

When observing cork through a microscope, this scientist compared what he saw to the rooms that the monks lived in. Name this man who noticed that the pieces looked like individual units separated by walls and coined the term cells.
These integers are greater than zero. What kind of whole numbers are illustrated by such integers as 34 and 19?

This part of sheet music has a name meaning "key" in French. It helps a musician determine which lines and spaces of a staff stand for which notes. Identify this part of music, which might be treble or bass.
This farming community in Kentucky is named for noise. It is located on a migratory path of the buffalo. What town is named for the sound of thousands of stamping buffalo waiting to drink?

Atoms are made up of small particles that give them their elemental properties. Name the subatomic particle, located in the atom's nucleus that is close in number to the number of protons and carries no charge.

The author included Filipino-American character Virgil Salinas in this novel to celebrate her own heritage. Its other characters include bully Chet Bullens, deaf Valencia Somerset, and psychic Kaori Tanaka. Identify this Newbery winner, written by Erin Entrada Kelly.
The recipe called for 0.375 cups of orange juice. As a simple fraction, in cups, how much orange juice should he use?

This music genre drew on Appalachian folk, Cajun, Latin, and African-American influences. Originally called hillbilly music, it grew throughout the Southern U.S., with its headquarters in Nashville. Identify this genre of Willie Nelson, Patsy Cline, and Dolly Parton.
Mother Ann Lee was the founder of this religious movement. What religious group of "shaking Quakers" founded a settlement at Pleasant Hill?

This type of simple machine has a thick edge tapering to a thin edge. As the machine is driven into a space, it will separate or split an object or objects. Name this type of simple machine, of which an axe head, knife, and chisel are examples.

In this Caldecott-winning book, a girl learns about the famine her mother's family endured. The girl picks the title plant from a ditch and, after cooking it, eats it for dinner. Name this book written by Andrea Wang and illustrated by Jason Chin.
The art teacher draws lines on 5 plates to divide each plate into 6 sections. Students in the first class paint 18 of the sections. What fraction of the sections did the class paint?

The so-called "steel" version of this instrument requires a steel bar to move against plucked strings. Other types include the bass, classical, acoustic, and electric. What is this typically six-stringed instrument played by Jimi Hendrix and Carlos Santana?
This strip of land is constantly changing. Even calm ripples along a beach can change it. What is the strip of land bordering the sea?

As you lift a box from the floor to a shelf, you transfer energy to the box to overcome the force of gravity. The transfer of energy that occurs when a force is applied over a distance is known as what scientific measure?

This type of long narrative poem originated in prehistoric times, where it was passed down orally. Often set in multiple places, it follows a hero's quest or journey. Name this genre of Homer's Iliad and Odyssey.
Samson uses a loaf of sourdough bread to make sandwiches. He cuts the bread into ten slices and uses eight slices for the sandwiches. What fraction of the bread did Samson use?

Although this instrument is made of wood, musicologists group it with the brass family. It is a long, hollow tube that produces a low drone when the player blows into it. Name this Australian Aboriginal instrument.
This industry in the United States has been decreasing. What is the industry that includes growing crops and rearing animals for food?

As water drips through cracks and crevices in a cave, it picks up small particles of limestone in each drop. As these drops hang from the ceiling of the cave and the water evaporates, the limestone particles are left behind, forming spikes along the ceiling. What is the scientific name for these spikes that can be seen hanging from the ceilings of caves?

This author wrote several novels about Anastasia Krupnik and four more books about her brother Sam. She also created Caroline Tate and Gooney Bird Greene. Who is this Newbery-winning author of The Giver Quartet?
A zoo has three polar bears and five manatees. What is the ratio of polar bears to the total number of polar bears and manatees?

The composer wrote these six works for Christian Ludwig, the Margrave of a Prussian territory. Each one showcases a small group of instruments and uses counterpoint. What were these Johann Sebastian Bach works?
This colony was not the first English colony founded in America. It was founded in 1607 in present-day Virginia. What was the first permanent English settlement in the Americas?
In the water cycle, this process occurs between evaporation and precipitation. What is the name of this phenomenon that occurs in Earth's atmosphere when water vapor forms clouds?

This literary element can be macro- or micro-. It might include the characters' general environment, as well as their geographical location and historical time period. Give the word for when and where a story occurs.
An oak tree in the park is 4 meters tall. A maple tree is 4 meters taller than the oak. How many centimeters taller is the maple tree than the oak tree?

This dance became popular with flappers in the 1920s. Arm swings and forward and backward steps characterize this dance, which later merged with the Lindy Hop. Identify this dance named for a coastal South Carolina city.

This war began in 1754 and ended in1763. The main cause of the war was whether the Ohio Territory was under British or French control. What was the American phase of the war between France and Great Britain?
questions.a: FRENCH AND INDIAN (WAR) (DO NOT ACCEPT SEVEN YEARS' WAR)

questions.q: Draco is an example of this specialized formation of celestial bodies that maintain their shape over the course of centuries. What is the name of these specialized groups of stars, of which Ursa Minor is another example?

Native American names for this legendary creature include Wendigo, Witiko, and Sasquatch. It is the North American equivalent of the Himalayan Mountains' Yeti or Abominable Snowman. Identify this large, hairy, apelike creature that supposedly leaves massive tracks around the Pacific Northwest.

A square is an example of this quadrilateral. All of its sides are equal in length. Its opposite sides are parallel and its opposite angles are equal. What quadrilateral is sometimes called a diamond?

This so-called "god of dance" was a soloist with the Mariinsky Theatre. He performed Michel Fokine's [mi-SHEL foh-KEENZ] choreography in the premieres of The Specter of the Rose and Schéhérazade [shuh-HAIR-uh-zod]. Name this choreographer of The Afternoon of a Faun and The Rite of Spring.
The attack on this fort was the official beginning of the Civil War. Where did General Beauregard's Confederate troops defeat Union troops to start the war?
This happens when normal liver cells are replaced by connective tissue cells, resulting in heavy scarring. What is this disease usually associated with alcoholism?

In one nursery rhyme, a boy with this first name pulled out a plum while eating a Christmas pie. In another, a man with this name ate no fat, but his wife ate no lean. Give this name of the boy who went with Jill to fetch a pail of water.
An equilateral triangle measures 35 inches on each side. What is the perimeter of the triangle in inches?

This dramatic term comes from 19th-century theater directors' practice of working out staging with mini models. Today, actors and directors establish it during rehearsal. What is the word for the onstage placement and movement of actors during a performance?
The United States declared war on this country after it bombed Pearl Harbor. What island country started World War Two in China?

These organisms form the base of the food chain. After dead and decaying leaves, insects, and animals are left on the soil surface, these organisms are responsible for breaking them down into useable pieces again. GIve the name of these organisms which break down dead and decaying matter to return the nutrients to the soil.
Correct the following sentence, if needed: Every Saturday, my brother and sister shops for groceries.
A regular septagon measures 7 units on each side. Determine the perimeter of the septagon.
For artistic forms, this adjective applies to the cube, sphere, and pyramid. For shapes, it applies to the circle, square, and triangle. What is this opposite of organic forms and shapes?
Only one state has a unicameral legislature. Which western state has a single house legislature?

Air and water movement within soil is important for agriculture and some organisms help this by churning up the soil so that air and water can mix through. What invertebrate, in the phylum Annelida, improves soil by making tunnels so that resources like air and water can move through with ease?
Spelled one way, this word is a synonym of "story." Identify this word that, spelled another way, names the long appendage on a cat's or dog's rear.
There are five purple marbles and one green marble in a bag. If you draw a marble without looking, what is the probability that the marble will NOT be green?

Paintings of this type include Cezanne's Mont Sainte-Victoire [mohn sant veek-TWAR] and Van Gogh's Wheatfield with Crows. Constable's The Hay Wain and Monet's Poplars are further examples. Give the word for an artwork that showcases natural scenery.
An addition to the Constitution guarantees this right to citizens. What right does the Second Amendment of the Constitution protect?
questions.a: (TO) KEEP AND BEAR ARMS (ACCEPT SIMILAR RESPONSE)

questions.q: The first of the three germ cell layers to develop in an embryo, it is responsible for the integumentary system. Two parts of this are the neural crest and neural tube, which form most of the nervous system. Name this outermost layer in developing embryos, located outside the mesoderm and endoderm.
Which of the following sentence's words should be capitalized? My science teacher, Miss Harris, is getting married next spring.

A bookshelf in the library had 2 red books on the first shelf and 4 red books on the second shelf. The third shelf has 8 red books and the fourth shelf has 16 red books. If the pattern continues, how many red books will be on the fifth shelf?

Art critic Louis Leroy said one of this man's sketchy landscapes reminded him of wallpaper. That artist also painted Rouen [roo-AHN] Cathedral and haystacks in different seasons and at different times of day. Name this Impressionist artist, whose Giverny [zhee-vair-NEE] garden inspired his Water Lilies series.
This decline in spending can last for months or years. What economic condition is less severe and shorter than a depression?

Appearing in both red and yellow varieties, this tissue comprises a small percent of our body weight. What is the spongy, interior portion of bone whose main function is to build red and white blood cells?
Every word in this part of speech is either concrete or abstract. Some are proper, while others are common. Identify the part of speech that refers to people, places, things, and ideas.
Substitute 23 for the variable in the following expression. What is the value of the expression 126 plus y?

This so-called "father of American music" lends his name to a state park in Bardstown. He wrote the music and lyrics for songs like "Camptown Races," "Jeanie with the Light Brown Hair," and "Oh! Susanna." Who wrote our state song, "My Old Kentucky Home"?
This residence is located at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue. What is this People's House where the president and first family live?

Changes in atmospheric pressure can allow meteorologists to predict upcoming weather. What instrument, once typically made with mercury, is used to monitor impending weather fronts through changes in pressure?
Identify the grammatical structure of the following sentence: They formed a new committee to research the problem.
A rectangle has a length of 2.7 units and a width of 5 units. What is the area, in square units, of the rectangle?

This craft of the Ashanti people displays bright colors and patterns with symbolic meanings. Originally worn by royalty, today anyone can wear it for religious or ceremonial occasions. Name this cloth from Ghana that has come to represent African-American pride.
This athletic competition showcased the Bird's Nest. What games were held in Beijing in in the summer of 2008?

This English astronomer and physicist was the first to publish a chart of prevailing winds across the globe in 1686. He collaborated with Isaac Newton in the shape of orbits in planetary motion, but his best known contribution to astronomy was in his work with other celestial bodies. Name this scientist who correctly predicted the 1758 return of his namesake comet, 76 years after the last previous sighting.
Spelling required. Do you believe in miracles? Spell the word from the preceding sentence meaning "to have faith in."
Like scales and keys, this aspect of music can be major or minor. Many examples, called triads, are made of three notes. Give the word for a combination of two or more notes played at the same time.

This activist delivered his "Our God Is Marching On" speech after leading a march from Selma to Montgomery, Alabama. His final speech, delivered in Memphis on the day before his assassination, was titled "I've Been to the Mountaintop." Who was this reverend and civil rights activist remembered for his "I Have a Dream" speech?
A spinner is divided into four equal sectors. One sector is green, one is black, and two sectors are orange. What is the probability that the spinner will land on orange?

Whether an object will sink or float in a liquid depends on how the mass is spread out over the object's volume. Name the property of matter whose value for water is 1 and which is calculated by dividing mass by volume.
This cave is the only UNESCO World Heritage Site in Kentucky. What giant cave system is home to many endangered species?

Mendelssohn composed a "Wedding" one of these works, while Elgar's "Pomp and Circumstance" is one heard at many graduations. John Philip Sousa was the so-called "king" of them. Name this strongly-accented music played by military and school bands.

This Newbery-winning novel is set in the Kingdom of Dor. The title animal saves his love, Princess Pea, from a kidnapping plot. Name this Kate DiCamillo [dee-kuh-MILL-oh] novel about an exceptional mouse.
questions.a: (THE) TALE OF DESPEREAUX [DES-puh-row] (BEING THE STORY OF A MOUSE, A PRINCESS, SOME SOUP AND A SPOOL OF THREAD)

questions.q: This question requires multiple answers. These numbers can be found to the left or right of zero on a number line. What two types of numbers are called signed numbers?

In order to describe position, location is typically stated relative to this point. For example, you may say that your house is ten blocks east of the center of town. What is the name for this point, the starting point you choose to use to describe the location or position of an object?
Louisville, Kentucky was the boyhood home of this President of the United States. What twelfth President is buried in the family cemetery in Louisville?

In the pedal kind of this instrument, the strings are alternately colored red and black. The lever type is smaller than the pedal type, but both have triangular frames. Name this large instrument whose vertical strings are plucked.

This man earned a Caldecott Medal for illustrating Norton Juster's book The Hello Goodbye Window. He won his second Caldecott for creating a nearly wordless picture book about a dog and her favorite toy. Identify this author and artist of A Ball for Daisy.
Mr. Persinger needs 200 Language Arts Quick Recall questions. Writers have submitted 0.8 (eight-tenths) of the required questions. How many questions have been submitted?

In a game of basketball, this type of energy increases when a player applies force to shoot the basketball. On the other hand, a pot of water doesn't see this value increase when it is heated on the stove. What is this term for the total energy of an object or group of objects due to large-scale motions?
St. Louis, Missouri, is the home to this giant structure. It is the earth's largest man-made arch. What "Gateway to the West" was designed by Eero Saarinen?
This Baroque violinist was nicknamed "the Red Priest." He taught music to orphaned girls and wrote a set of four concertos. Who composed The Four Seasons?

This phrase names a poetry book that contains "Boa Constrictor" and "Ickle Me, Pickle Me, Tickle Me Too." It is also the title of a poem about a place where, quote, "the grass grows soft and white," and, "the sun burns crimson bright." Give the name of this poem and book by Shel Silverstein.
Kwan has 10 pieces of colored paper to make origami birds. He folds two-fifths of the paper into birds. How many birds did Kwan make from the paper?

As stalactites and stalagmites form in the chambers of caves, they continue to grow as long as there is a drip of limestone water. As the water continuously drips and the structures get larger, they will, at times, join to form a new cave feature. What is the name of this feature of a cave, formed when stalactites and stalagmites join together after extended growth?
These areas of the United States have open country spaces and small settlements. What term, according to the U.S. Census Bureau, has fewer than 2,500 residents?
This student of Salieri [sal-ee-AIR-ee] spent his early career as a piano virtuoso. Later, he wrote the Faust Symphony and Transcendental Études. Name this composer of Hungarian Rhapsodies.

This winner of Hans Christian Andersen and Laura Ingalls Wilder Awards titled her first novel Zeely. Arilla Sun Down, Justice and Her Brothers, and Sweet Whispers, Brother Rush were three of her novels for young people. Identify the author of The Mystery of Drear House, the sequel to The House of Dies Drear.
Kroger sells apples and oranges in a ratio of 4 apples to 2 oranges. The grocery sells 8 apples in one hour. How many oranges are sold in that hour?

These huge masses are formed from heavily compacted snow and ice. Identify these crushing masses of ice with the ability to "flow" like a river, moving very slowly and significantly changing the landscape of the Earth.
