There were 30 tribes in his chiefdom when the English arrived in the New World. What leader of this chiefdom was the father of Pocahontas?

This basic ballet position provides a foundation for the pirouette [peer-oh-WET]. The dancer evenly divides her weight between both feet, which are in turn-out. Name this position that places one foot about 12 inches in front of the other.
Sibilance is a special type of this sound device. That device is found in the sentence, "Go and gather the green grapes." What is this repetition of initial consonant sounds?
The moderator ruled Shelley's answer incorrect. Shelley had answered the ratio question by saying "six to twelve." In order to be correct, what simplest form of the ratio should Shelley have said?

Nearly nine and a half times wider than Earth, this planet boasts no solid surface, despite being 90 times more massive than the third rock from the sun. Surrounded by layers of ice particles, this planet is known for its giant moon, TItan-- and its many other moons! Give the name for this planet which shares its name with the father of Jupiter, and which is known best for its rings.
This Spaniard accompanied Pizzaro in his conquest of Peru. What Spaniard was the first European to cross the Mississippi River in 1541?

This woman was the first Western dancer to perform without tights or shoes. Instead, she wore filmy, flowing tunics to complement the movements she based on Greek sculpture. Identify this modern dancer, who died when her scarf wrapped around a car's tire.

This Aesop fable teaches that, quote, "Gratitude is the sign of a noble soul." In it, one title character removes a thorn from the other character's paw, with the animal later refusing to eat his helper. What is this fable about an escaped slave and a large cat?
A green ribbon is 18 centimeters long. The yellow ribbon is 12 centimeters long. In centimeters, how long will the ribbons be when they are laid end to end?

In muscle cells, a special type of this organelle stores calcium ions. This organelle that is made of cisternae has one variant that is studded with ribosomes. Name this organelle that comes in smooth and rough varieties.
On September 18, 1861, this Kentucky city was seized by Confederate troops. What Warren County city became Kentucky's Confederate state capital?

Since 1997, a replica of this theater has stood near the River Thames [TEMZ]. The original, built in 1599 and rebuilt in 1614, staged the world premieres of Othello, Macbeth, and Hamlet. Identify this London theater that housed many of Shakespeare's plays.
The Latin root "spec" is found in words like "specimen," "spectator," and "inspect." What is its English meaning?
questions.a: (TO) SEE (Accept WATCH, LOOK AT, OBSERVE, OTHER EQUIVALENTS)

questions.q: This quadrilateral is a special type of parallelogram. Adjacent sides may or may not be equal in length. It has four right angles. What quadrilateral has opposite sides that are parallel and of equal length?

A plant placed far from a window may try to find ways to get back toward the light through bending and growing in that direction. What is this specific type of movement in a plant caused by the outside stimulus of light?
This 31st president of the United States was president when the Great Depression started. What president's name was used to describe the shanty towns that popped up during the depression?

Though traditionally made of wood, this art tool also comes in aluminum and steel varieties. They can be A-frame or H-frame and can be used outdoors or in an artist's studio. Identify this upright stand that supports a canvas.

In one sense, this word names the flattened space on either side of a person's forehead. It also refers to the most sacred Mormon buildings. Give this word for a Reform or Conservative Jewish synagogue.
The area of the rectangular kitchen floor is 72 square feet. One side of the floor is 9 feet. In feet, what is the length of the other side?

Different classes of invertebrates possess different characteristics. One class is typically characterized by having one pair of antennae, at least one pair of compound eyes, and usually two sets of wings, though there are always exceptions. What class of arthropods is always characterized as having three pairs of legs on its thorax and has members such as flies, bees, and ants?
This term means someone who runs for office. What is the name for a person who is nominated for election?

This landmark consists of pounded copper sheets shaped around an iron framework. Those copper sheets have turned green after years of exposure to weather. Frédéric Bartholdy [bar-TOLD-ee] sculpted what artwork that stands in New York Harbor?
How many commas does the following sentence need? The dog begged for table scraps while I was eating.
The Hammonds are moving and they rented a van with a floor of 14 square units. The height of the van is 2 units. What is the volume of the moving van in cubic units?

Scavenging at human garbage dumps is hypothesized by some scientists to have led to the domestication of this genus. Artificial selection within this genus produced breeds like spaniel and terrier. Name this genus that includes wolves and dogs whose name also describes their large, fanglike teeth.
This right ensures that no law enforcement agency can enter your home without a warrant. What does the Fourth Amendment bar the government from doing?
questions.a: UNREASONABLE SEARCH AND SEIZURE (ACCEPT SIMILAR RESPONSE)

questions.q: This artist sculpted Mary holding Jesus's body in her lap in his Pietà [pee-ay-TAH]. He depicted a biblical giant slayer in the marble statue David. Who was this Renaissance artist of the Sistine Chapel ceiling?
State the following sentence's predicate nominative: Becky is the school newspaper's photographer.

When Kelsey checked his media bill, he saw that he had sent 4 texts in January and 12 texts in February. In March he had sent 36 text messages. If Kelsey continues this geometric pattern of texting, how many texts will he send in April?
The kidneys work to remove waste and extra fluid from the body. What is the name of the branch of science that studies the physiology and disease of the kidneys?
The Dow Jones and NASDAG are types of these markets. What is the set of places where shares of companies are bought and sold?

This holy object of Northeast and Plains tribes was used for personal and communal rituals. Native Americans often used this long-stemmed item to cement peace treaties. Name this tobacco container that emits smoke to show communication between the human and spirit worlds.
What is the grammatical structure of the following sentence? Henry likes tea, but John prefers hot chocolate.
The cost of 8 bananas is 8B. B equals 50 cents. How much will the 8 bananas cost?
It involves technology as simple as electronic mail and as complex as virtual reality. What is the name given to the virtual "space" created by a web of computer systems?

This symbol of the United States was dedicated to women. It depicts a woman in work clothes with her muscular arm raised. What cultural icon honors the women who worked in the factories during World War Two?

This daughter of the Earth goddess and the creator god was exiled from Tahiti because of her temper. She moved from Kauai to the Big Island, where she still resides on Mount Kilauea [kil-uh-WAY-uh]. Who is this Hawaiian goddess of fire and volcanoes?
Spelling required. My uncle is a literature professor at a distinguished university. Spell the word in the previous sentence that names a high-ranking teacher.
What are the next two numbers in the following geometric sequence: 4, 8, 16, 32, and so on?
This scientist developed a storage device that could supply continuous current to an electrical circuit. Name this man who, in 1799, made the precursor to the modern battery.
Four letter answer please. This medium for communication became more important in the last ten years. What are these informational websites published on the Internet?

This novel opens with the title character eavesdropping on a twelve-step meeting in Hard Pan, California. That girl runs away because she believes her French guardian Brigitte doesn't want to adopt her. What is this Newbery-winning Susan Patron [puh-TRONE] novel?
This number is always the remainder when any number is divisible by another number. It is the remainder when 25 is divided by 5. What is also the remainder when 10 is divided by 2?

This musical element changes when the player encounters words like "crescendo" and "diminuendo." "Fortissimo" and "mezzo piano" are also words associated with it. What is the word for how loud or quiet a note is?
This special white rainbow appears during a full moon. What special rainbow can only be seen in the western hemisphere at Cumberland Falls?

Made up of protons, neutrons, and electrons, atoms are the smallest units of elements that maintain the properties of the element. Name the atomic structure that houses over 99 percent of the atom's mass.

This picture book's text is a poem meant to encourage African-Americans. It recalls the community's triumph over slavery and segregation and honors members of many occupations. What is this Caldecott-winning book written by Kwame [KWA-mee] Alexander and illustrated by Kadir [kuh-DEER] Nelson?
Thirteen hundredths of a shipment of flowers was damaged when the florist received the order. There were 100 roses in the latest shipment. How many roses were NOT damaged in shipping?

Songs of this type include "God Bless Our Homeland Ghana" and "Jamaica, Land We Love." "O Canada" and "God Save the Queen" are further examples. What is this two-word designation for the United States' "The Star-Spangled Banner"?
This frontiersman blazed the Wilderness Road through the Cumberland Gap. What early explorer settled in Kentucky with his family at a fort named for the family?

A baseball player runs the bases from home to 3rd base. While his total distance from home is 270 feet, there is another term to describe his final position. What three syllable term is the difference between his initial position and final position, not the total distance traveled?

This type of poem sometimes relies on the typeface and color of the font. The physical arrangement of letters and words matters as much as their sound and meaning. What is this style in which a poem is shaped like its subject?
Mrs. Brown is making an Afghan with 14 equal squares. She knits 1 square of the Afghan at noon and then 4 more squares after dinner. What fraction of the Afghan has she completed?
This instrument comes in upright and grand varieties. It has three pedals, as well as hammers that strike its strings. What is this 88-keyed instrument, whose name is Italian for "soft"?
Hawaii is located just south of this line of latitude. What is this line of latitude located at 23 degrees 27 minutes north of the equator?
All objects or materials are made of various particles that are in constant motion. What type of energy changes due to the motion and collisions among the particles within an object?
This novel's title refers to teenage Matty, a resident of Village. He sacrifices himself to heal The Forest and his fellow villagers. What is this third novel in Lois Lowry's Giver Quartet?
You need 3 cases of Gatorade for every 9 athletes. There are 18 athletes on the field. How many cases of Gatorade will you need?
This father of 20 children wrote Toccata and Fugue in D minor for the organ. He also composed cantatas for each of the Four Gospels. Identify this Baroque composer of The Goldberg Variations.
Residential and recreational are two types of this human use of the land. What two-word term represents the economic and cultural activities of a given place?

Pencil lead is not even lead at all! As a matter of fact, pencil "lead" is specialized sheets of carbon. What is the term for this carbon structure that sloughs off as you write to leave behind pencil marks?
This sort of internal rhyme appears in the sentence, "The crowd gave a loud, proud shout." Give the word for the repetition of vowel sounds.
Kim started his mall shopping spree with $40.00. He spent 50 percent of his money at the puzzle store. How much money does he have left?

This man wrote the operas La Traviata [tra-vee-AH-tuh] and Rigoletto [rig-oh-LET-oh]. He also composed a work about an Ethiopian princess in Egyptian captivity. Identify this Romantic Era composer of Aida [eye-EE-duh].

This Portuguese explorer discovered a South American strait named for him. He was killed in battle in the Philippines. What explorer is credited with being the first whose expedition sailed around the earth?
Often seen in the sky on bright, sunny days, these clouds appear puffy, like floating cotton. Give the name for this type of cloud that is a good indicator of fair weather.

The earliest references to this legendary British creature date from about 500 A.D. Sometimes described as a plesiosaur [PLEZ-ee-uh-sor], she supposedly lives in Great Britain's largest freshwater lake. Identify this Scottish cryptid nicknamed "Nessie."
You have a very long rope that is 1,000 meters long. How many kilometers long is the rope?
This lively swing dance evolved into the ballroom dance known as the jive. It relies on the rock step in a quick, quick, slow, slow pattern. What is this dance, whose name sounds like an insect?
This Spanish explorer settled Puerto Rico and founded its oldest settlement. He was the first European to reach Florida in 1513. What explorer searched for the Fountain of Youth?
These stars are similar to our own sun-- dense and hot. They are the remnants that are left behind when a star has exhausted its fuel supply. Name this type of star, the most likely to become a nova.
This nursery rhyme character sat on a footstool as she enjoyed cottage cheese. She ran away in fright when a spider joined her. Identify this character who sat on a tuffet.
These polygons are made of straight line segments. This type of polygon does NOT have all sides equal and all angles equal. What word meaning NOT regular describes these polygons?

Someone once claimed of this ballerina, quote, "She does not dance; she soars as though on wings." The Imperial Ballet's prima ballerina, she guest starred with the Ballets Russes [bal-EY ROOS] before founding her own touring company. Who was this soloist of The Dying Swan?
Enslaved people worked on these large farms in the South. What are these large farms that grew cotton as their main crop?

In this stage of mitosis the nucleolus disappears and the chromatin becomes visible. This phase leads to prometaphase, which in turn leads to metaphase, and it follows the second gap of interphase. Name this first stage of mitosis.
This arthropod's name contains the Latin root for "foot." It also uses a Latin prefix meaning "hundredth." Identify this creature that supposedly has one hundred legs.
A square scarf measures 16 inches on each side. In square inches, what is the area of the scarf?

This musical sets Romeo and Juliet in 20th-century New York City. The Montagues and Capulets become rival gangs, the Sharks and the Jets. Maria and Tony's forbidden love lies at the heart of what Leonard Bernstein and Stephen Sondheim musical?
President Roosevelt introduced this plan to help the American economy in 1933. This plan had three goals: relief, recovery, and reform. What was the name of this economic plan?

Many plants have properties that allow them to survive even under harsh conditions, particularly those that live in the desert. This type of plant has adaptations such as spikes and barbs to fend off predators and a thickened "skin" to conserve water. Common examples of these plants are the prickly pear and the saguaro. What are they called?
This word may refer to a person who hasn't reached legal adulthood. It can also allude to anything less important or smaller than something else. State this opposite of "major."

In order to win the math game, Leroy needs to roll a sum of seven. He uses a fair pair of six-sided dice. As a fraction in reduced form, what is the probability that he will roll a sum of seven and win?
This element of art deals with all the tones, shades, and tints in a work. Which element is concerned with a hue's lightness or darkness?
President Biden chose this person to be his running mate. What woman became the first female vice president?

Different phyla of invertebrates possess different characteristics. An animal in the Porifera phylum has no internal organs and usually remains attached to the same underwater surface as an adult. What is this animal that was once used for housecleaning purposes?
How many of the following sentence's words need to be capitalized? I hope the Miami Heat basketball team beats the Oklahoma City Thunder.
A spinner has 10 equal sectors. There are 5 green sectors, three yellow sectors, 1 red sector and 1 blue sector. What is the probability that on one spin, the spinner will land on blue?

This architectural period lasted from approximately the mid-12th century to the 16th century. Stained glass windows, pointed arches, gargoyles, and flying buttresses were its hallmarks. Name this style exemplified by the Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris.
Trial by jury is guaranteed by this Amendment. What amendment also guarantees the right to a speedy trial?

Hematopoietic [HEEmatohpohYETik] stem cells form within long structures made of this tissue, which can suffer rickets due to a lack of vitamin D or calcium. This tissue is made by osteoblasts and surrounds marrow. Name this tissue that makes up the skeletal system.
What is the direct object in the following sentence? This Saturday, we'll go fly a kite at the park.

Five jars are sitting on the table with a different number of shells in each jar. The number of shells in the first four jars is 22, 33, 44, and 55 respectively. If this pattern is continued, how many shells should be in the fifth jar?
This artist experimented with Expressionism in The Night Café. He created 11 paintings with sunflowers as the primary subjects. Identify the artist of The Starry Night.
If you buy a candy bar for fifty cents and sell it for a dollar, you have made this. What is the financial gain you made after you paid for the candy bar?

When you walk from a dimly lit room into the bright sunshine, your eyes may take a moment to adjust. This adjustment is due to actually muscles around the pupil of the eye dilating or contracting to change the amount of light that the eye absorbs. What is the name for the part of the eye that is better known for displaying a wide variety of colors?
Identify the following sentence's structure: Although she was scared, she gave the speech.
Mathematical expressions contain variables and operational symbols. What other part of a mathematical expression has a value that does NOT change?

For colonial militias, this instrument paired with the fife to relay the commander's orders to infantrymen. In West Africa, the djembe [JEM-bay] was one of these instruments used to communicate over distances. Native Americans sometimes played what percussion instrument in sweat lodges?
This park is one of our country's first national parks. It was dedicated in 1872. What park in the western U.S. is famous for the geyser, Old Faithful?

These scientists lead explorations to determine the age of fossils that are, perhaps, thousands of years old. Identify the scientists who study the past by searching, digging, or excavating the remains of ancient cities or dwellings?
Spelling required. An insect's body is divisible into the head, thorax, and abdomen. Spell the word in the preceding sentence that means "capable of being divided."

Henry is preparing a meal that calls for milk in each dish. If he needs a quarter cup for the first dish, a third cup for the second, and half a cup for the final dish, how much milk does he need altogether?

This 2021 Time magazine Athlete of the Year called her autobiography Courage to Soar: A Body in Motion, A Life in Balance. To date, she has won 25 World Championship medals and 7 Olympic medals. Identify this woman, history's most decorated gymnast.
This virus made news as it crossed borders. What was the virus that caused the pandemic of the last few years?

Nicknamed the Wizard of Menlo Park, this man invented the movie camera. He sometimes said of his most famous invention, "I didn't fail, I just found 10,000 ways that won't work." Name this man, the inventor of the light bulb.
This question requires multiple answers. What must the units digit be in order for a number to be divisible by 5?
This accidental resembles a lowercase B. It performs the opposite operation of a sharp. Which accidental means a musician should lower a note by one-half step?
The Federal Hill mansion at this site celebrated its 200th birthday in 2018. What site in Kentucky is named for Kentucky's state song?
Although an object's mass will remain the same on different planets, this quantity may change. What is this property, a measurement of the amount of gravitational force acting on an object?
How many hyphens does the following sentence need? The candidate won the election with sixty-six and two-thirds percent of the vote.
Juan finished a race with a time of 12.57 seconds. The only other runner finished with a time of 12.36 seconds. By how many seconds did Juan win the race?

This music genre combines African, Caribbean, and Spanish influences. Celia Cruz popularized this style, which shares its name with a Latin American dance. Identify this music, whose name is Spanish for "sauce."
This racetrack was founded in 1875 on land owned by Meriwether Lewis Clark. What racetrack began a tradition of horseracing called the "Home of the Kentucky Derby"?

In physics, speed is a measure of how fast or slow an object is moving. With no thought given to direction, speed, unlike another scientific quantity, is always positive. Which sister quantity in physical science takes into accound distance, time AND direction for an accurate calculation?

This novel's protagonist, Katie Takeshima, has a younger brother named Sammy and an older sister named Lynn. Katie's life changes when Lynn dies from lymphoma, a blood cancer. Give the Japanese title of this Newbery winner by Cynthia Kadohata [KA-doh-HA-tuh].
The park has a track with 7 lanes. The coach uses three-sevenths of the track for sprinting practice. Using simple fractions, how much of the track is NOT used?

At one corner of this instrument, its metal rods don't touch, allowing the instrument to vibrate. It hangs from a string or a small piece of leather as the player hits it with a beater. Identify this small percussion instrument that shares its name with a geometric shape.
This imaginary line is located in the Pacific Ocean. It defines the boundary between one day and the next. What zigzagged line marks the eastern and western hemisphere divide?

Because energy can neither be created nor destroyed, it must undergo constant changes. For example, a roller coaster moving downhill will begin with high potential energy that quickly changes to kinetic energy. What is the term for these changes in energy from one form to another?

In this nearly wordless picture book, a young girl in a red coat rescues a wild animal pup. She returns that pup to its pack, who howl to let the lost girl's parents know where to find her. Identify this Caldecott winner by Matthew Cordell.
The Mexican restaurant served 8 tacos in 10 minutes. At this rate how many tacos will the restaurant serve in one-half hour?

This Romantic composer nicknamed two of his symphonies Pastoral and Eroica [uh-ROH-ick-uh]. He may have dedicated his piano piece Für Elise to a woman named Terese. Name this composer of Moonlight Sonata.
This question requires two answers. What two statistics about a population are shown in a population pyramid?
At times, volcanic eruptions are so violent that they damage the structure of the volcano itself. Name the type of crater formed when a volcano produces so much lava that it collapses in on itself.

This poet used similar titles for "Early Moon" and "Child Moon." The speaker emphasizes the strength and fragility of words in his poem "Little Girl, Be Careful What You Say." Name this Illinois poet of "Fog."
Lawrence's free throw percentage is 60 percent. He shot 30 free throws during practice. How many free throws did he make?

Virtuosos in this dance form included Bill "Bojangles" Robinson, Gregory Hines, and Savion [SAY-vee-ahn] Glover. West African step dances and British Isles clogging and jigs combined to create this percussive form. What is this dance in which metal plates on shoes' soles create loud sounds?
This Frenchman made three expeditions to the New World. He laid French claims to North America and named Canada. What mariner was the first European to navigate the St. Lawrence River?

In the day time, these clouds appear brighter than any other cloud in the sky. Appearing like streamers or tufts of hair, you can watch their movement to see which way approaching weather is moving. What is the name for these short, detached, hair-like clouds found at high altitudes?

This novel's protagonist is Polly O'Keefe, teenage daughter of Meg and Calvin. While visiting her grandparents in Connecticut, she stumbles on an imminent war between two Tribes of the Lake. What is this final novel in Madeleine L'Engle's Time Quintet?
The base of a birdhouse is 12 inches long. The height of the birdhouse is 8 inches tall. How many feet long is the base of the birdhouse?

Be specific. From the 1400s to the 1600s, some Italians believed this animal's bite caused an overwhelming urge to dance. The resulting quick, whirling dance was called the tarantella [tair-un-TELL-uh]. That dance was named for what kind of spider?
He was a political and religious leader in the 1600s. He believed that there should be a separation of church and state in colonial America. What man founded Rhode Island?

Neutron stars are stars that have condensed as they have run out of fuel. As the core collapses, protons and electrons are crushed together, creating a neutron star that spins. What is the name for this special type of spinning neutron star that emits bursts of radiation?

This type of sound repetition is found in the sentence, "Ike likes his new bike." Unlike true alliteration, it doesn't have to happen with the first letters of nearby words. Identify this repetition of consonant sounds.
This regular polygon has seven angles that measure 128.571 degrees. It has one more side than a hexagon. What is a regular polygon with seven sides?

Like her sister Marjorie, this woman studied dance with Bronislava Nijinska [broh-nee-SLAH-vuh nee-ZHIN-skuh]. She worked with Chicago's Lyric Opera Ballet and the Chicago City Ballet after retiring from performance. Name this wife of George Balanchine [BAL-un-sheen], star of the New York City Ballet, and member of the Osage tribe.
In 1793 Eli Whitney invented this machine. What invention removed the seeds and twigs from the cotton plants?
Somatic cells of humans have 44 of these. Give the name for these non-sex chromosomes, the entire complement of genetic code except for X and Y.

Different tall tales characterize this man as an oilfield worker, a buffalo hunter, and a railroad man. Most stories make him a cowboy who invented the lasso and the branding iron. Name this owner of the horse Widow-Maker and husband of Slue-Foot Sue.

For his math assignment, Julio had to draw a circle with a diameter of 3 inches. Then he had to determine the circumference of the circle. What is the circumference of the circle in terms of pi and in inches?
On a small scale, this word means removing a prop or set piece from a stage. What word also names the process of dismantling a set and storing costumes and props to make room for another production?
He was the commander of PT-109 when it was hit by a Japanese destroyer. He wrote Profiles in Courage. What president was assassinated in Dallas on November 22, 1963?
Phyla in this group include ginkgos and conifers. Bearing a name which translates to “naked seed," name this group of plants that lack an enclosed chamber for its seeds, as opposed to angiosperms.

Among this fairy tale's characters are a grandfather, Sasha the bird, Ivan the cat, and Sonya the duck. Soviet composer Sergei Prokofiev [pro-KAH-fee-ev] set it to music in 1936. Give the name of this story about a young boy who saves his human and animal friends from a large predator.
You roll a fair 11-sided die numbered 1 to 11. As a fraction in reduced form, what is the probability of rolling a 10?

Traditionally, this art form doesn't allow artists to cut their materials. Instead, they create simple or elaborate creases to make flowers, animals, or inanimate objects like boxes. Give the Japanese word for the art of paper folding.
This chamber of Congress has 435 members. Which lower chamber of Congress's membership is based on state populations?

The blue-ringed type of these animals is poisonous to humans. They do not have a skeleton, but do have a beak near their mouth. These animals are quite intelligent and can shoot ink in self-defense. Name these mollusks that live up to their name by having eight arms.
This Latin root is sometimes found after "e-," "dis-," or "bank." What is this root meaning "break" or "burst"?
Mr. Garcia's class was conducting experiments with coin flips. They flipped a coin 25 times and it landed on heads 14 times. What is the experimental probability of the coin landing on heads?
This Doric temple once housed a large statue of the goddess Athena. A replica, complete with Athena statue, stands in Nashville. The ruins of what temple stand on the Acropolis in Athens?
Besides freedom of speech, this amendment also makes worship a right of U.S. citizens. What amendment guarantees freedom of religion?

Mobbing is one strategy for opposing these organisms, whose keystone examples include the sea otter in kelp forests. Herbivores like deer can be considered this type of organism in relation to plants, while typical “apex” ones include the polar bear, lion, and great white shark. Name these organisms that hunt for prey.

The first part of this compound word is an antonym of "give." The second part is an antonym of "in." What is this word for food prepared in a store or restaurant that's meant to be eaten somewhere else?
Sam had 20 vacation days and he took 18 of them. Then he received 3 more days as a bonus. How many vacation days does he have now?
This man made the subjects of his painting Three Musicians resemble collages. He painted The Old Guitarist in 1904 during his Blue Period. Give the name of this co-founder of Cubism.
These two syllable places have been a part of civilization for centuries. What is a way for buyers and sellers to come together to exchange goods and services?

Certain disorders can cause pain and inflammation in the body. This disorder comes in varieties such as osteo, rheumatoid, and juvenile. What is the term for the chronic conditions that cause pain and swelling, primarily in the joints?
Identify the following sentence's indirect object: For the book fair, Mom gave Oscar $10.
Kelly replaced the variable with a 6 to solve the mathematical expression. What process did she use to solve the expression?

In early America, this folk art came in broderie perse [BRO-duh-ree PAIRCE], medallion style, and whole-cloth varieties. When fabric prices increased, the patchwork style predominated. Identify this bed covering made of two stitched fabric layers with a soft substance in between.
This small federally owned island is located in New York and is appropriately named. On what island, which is very near Ellis Island, is the Statue of Liberty located?

Two word answer, please. Without one, a computer system would be very difficul to use. These programs contain the specialized set of instructions that the computer will follow in order to complete basic tasks. What are these special programs, examples of which are O. S. ten and Windows?
What is the following sentence's grammatical structure? When the fireworks started, the dog ran away, but he later came home.
This figure has two equal angles opposite two equal sides. The third angle is not equal to the other two. What kind of triangle is it?

One member of this sports dynasty is a senior at Isidore Newman School in New Orleans. His uncles won Super Bowls for the New York Giants, Indianapolis Colts, and Denver Broncos. Give the last name of quarterbacks Arch, Peyton, and Eli.
Elon Musk introduced this humanoid robot in 2022. It could lift its leg and grip its hand. What robot's name means one of the best?

In critiquing an opposing theory, he criticized the separate treatment of each planet, as had been done by Ptolemy (TAHL-eh-mee). Name the Polish astronomer who first proposed the theory of heliocentrism.
Spelling required. Defeating an ignorant person in an argument is impossible. Spell the word from the previous sentence that means "uninformed."
Composers often think of this musical element first and add harmony to it later. It is a group of pitches played one after another. Give the official name for a song's tune.

Ten-year-old Annemarie Johansen narrates this novel set in World War Two-era Copenhagen. Annemarie's family helps Ellen Rosen's family escape to Sweden so they won't be sent to a Nazi concentration camp. What is this first Newbery-winning novel by Lois Lowry?
This number is an identity element for real numbers. The product will not change when a real number is multiplied by this number. What is the identity element for multiplication?
This natural phenomena can be defined as a disturbance of air. Give the name for this phenomena that is measured in decibels and perceived by the human ear.
This President was born in Kentucky and was nicknamed the "rail splitter." He was a Whig who later became a Republican. What "honest" man became the 16th President of the United States?

Country singer Jimmie Rodgers popularized this singing technique in the U.S. It requires fast switching between the low chest and high falsetto voice. Give the name of this technique heard in the Swiss Alps.

This Caldecott winner is a companion book to works about bears and turtles. In this middle book of the trilogy, a small fish steals an object from a much larger fish. Give the title of this Jon Klassen [KLAH-sin] book.
Consider the number 27 and 803 thousandths. (27.803) Which number is in the ones place?

When you are in a car stopped at an intersection, you have a velocity of zero. Once the light changes to green, your driver will step on the gas pedal, increasing in speed until you reach the desired cruise control setting. What is the term for this increase of speed, the change in velocity over a given amount of time?
The salt springs here attracted prehistoric animals, Native Americans, and pioneers. What state park is known as the site of the last Revolutionary War Battle in Kentucky?

This brass instrument practically ties the trumpet for the title of loudest orchestral instrument. Before about 1700, it was called the sackbut. Give the name of this instrument, which changes notes by way of a telescoping slide.
This kind of lyric poem arose in Italian Renaissance courts. In England, Shakespeare wrote 154 examples in a slightly different format. Identify this 14-line poem.

Helen and Lisa are selling balloons for the fall carnival. In the first hour, Hannah sold 3 balloons and Lisa sold 5 balloons. If they both keep selling at the same rate, how many balloons will they sell in 5 hours?
During photosynthesis, a plant accepts radiant energy in order to convert it to another, more useful type. What type of energy do plants produce when they make use of photosynthesis to create sugar?
This Native American tribe formed the strongest connection to Kentucky. Its lands covered most of the state. What Native American tribe's most famous leader was Tecumseh?
This composer called for cannons in his 1812 Overture. Odette and Siegfried are two of the main characters in his ballet Swan Lake. Give the name of this composer of The Nutcracker.

This novel's supporting characters include folk historian James K. Lewis and independent Lurhetta Outlaw. The title boy sits atop a pole as he ponders ways to save his family's ancestral home, Sarah's Mountain. Identify this Newbery-winning novel by Virginia Hamilton.
There were three-fifths of Granny's Great Cherry Pie left after lunch. Granddad ate one-fifth of the pie for an afternoon snack. How much of the pie was left?

Often times our geologic landscape is changed by violent events like earthquakes. In 1964, an Alaskan earthquake of massive scale was followed by many smaller earthquakes shortly thereafter. What is the term for these smaller earthquakes that follow a large earthquake and sometimes go on for many days or weeks?
Oceania is a region that contains this continent plus many islands in the Pacific Ocean. What continent "down under" is famous for its kangaroos and koalas?

When this dance form began in the 1500s, the French king and royal court members adapted steps from social dances. After Louis the Fourteenth founded the Royal Academy of Dance, only professionals performed it. The plié [plee-AY], jeté [zhuh-TAY], and pirouette [peer-uh-WET] are basic movements in what dance discipline?
This figure of speech appears in the sentence, "The stars are dancing a jig in the sky." Name this device that gives human qualities to animals, objects, or ideas.
The school fall festival had 11 balloon booths and 5 fishing booths. Three fishing booths close. What is the ratio of the remaining balloon booths to fishing booths?

This weather phenomenon is one of the many sources of erosion on Earth. The intensity of this phenomenon is measured on the Beaufort scale. Typically caused when warm and cold fronts meet, what is the name for this phenomenon, examples of which are breezes and gales?
This is one of the specialized fields of human geography. What field of geography studies the spaces and places dedicated to young people?

Before the waltz, this dance in 3/4 time was popular in European courts. Couples performed elegant floor patterns as they displayed their fancy outfits. Identify this dance, whose name comes from the French for "small."

This fable illustrates cognitive dissonance--the condition of holding two conflicting ideas in your mind. In it, the title animal repeatedly tries and fails to reach a bunch of fruit hanging high on a vine. Identify this Aesop fable, which ends with the animal concluding that the fruit must be sour.
Gerald had 90 baseball cards. He gave his brother 70 percent of his cards. How many cards did he give his brother?

While many scientists believe that this planet once had water on its surface, extensive searches have found only dry basins. Name this planet, the fourth from the sun, which shares its name with the Roman god of war.
This prehistoric refuse heap contains shells and human artifacts. They usually date from the late Mesolithic period. What are these mounds also called Kitchen middens?

In 1681, this man danced with King Louis the Fourteenth in The Triumph of Love. As director of the Royal Academy of Dance, he devised the five basic ballet positions. Identify this first choreographer of the Paris Opéra.

Two years after this man delivered his 1964 speech "A Time for Choosing," he was elected Governor of California. As U.S. president, he addressed the nation after the Challenger explosion in January 1986. Name this leader who, in 1987, urged the Soviet Union's Mikhail Gorbachev to, quote, "tear down this wall."
A horse is 17 hands tall. Each hand equals 4 inches. How many inches tall is the horse?
Leukocytes, or white blood cells, use this process to protect the body from bacterial infections. Name this process also carried out when protists use their cell membranes to ingest nutrients.
This assembly was established to pass laws for the Jamestown Colony in Virginia. What was this first English representational government in the North American colonies?

Other names for this stage include platform and open stage. A modeling catwalk is one example of this earliest type of Western staging. In what seating arrangement is the audience on three sides of the stage?
At one time, this Latin prefix came before "sonics" in the name of a Seattle NBA team. You might also find it before "natural," "market," and "man." Identify this prefix meaning "above" or "beyond."
This polygon has interior angles measuring close to 180 degrees. It has 10 to the 100th number of sides. What polygon's name sounds like a search engine?

The stroma within this organelle is the location of the Calvin cycle, which is also known as the dark reactions, and these organelles are often contrasted with mitochondria because both convert energy. Name these organelles evolved from cyanobacteria that conduct photosynthesis and are green.
This President was impeached in 1998. He is the husband of the woman who lost the 2016 presidential election. Who was the 42nd President of the United States?
This color term is the opposite of tint. What does an artist create when she adds black to a hue in order to darken it?
The first part of this compound word is a caffeinated drink popular in England. The second part is a utensil. Identify this cooking unit of measure equal to 1/3 of a tablespoon.
To cover the baseball field, the park needs a tarp that measures 90 feet on each side. In square feet, what is the area of the tarp that the park will need?

Insects molt because they outgrow this structure, which is usually made of chitin. This protective structure is also present in crustaceans and shelled mollusks such as snails and clams. Name this structure that helps support an animal from the outside, unlike an endoskeleton.
This branch of the U.S. government has two houses. What branch of government makes laws?
Jan [YAHN] Vermeer's View of Delft is one of these paintings. Georgia O'Keeffe explored the genre in Shelton with Sunspots and Radiator Building at Night. Give the word for an urban landscape.
Which words should be capitalized in the following sentence? My mom asked, "Will you please wash the dishes?"

You have a bag that contains two red balls, four green balls, and one orange ball. You close your eyes and reach into the bag. As a fraction in reduced form, what is the probability that you will pull out an orange ball?

The competitive exclusion principle prevents two of these groups from occupying the same “niche.” A classification more specific than genus is what title subject of a book by Darwin about their Origin?
This is one of the main responsibilities of a citizen. What should citizens do to select their leaders?

This 1872 painting shows the port of Le Havre [luh AHV-ruh], France. Green boats float in blue-green water as a bright orange circle hangs in the background. What is this Claude Monet painting that gave an art movement its name?
Like the exclamatory sentence, this part of speech often expresses strong emotion. Identify this part of speech, examples of which are "wow" and "oh."
Howard has 3 green shirts and 7 blue ties and 2 yellow hats. How many possible outfits of shirts, ties, and hats can he make?

DNA replication is a continuous cycle in the cells of living things. During this process, however, environmental factors or random mistakes can occur that change the replication. What is the term for a change in a gene that can be inherited by future generations.
Pineapples from Hawaii are examples of these goods. What are goods or services sold to another country?

The Cherokee used this dance in part to remove evil spirits from the Earth. Dancers wear feathers and turquoise to symbolize the weather phenomena they hope to cause. Give the name of this dance meant to induce precipitation.
What kind of dependent clause is part of the following sentence? We adopted the two dogs because they are a bonded pair.
When school started there were 20 students in the fourth grade. Eight more students enrolled on the second day, but one student moved on the third day. How many students are in the class now?

The International Space Station at any given time has a finite amount of supplies on board and must have other ships to bring necessary supplies or transport astronauts home. Joining two spacecraft together is no easy task, but happens by way of ports on the station and with the help of the robotic arm that is there. What is the term for joining two crafts in space which shares its name with the term for parking a boat?
This monument was designed by Thomas Casey. It is located in the center of Washington, D.C. What is this large obelisk that memorializes our country's first President?

In June 2022, this star donated $1 million to Vanderbilt University for pediatric infectious disease research. She donated to Middle Tennessee flood relief and to victims of the 2016 fires in her native Sevier County. Who is this Imagination Library founder and singer-songwriter of "9 to 5" and "Jolene"?
Spelling required. The company expects to quadruple its profits next quarter. Spell the word in the previous sentence meaning "multiply by four."
Solve the mathematical expression by substituting 3 for the variable n. What is the value of 12n plus 2?

Increased efficiency comes from multi-junction parts, and this is harnessed by crystal layers of doped semiconductors in an electric field under a cover plate. Several recent projects have combined this power source with thermoelectric. Name this power source utilizing photovoltaic cells often used by space stations because they are not impacted by cloud cover.
She was an associate justice of the Supreme Court. She wrote dissents to cases that did not improve women's rights. What feminist icon is known for her distinctive collar?

Characters in this novel's flashbacks include Kissin' Kate Barlow, Madame Zeroni, and Elya Yelnats. Stanley befriends Zero as the boys solve the mystery of Camp Green Lake. Name this Newbery Medal-winning novel by Louis Sachar [SACK-er].
If you multiply four-fifths by this multiplier, the product will be four-fifteenths. What is this fractional multiplier?

This musical idea's symbol is the crosshairs--an oval with a cross through it. It can range from a few measures to an entire section of the piece. Give the word for a passage that ends a musical movement or composition.

The Wilderness Road passed through this site in Danville. The home of this site was chosen to be Kentucky's first seat of government. What place in Kentucky has a bronze statue of the state seal surrounded by plaques dedicated to all of Kentucky's governors?

In science, mixtures can have either the same or different composition throughout. For example, If you fill a bucket with sand at the beach which contains small shells it will not be the same throughout. What type of mixture is this, one in which the individual substances are not evenly mixed?

This picture book's title character spends her night running down the sidewalk, through the garden, past the field, and by the pond. She mistakenly believes the sky holds a large bowl of milk. Name this Caldecott winner by Kevin Henkes [HANK-us].
You have a die with the numbers 1 through 6. What is the probability of rolling a 7 with this die?

Music historians distinguish this type of music from art--that is, classical--music. Its performers are often amateurs who have learned the music orally instead of seeing it written down. Identify a country's or culture's traditional music handed down among ordinary people.
This Kentuckian was known for his civil rights activism. He was born in Louisville and was a professional boxer. What boxer "stung like a bee" as he won gold at the 1960 Olympic Games in Rome?
A bicycle travels 240 meters in 6 minutes. In meters per minute, at what average speed is the bicycle traveling?

This poet titled one of his elegies for Abraham Lincoln "When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom'd." He also elegized the president in "O Captain! My Captain!" Who was this 19th-century poet of "Song of Myself," part of his Leaves of Grass?
When this additive inverse is added to negative 5, the sum will equal zero. What is the additive inverse of negative 5?
This word can name a four-stringed, low-pitched electric guitar. It also refers to the largest and deepest-sounding drum. Give this word for the lowest male singing voice and for a type of clef.
This 20,310 feet tall mountain was formerly named Mt. McKinley. What is this tallest mountain peak in North America?

Sometimes materials hold electrons more loosely than other materials. When this happens, electrons can easily move from one object to another, producing a charge. What is this phenomenon that you often see in the winter when your hair stands on end after you put on a sweater?

At this novel's conclusion, Mr. Pluto and his son Mayhew live peacefully with the protagonist's family. That family, the Smalls, help preserve the treasures found in their new residence, which was once a stop on the Underground Railroad. Name this Virginia Hamilton novel.
A certain decimal number has three places to the right of the decimal point. Identify the place value of the third digit to the right of the decimal.

Two of this composer's operas were Don Giovanni and Così fan tutte [kaw-ZEE fawn TOO-tay]. He also wrote The Marriage of Figaro and the Jupiter Symphony. Which Classical composer's final work was the unfinished Requiem?
The geography of these areas is focused on villages, towns, and cities. Louisville and New York City are examples of these areas. What is a densely populated area like a city?

Found in bogs and swamps, this organic material is typically made up of vegetable matter. As the matter builds up, over time it becomes carbonized, breaking down. What is the term for this carbonized vegetable matter from which all coal deposits originate?
Examples of this figure of speech include, "The snow is a white blanket," and, "You are the apple of my eye." What is this comparison between two unlike things without using the words "like" or "as"?
The numbers 12 and 18 have four common factors. What is the greatest common factor of 12 and 18?
This dance is called noho if the performer is sitting and luna if he is standing. Its first dance was supposedly for the fire goddess Pele. Give the name of this storytelling dance native to Hawaii.
These Portuguese plantations were worked by enslaved people. What plantations, set up in the Americas, grew and harvested sugarcane?

As part of the water cycle, water evaporates from the ground and is trapped in the atmosphere before it reaches higher altitudes, cools, and condenses. The water vapor in the air, however, still has an effect on plant and animal life, often leaving us humans to feel "muggy". Give the term for the amount of water vapor in the air, measured with a hygrometer.

This tall tale man was a real folk hero whose death in 1900 led to a ballad. Born in Kentucky, he saved the fireman and all the passengers on a speeding train near Vaughan, Mississippi. Give the name of this locomotive engineer.
There are fifteen barrels in the shed. Seven of the barrels are empty. What is the ratio of filled barrels to empty barrels?

This dancer's professional debut was in the Denishawn ballet Xochitl [so-CHEET-ul]. Her work throughout the 20th century earned her the nickname "mother of modern dance." Give the name of this choreographer of Appalachian Spring.
Month and day please. On what day does the United States celebrate its independence from England?

This two-word term is used to designate one result of a supernova. It is defined as a relatively small but extremely dense body from whose gravitational pull nothing can escape. What is the name of this heavenly body?

In some versions of this fairy tale, the title character is called Henny Penny. She encounters a rooster, a duck, a goose, and a turkey on her way to visit the king. Foxy Loxy spells doom for the animals in what fairy tale, whose protagonist fears the sky is falling?
One inch equals 2.54 centimeters. How many inches are equal to 5.08 centimeters?

From 1925 to '29, this man was the ballet master for the Ballets Russes [bal-EY ROOS]. After moving to the U.S., he partnered with Lincoln Kirstein to establish a ballet company and a dance school. Name this co-founder of the School of American Ballet and the New York City Ballet.

The final battle of this war was fought after the peace treaty was signed. It was called "Mr. Madison's War." What war between Great Britain and the United States ended with the signing of the Treaty of Ghent?

They are typically protein molecules that bind to their favored location by way of an area known as an active site. Although pepsin was possibly the first one to be discovered, they typically end in "ase". Give the name for these biological molecules that speed up cellular reactions.
This Greek prefix means "many" or "much." Give this prefix that can appear before "gon" or "theism."
Kelly wants to measure the bathmat in inches. The box says it is 1 yard long. How many inches long is the bathmat?

Among this musical's characters are Jack Kelly, Katherine Plumber, and Joseph Pulitzer. Adapted from a 1992 Disney movie, it features the songs "Seize the Day," "Santa Fe," and "Carrying the Banner." Identify this musical based on an 1899 paperboy strike in New York City.
During this time, the United States tried to recover from the Civil War. What was the period immediately following the Civil War called?
Tendrils and spines are modified types of these structures that usually consist of a petiole and blade. Name these flat, green plant structures, the major site of photosynthesis.

One member of this homophone pair is an iron-carbon alloy metal that can be stainless. The other member names something baseball players can do to a base. Give the shared pronunciation of these words, one of which is a synonym of "rob."
This polygon can be found in nature. A honeycomb is made up of these polygons. What polygon has six sides?

The aerial type of this art technique relies on color and clarity to depict distance. The linear type can be one-, two-, or three-point. Give the word for the depiction of three dimensions in two-dimensional paintings and drawings.
The Supreme Court is the highest court in the land and represents this branch of the government. This branch interprets the meaning of laws. What branch decides if laws are constitutional?

This body part is “compound” in most insects. The retina, located here, is an area of this body part that processes light signals and sends them to the brain through the optic nerve. Name this body part that helps invertebrates see.
This punctuation shows a closer relationship between independent clauses than a period does. It can correct a comma splice. Identify this punctuation that looks like a dot placed above a comma.
The cover of a notebook is 8 inches tall and 10 inches wide. What is the area of the notebook's cover in square inches?

This ancient Greek architectural order featured slender, fluted columns with capitals that resembled acanthus [uh-KAN-thus] leaves. It was the latest to develop and the most ornate of the three orders. Name this counterpart of the Doric and Ionic orders.
This responsibility of citizenship is important in law. What duty should you complete if you are called?

Parts of this structure fuse to form the human sacrum. A sideways curve of this structure is called scoliosis, and CSF is extracted by a “tap” of this body part. Thoracic, cervical, and lumbar segments make up what structure that invertebrates do not possess?
Words in this part of speech are either correlative [kuh-REL-uh-tiv], subordinating, or coordinating. What are these words that connect words, phrases, and clauses?
This question requires a fraction in reduced form. You have two fair six-sided dice. What is the probability of rolling a sum of 12 with the pair of dice?

This artist joined the Impressionists at the request of her friend Edgar Degas [day-GAH]. Her portraits included Little Girl in a Blue Armchair and The Child's Bath. Name this painter, whose favorite subjects were women and children.
People use these two things to meet their needs and wants. What are these backbones of a traditional economy?
This area of the brain controls the body's movements. It is also the center of thought, feelings, and memory. Identify this largest part of the brain.
What is the following sentence's adjective clause? There is the lemur that we are going to feed.
questions.a: THAT WE ARE GOING TO FEED

questions.q: Determine the number of terms in the following mathematical expression. How many terms are included in 4 plus 6 minus 3?

In colonial America, these objects sometimes had carved nuts, pinched apples, or pieces of china for heads. Some were made of corncobs, while others were fashioned from rags and cloth scraps. What were these toys meant to resemble boys, girls, men, or women?
Three word answer please. This symbol of America is found on the one dollar bill. What symbol shows an eye enclosed in a triangle and surrounded by rays of light?

In order to precisely conduct an experiment using reagents, volumes must be measured as accurately as possible. Give the name for the piece of lab equipment that is a narrow glass tube used to measure and deliver small volumes of liquids.
Spelling required. A column of smoke rose from the building's chimney. Spell the word from the preceding sentence that means "something resembling a supporting pillar."
This math term is defined as a comparison between two expressions that are equal. What mathematical comparison contains an equal sign?

This singer-songwriter collaborated with her brother Finneas O'Connell on the 2017 EP Don't Smile at Me. Her first full-length album, When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?, made her history's youngest album of the year Grammy winner. Name this singer of "Everything I Wanted" and "Bad Guy."
His wife was the Secretary of Transportation during President Trump's administration. He is now the Senate minority leader. What Kentucky Senator was the Senate Majority leader until 2021?

A co-founder of INTEL initially observed this while preparing for a speech. It accurately predicted the advancement of computer technology from the mid-sixties to present day. Name this law that states that the capacity of a silicon microchip will double every 18 months.

This math property sounds like a word meaning to travel. This property is true for addition and multiplication, but not for subtraction and division. What property of addition is shown by the equation 3 plus 10 equals 10 plus 3?

Along with the string quartet, Haydn [HI-den] likely developed the form for this instrumental work. Usually divided into 3 or 4 movements, it is written for an orchestra. What is this format of Tchaikovsky's [chigh-KAWF-skeez] Pathétique [pah-tay-TEEK], Mozart's Jupiter, and Schubert's Unfinished?
This dam produces electricity for local communities. It is located on a river between Mercer and Garrard counties. What dam was built to help reduce flooding on the Kentucky River?

Carbon is a black solid while oxygen is a gas that enables fuels to burn. When the two elements are reacted, a completely new substance with new chemical properties is formed. What is the name for this type of substance made up of two or more elements that are chemically bonded together?

This Newbery Medal-winning novel was inspired by Madeleine L'Engle's A Wrinkle in Time. In it, Miranda Sinclair learns that the Laughing Man has time traveled to save Sal's life. Give the title of this Rebecca Stead book.
Determine the value of the six in the following whole number. What is the value of 6 in three thousand, four hundred sixty-five (3,465)?

This sacred music style is also called plainsong. It uses an unmeasured rhythm and a single melodic line with no harmony. Name this style dating from the medieval Catholic Church under Pope Gregory's reign.
A historical marker in Johnson County recognizes this physician's first expedition into Kentucky. What explorer named Cumberland Gap and the Cumberland River after the Duke of Cumberland?
Helping mom one day, Alex decided to push the coffee table to the other side of the room. In order to make the table move, what physical quantity did Alex have to apply to it so it would slide?

This book explores how the author-illustrator loves two places: Japan and California. It charts his ancestor's immigration to the U.S. and his return to Asia with his family. What is this Caldecott winner by Allen Say?

Three students attend karate practice every 3 days, every 4 days, and every 2 days, respectively. If they start on the same day, what is the first day all three karate students will attend practice on the same day again?

In a drum kit, the hi-hats are paired examples of this percussion instrument. They are metal discs made of copper, bronze, or another alloy. Name these instruments that the player can hit together to make a crashing sound.
This question requires multiple answers. What are the four cardinal directions located on the compass rose?

A television is an example of a special pathway of electrons. In a television, electrons continue moving as long as the device is powered on as the electric current flows in a special closed path to form a source of energy. What is the name for a complete path that a current travels?

This lyric poetic form's name comes from the Greek for "to sing." While they're no longer meant to be sung, they still express heightened emotion as they praise a person, animal, or thing. What type of poem did John Keats write "on a Grecian Urn"?
There are three triangles, five squares, and four circles scattered on the play table. One-third of the shapes are yellow. How many shapes are yellow?

This composer collaborated with his lyricist brother on songs like "Swanee" and "I Got Rhythm." His time studying in the French capital inspired his composition An American in Paris. Who wrote Rhapsody in Blue?

At least nine Southern states are considered part of this belt. Sometimes Kentucky, parts of Texas, and even Utah are included in it. What region of the U.S. is known for its high number of Christian churches?

Typically appearing as a crystal, this group of minerals is often found throughout other rocks. SIlica based, it is shiny when polished, and comes in a variety of colors. Name this rock class that is the most abundant mineral and has varieties such as amethyst, rose, and smoky.

This author created the characters Cedric Errol and Sara Crewe. She also imagined Dickon Sowerby, Colin Craven, and Mary Lennox. Who wrote Little Lord Fauntleroy, A Little Princess, and The Secret Garden?
Three packages of copy paper cost $18.00. Lisa needs only two packages of paper. At this rate how much will the two packages cost?
This dance accessory may be a ghillie [GIL-ee], pointe type, or clog. The ones used in tap dance have metal plates attached to their soles. Identify this specialized foot covering.
Cortez and Pizzaro are examples of these warriors. They were leaders of the Spanish explorers in Mexico and Peru. What name was given to these men who led the conquest of the Mayans and Aztecs?

Unlike in the troposphere, in this atmospheric layer, temperature rises as you increase in altitude. Ozone in this layer absorbs sunlight and heats this area very effectively. Name this layer of Earth's atmosphere that is heated by ozone and whose lowest boundary is the tropopause.

An example of this figure of speech is, "That dog is as black as coal." One also appears in the sentence, "We go together like ketchup and mustard." Give the word for a comparison between two things using "like" or "as."
Mrs. Jayne said add 273.15 degrees to the Celsius degrees to find the Kelvin temperature. Determine the Kelvin temperature if the Celsius temperature is 30 degrees.

This charter member of the American Ballet Theatre choreographed Fall River Legend and Three Virgins and a Devil for that company. She also choreographed musicals like Carousel, Brigadoon, and Paint Your Wagon. Name the choreographer of the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical Oklahoma!
Five of the original thirteen colonies are classified as these colonies which take the description from a cardinal direction. What group of colonies include South Carolina and Georgia?
Scientists believe that our sun is a middle aged star of the yellow dwarf variety. As it ages and dies, however, what type of star will the sun turn into, though not for another 5 billion years?

Ancient Egyptians associated this mythical bird with the sun's worship. Every 500 years, it supposedly builds a funeral pyre, burns itself, and rises from the ashes to begin a new life. What is this bird that shares its name with Arizona's capital?
A bag of grapes weighs 32 ounces. How many pounds does the bag of grapes weigh?

In 1905, this man choreographed Anna Pavlova's [PAH-vluh-vuhz] solo The Dying Swan. For five years, he was the chief choreographer of the Ballets Russes [bal-EY ROOS] in Paris. Who choreographed the ballets Petrushka [puh-TROOSH-kuh] and The Firebird?
This name for the Southern states was popularized by a song composed by Daniel Emmett. What name was used to refer to the Confederate States of America?

This part of a cell may have been developed by cells absorbing bacteria and is surrounded by a double membrane. This part of a cell has a key role in processing nutrients taken in by the cell and converting them to energy. Name this “powerhouse” of the cell.

In this nursery rhyme, the speaker refuses to wake the title lad. While that child is fast asleep under a haystack, the sheep has moved to the meadow and the cow has wandered into the corn. What is this rhyme that urges the child, quote, "come blow your horn"?
These angles are used to name some triangles. These angles measure less than 180 degrees and greater than 90 degrees. What type of angle is an angle that measures 116 degrees?

This kind of stage takes its name from part of an ancient Greek theater. The audience sits directly in front of it. What is this so-called "picture frame" stage in which a curtain represents the fourth wall?
People called this war that lasted from 1914 to 1918 the Great War. What war is usually considered the first modern worldwide war?

In fungi this structure takes the form of chitins and it is composed of a polymer called cellulose. Due to its turgor pressure, it prevents plant cells from undergoing cytolysis. Name this rigid permeable structure absent from an animal cell that surrounds the plasma membrane of most plant cells.
Correct the following sentence, if necessary: Will you give Harrison and I more ice cream?
The aquarium is 12 inches long by 8 inches wide by 10 inches deep. What is the volume of the aquarium in cubic inches?

This art form resembles decoupage [day-koo-PAHZH] and photomontage [fo-to-mahn-TAHZH]. An invention of Synthetic Cubism, it consists of everyday materials fastened to a background. Identify this art form that may use newspaper clippings, ticket stubs, or photographs.
The president and vice president play key roles in this government branch. It also includes the president's cabinet. What branch's responsibilities include enforcing laws made by Congress?

The nearest living relatives of these creatures are horseshoe crabs. These creatures became the most common animals on Earth during the Cambrian Explosion, but these water dwelling arthropods went extinct at the end of the Permian period. Name this diverse group of insectlike fossil animals named for their three lobed bodies.
Spelled one way, this word is a synonym of "rough." Spelled another way, it names a college class or one part of a meal. Give this word for the place where golf is played.
This question requires multiple responses. Between what two whole numbers does the probability of an event occur?

Some historians call this art style Neo-Impressionism. Paul Signac [seen-YAK] learned it from his mentor and the style's inventor, Georges Seurat [ZHAWRZH suh-RAH]. What was this style that used small brush strokes or dots of color that the viewer's eye blended together?
This legal term sounds like the last part of a TV game show. What term means you cannot be tried or face punishment for the same crime more than once?

Taxonomy is the biologic science of classification that arranges organisms into groups like orders and families. The modern system divides all organisms into one of five of these broad categories. What is the term for the largest taxonomic group after Domain, with Animalia and Plantae as examples?
How many words in the following sentence need to be capitalized? Our class began reading The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe.
The first four numbers in a sequence are 3, 7, 11, and 15. What is the next number in the sequence?

This artist imagined similar scenes in his paintings Circus Sideshow and The Circus. His works, including Can-Can and The Eiffel Tower, consist of small dots of pure color. Who was this leader of the Pointillist style?

Land, tools, and workers are examples of these things. Some adjectives used to describe these are natural, renewable, and non-renewable. What are things that people need to meet their needs and wants?

Iron is an example of these inorganic substances that keep the body working properly. They help to keep teeth and bones strong and also maintain muscles. Identify this class of substances that work with vitamins in order to maintain optimum health.

This part of speech can be relative, demonstrative [duh-MON-struh-tiv], or indefinite. It may also be reflexive, intensive, or personal. What is this part of speech, whose examples include "ourselves" and "my"?
This question requires multiple answers. What are the exponents in the mathematical expression 2 cubed plus 4 squared?

Like the Mennonites, this Christian group descends from Swiss and German Anabaptists. Followers dress simply and many work as farmers, carpenters, or blacksmiths. Name this group that lives separately from the rest of society and refuses to use electricity or technology.
This mountain is located in Georgia. It has an enormous relief carved into its north face. What mountain includes a carving of Confederate leaders?

This technology also used Network Control Programs, which are analogous to communication protocols, and its applications increased with the development of file transfer protocol, though the majority of its early usage was for e-mail. Name this predecessor of the internet, developed by a part of the Defense Department.
Identify the following sentence's noun clause: I will tell whoever will listen my good news.
Van Gogh used four blue paints and three green paints. He then added four more blue paints and 1 more green paint. How many total paints did Van Gogh use?

This animated film is named for a magical, mountainous realm that protects the Madrigal family. Its protagonist, Mirabel, searches for answers when her family members begin losing their magical powers. Identify this Disney movie that gave the world "We Don't Talk About Bruno."
This president is the only one to have been impeached more than once. He was elected in 2016. Who was the 45th president of the United States?

Dr Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine against this disease by studying a related illness in milkmaids. Due to his discovery, this disease was declared eradicated in 1979. Name this infectious disease that killed many natives of the Americas and was probably a mutated form of cowpox.
Spelling required. Every afternoon, the performers will rehearse for the talent show. Spell the word from the previous sentence that is a synonym of "practice."
This musical dynamic marking is the opposite of "piano." On sheet music, a lowercase F symbolizes it. Identify this dynamic marking meaning a note should be sung or played loudly.

This sequel to All Alone in the Universe is loosely based on Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream. It follows the summer adventures of Lenny, Phil, Hector, Patty, and Debbie. What is this Lynne Rae Perkins Newbery winner?
This question requires multiple answers in correct order. Arrange the following temperatures from smallest to largest: 55 degrees Fahrenheit, 0 degrees Fahrenheit, and negative 4 degrees Fahrenheit.
questions.a: NEGATIVE 4, 0, 55 (DEGREES FAHRENHEIT) (NOTE: MUST BE GIVEN IN THIS ORDER)

questions.q: In science, substances are matter that has a chemical composition that is always the same. What special substance is made up of only one type of atom?
You can visit the Elk and Bison Prairie here. What is this national recreation area located between Kentucky and Barkley lakes?

This vocal technique likely began when jazz singers tried to imitate instrumental sounds. Ella Fitzgerald and Louis Armstrong were experts at it. What is this substitution of made-up, nonsense sounds for a song's words?

In this picture book, the widow Gateau runs a boarding house where she lives with her daughter. That daughter asks the Great Bellini to teach her the skill of wire walking. Name this Caldecott-winning book written and illustrated by Emily Arnold McCully.
The numerals 7, 17, and 19 are examples of these types of numbers. What kind of positive whole number have only two positive factors: itself and one?

There are two basic groups of forces. One type, more mechanical in nature, has an object directly acting on another object while the other does not. What type of force, an example of which is gravity, allows for movement without the touching of two objects?
George Nicholas was the primary writer of the Kentucky Constitution dated in this year. In what year did Kentucky join the Union as the fifteenth state?

Westerners call one of these instruments with an indefinite pitch a tam-tam. It can have shallow or deep rims and may have a knob in the center. Identify this large metal plate that the player hits with a beater.
This man wrote of a sailor missing his young child in the lullaby "Sweet and Low." He described a white nocturnal bird in "The Owl." Identify the English poet of "The Charge of the Light Brigade."
Sarina wants to arrange a set of blocks in four rows so that each row has the same number of each colored block. She has 16 red blocks and 8 blue blocks. How many red blocks should be in each row?

When helping your family string Christmas lights, you find that the strand is not working because the lights are wired together in a special type of circuit. In this type of circuit, there is only one path for the current to go, and any blown out bulb will cause the strand to stop working. What type of circuit is this?
The border between the U.S. and this country is the longest international border on earth. What United States' northern neighbor also shares Niagara Falls with the U.S.?

This opera's setting is Charleston, South Carolina's Catfish Row. Sometimes called an American folk opera, it opens with the song "Summertime." Give the title of this opera by DuBose Heyward and George and Ira Gershwin.

In this novel, the title tween moves to Riverboro, Maine to live with her aunts. Although Aunt Miranda finds fault with her, she remains positive, even giving their farm its cheerful name. Identify this Kate Douglas Wiggin novel.
A recipe calls for one and one-third cups of flour for each batch of cookies. You need to bake 3 batches of cookies. How many cups of flour will you need?

This rock is a common rock of the coarse-grained igneous rocks. Made up of quartz and feldspar, this material is known to be very hard and works well as a building material. Name this type of rock found in Stone Mountain in Georgia and often used as counter tops in kitchens.
Areas in the United States south of the 36th parallel are known by this name. The Sunshine State is a prime example of states in this region. What area is named for its warm temperatures?

This American folk dance descends from English country dances. A relative of the European quadrille, it calls for steps like the do-si-do, sashay, and promenade. What is this dance style named for the geometric shape the couples make?

Examples of this sound device include "sploosh," "zoom," "hiccup," and "bang." Comic books rely on other examples like "zap," "boom," and "pow." What do we call a word that resembles the sound it represents?
Two numbers are in the ratio 3:1. (three to one). The sum of the two numbers is 32. What is the larger number?

The continuous movement of water in its various forms throughout the atmosphere and surface is commonly called the water cycle. Scientfically speaking, this cycle sees precipitation, run-off, evaporation, and condensation work together to continuously provide the planet with a stream of fresh water. Based on the ancient root word for water, what is the scientific name for the water cycle?
This people of Mexico were probably nomadic at first. They became the dominant group of central America in the 15th century. What empire did Cortes overthrow in 1521?

In a scene from Royal Wedding, this man appeared to dance on a room's walls and ceiling. He often performed in a top hat, white tie, and tails while carrying a cane. Identify this on-screen partner of Ginger Rogers.

In one fable, this animal drowns a mouse by tying the rodent to its leg. In another fable, these aquatic animals burrow into the mud when a group of hares passes them by. Name these amphibians who, in yet another Aesop story, wish for a king.
The trail is 1.75 (one point seven five) kilometers. How many meters long is the trail?

The planetary type got their name because they appear similar to distant planets, and include the Eskimo and Dumbbell. Name these regions where star and planet formation takes place, a type of interstellar cloud.
This group of investors hoped to find gold and silver in the New World. What group was chartered by James the First to colonize the eastern coast of North America?

In this musical, the protagonist transforms Boq into the Tin Man, while Fiyero [fee-YAIR-oh] becomes a scarecrow. Popular Glinda rooms with green-skinned Elphaba [ELF-uh-buh] at Shiz University. Identify this musical reimagining of The Wonderful Wizard of Oz.

In this fairy tale, four animals escape death at the hands of their respective owners. The donkey, rooster, cat, and dog make so much noise that they frighten away robbers and take over the thieves' house. Identify this Brothers Grimm fairy tale, whose title mentions a northern German city.
A recipe calls for 1 pint of beans. How many cups of beans does the cook need?

At times, cellular regulation doesn't function properly and abnormal growths emerge. The suffix “-oma”, as in sarcoma or carcinoma, is used for this type of abnormal tissue growth. Name these masses that may be biopsied to test for cancer.
When this land was purchased, it doubled the size of the United States territory. The United States paid $15 million for this land. What land purchase did President Thomas Jefferson arrange?

This Lerner and Loewe musical features the songs "I Could Have Danced All Night" and "The Rain in Spain." In it, phonetics professor Henry Higgins teaches Eliza Doolittle how to behave and speak like a proper English lady. Name this musical adaptation of George Bernard Shaw's play Pygmalion [pig-MALE-ee-un].
This Anglo-Saxon suffix means "condition" or "state of." In many cases, it transforms an adjective into a noun. What is this suffix that might follow "dark" or "kind"?
A line segment is this type of angle. What type of angle measures 180 degrees?
