Members of this kingdom have bodies made from hyphae, reproduce by way of spores, and have cell walls that contain chitin. Decomposers such as molds are members of which kingdom of organisms that also includes yeasts and mushrooms?
Two word answer please. Many banks and businesses were forced to close during this time. It lasted about ten years. What was this period of economic hardship that began in 1929?

This substance formed a so-called "army" of statues found in a Chinese tomb. It can apply to unglazed ceramic art, sculpture, or architecture made from porous clay. What is this reddish-brown substance with a name meaning "baked earth"?

As a verb, it can mean, quote, "to deposit (an article) as security for the repayment of a loan." As a noun, it may refer to, quote, "someone who is used or manipulated to further another person's purposes." What is this word for the lowest valued piece in chess?
A square box measures 10 units on each side. Determine the volume of the box in cubic units.

Karl von Frisch determined that these animals communicate food locations by way of dancing. Male ones of these animals are only used for mating and do not assist female workers with gathering nectar or pollen. Habitat loss and the use of pesticides threaten what insects that produce honey?
Advisors to the president make up this part of the executive branch. What group includes fifteen heads of the executive departments?

This early 20th-century art movement grew from psychologist Sigmund Freud's theories. Its artists explored strange images from their dreams and unconscious minds. Identify this movement that spawned The Persistence of Memory by Salvador Dalí.

This punctuation mark's em version is slightly longer than its en version. It can replace a comma, parenthesis, or colon, as well as indicate a range between dates. What is this punctuation that resembles a hyphen?

Balloons-R-Us makes 16 different balloon bouquets using only red, green, and yellow balloons. Each bouquet uses one of each color balloon. The company has 2 different red balloons and 4 different green balloons. How many different yellow balloons do they use?

This is the condition of optimal functioning for the organism and includes many variables, such as body temperature and fluid balance, being kept within certain pre-set limits. In biology, what is the state of steady internal, physical, and chemical conditions maintained by living systems.
Every person has the right to report news without censorship from the government. What is this right guaranteed by the First Amendment?

Among this woman's paintings were The Old Oaken Bucket, Catching the Thanksgiving Turkey, and Sugaring-Off in the Maple Orchard. She also created Making Apple Butter, Black Horses, and other scenes from rural American life at the turn of the 20th century. Give the name of this artist, who had her first professional exhibition at age 80.
Correct the following sentence, if needed: Whom should I speak with about the noise?
Determine the rule for this number sequence. The first number is two and the third number is eight and the fourth number is eleven. What number should be added each time?

Located in the small of your back, these fist-sized organs play a key role in filtering your blood. Name this pair of organs, located next to the adrenal glands, that allow humans to process waste from the body for excretion as urine.
This happens when demand for a resource is greater than the supply. What economic term means there is not enough of a resource to meet people's needs and wants?
questions.a: SCARCITY (ACCEPT: OTHER FORMS OF THE WORD)

questions.q: These large folk art objects represented the owner's mythical ancestors. Similar to a European family crest, they once decorated Native American settlements in the Pacific Northwest. Identify these tall wooden poles carved and painted to resemble animals or people.
This type of verbal appears in the sentence, "Removing her parka, she hung it on the coat rack." In it, a verb acts as an adjective. Name this phrase, whose verb ends in -ed or -ing.
The baseball team is selling donated chili dinners for $10 each. By the end of the day, they had sold 27 dinners. How much money did the team earn?

Scientists believe that earthquakes begin in the core, travelling outward to the crust. The scientific study of the Earth’s core is often related to this science of earthquakes because they are both concerned with elastic waves traveling through Earth. What scientific field is related to the study of the Earth's core?
This federal holiday is celebrated in September each year. What holiday honors the contributions of the nation's workers?

This author of Don't Forget, God Bless Our Troops titled her autobiography Where the Light Enters: Building a Family, Discovering Myself. While serving as second lady, she taught English at Northern Virginia Community College. In January 2021, who became the First Lady of the United States?
Spelling required. Torrential rain delayed the semifinal baseball game. Spell the word from the preceding sentence that means "violently or forcefully flowing."
Today's Pets has 5 dachshund puppies. PetSmart has 2 fewer dachshunds than Today's Pets. How many dachshund puppies do the two pet shops have all together?

This man described the “music of the spheres” in his Harmonices Mundi. He determined that the Sun lies at a focal point of the elliptical orbits of the planets. Name this German astronomer who formulated three laws of planetary motion.
When he was elected in 2008, this man became a first for the presidency. He was born in Hawaii in 1961 and he spent much of his life in Indonesia. Who was the first African American president?

This book precedes two other novels subtitled At the Edge of the World and The End of Time. Its hero is an orphaned boy who learns that his father was a wealthy man. Name this medieval-set novel, which earned a Newbery Medal for Avi.
Helen drew a section of a number line that started with negative 10 and ended with positive 4. What number is located in the center of the number line?

This musical symbol's name comes from the Italian for "stop" or "stay." It consists of a dot with a curved line atop it. Name this so-called "birdseye" that means a musician should hold a note longer than its normal duration.
Just below Louisville, the falls of this river makes water travel difficult. Its name comes from the Seneca word meaning "Good River." What is the river that forms the northern boundary of Kentucky?

If you mix a gallon of water with a cup of salt, you will make a mixture. However, since water has a different boiling point than salt, the mixture can be easily separated back into its original components. Scientifically speaking, what type of change did mixing water and salt represent?

This picture book's images include a sea turtle with seashells on its back and a blue eye staring at a hermit crab. In it, a young boy discovers an underwater world thanks to a waterproof camera. Identify this Caldecott winner by David Wiesner [WEEZ-nur].
On Monday 45 schools registered for Governor's Cup. On Wednesday 17 more schools registered. How many schools registered on those two days?

The string one of these ensembles traditionally consists of two violins, a viola, and a cello. A vocal one may have a soprano, alto, tenor, and bass. Give the word for a group of, or a piece written for a group of, four musicians.

Legend claims that he was the first white man to explore Kentucky. This young man was wounded and captured by the Shawnee in Northern Kentucky. What man was saved from burning at the stake by a Shawnee chief who adopted him.

If you slide across a smooth floor in socks, you will move easily at first, and then stop. When you stop, you may notice that the force acting against you has warmed the soles of your feet, almost like you do when you rub your hands together. Name this force, that resists the motion of two surfaces that are touching.
This poetic form's most famous example is likely "Snow" by Adelaide Crapsey, the form's inventor. Its lines have two, four, six, eight, and two syllables. Name this unrhymed five-line poem.
Compare the multiples of the numbers 7, 4, and 2. What is the lowest common multiple of the three numbers?

This word can refer to a woodwind class subdivided into fipple and transverse types. The piccolo is the modern orchestra's smallest and highest-pitched example of one. What is this metal woodwind held parallel to the floor and played by directing a stream of air against a sharp edge?
This reference book is named for the Titan that held the Earth on his shoulders. Worldinmaps.com is an electronic version of this book. What is a book of maps and charts?
Magnets are objects that attract some metal. All magnets have two special regions where the magnetic pull is strongest. What is the name given to these regions that can be found in every magnet?

This 11-year-old orphan moves to Beldingsville, Vermont, to live with her spinster aunt. She plays the "glad game," but temporarily loses her optimism when an accident leaves her paralyzed. Name this happy creation of Eleanor H. Porter.
Three and four-ninths balls of yarn lay in the basket. Fluffy unwound one and one-third balls. As a mixed number, how many balls of yarn were NOT unwound by the kitten?

This opera's characters include the magician Sarastro [suh-ROSS-troh] and the Queen of the Night. At its conclusion, Papageno [pa-puh-GAY-noh] and Papagena love each other, as do Tamino and Pamina. Masonic symbols are found throughout which Mozart work about an enchanted instrument?
This state's population has grown more than any other state's population between 2010 and 2020 according to the 2020 census. What state has its capital at Austin?

This soft, rock is made of many layers of sediment pushed together. Due to its clay-like origin, pieces of vegetation can often be trapped in between the layers, leaving it with abundant fossils. Name this type of rock that, over time, will become slate.
Your friend uses this figure of speech when she says, "I'm so hungry I could eat a horse!" What is this over-the-top exaggeration, often for humorous effect?
Multiple answers. Two numbers are in the ratio 4:3. The sum of the two numbers is 14. What are the two numbers?

The Romantic type of this dance costume reached to within 12 inches of the floor. Throughout the 1800s, it was shortened until almost the entire leg became visible. Name this frilly, multi-layered skirt worn by ballerinas.
This group of South American people ruled an empire in the Andes Mountains. They left no written records of their early civilization. What civilization was led by Atahualpa?

While weather changes from hour-to-hour, week-to-week, or month to month, one environmental condition tends to remain relatively stable. Defined as the cumulative weather patterns over the course of an extended period of time, give the name for this scientific descriptor, examples of which may be mild, temperate, or rainy.

Legends claim this creature sings campfire songs as it mimics a human voice. Only whiskey can calm an angry one, and lumberjacks supposedly wore stovepipes to protect their legs from attacks by these cryptids. What is this mythical rabbit/deer hybrid?
One mile equals 1,760 yards. How many feet are in one mile?

This director and choreographer earned a special Oscar for his contributions to film musicals. He both choreographed and starred in An American in Paris. Who was this choreographer, co-director, and co-star of Singin' in the Rain?

These workers agreed to work for landowners for several years. The landowners paid for their passage to America. What two word identifier was given to these workers who might receive some land after their service ended?

The interplanetary explorer with the greatest longevity was launched on March 2, 1972, and on June 13, 1983, became the first manmade object to travel beyond the known solar system. Name this explorer, retired in March 1997.

Multiple answer required. In a nursery rhyme, these three items are the counterparts of "sugar and spice and everything nice." State the three things, according to the rhyme, that little boys are made of.
The spool of ribbon is two and two-thirds yards long. How many inches long is the ribbon?

This musical combines plot points from Gertrude McFuzz and the two Horton picture books. Among its characters are JoJo, the Grinch, and the Cat in the Hat. Give the title of this musical filled with Theodor Geisel's creations.

President Jefferson sent a secret message to Congress about this expedition. Officially, the group conducting this expedition was called the Corps of Discovery. What expedition explored the Louisiana Purchase?

Nobel laureate Linus Pauling advocated taking mega-doses of this compound to prevent the common cold. This compound is needed by the body to build collagen in cells, so its deficiency will result in scurvy. Name this vitamin concentrated in citrus fruits like limes and oranges.
The first half of this compound word is an antonym of "under." The second half is an antonym of "catch." Give this verb that can mean "to bring down a government."
The minute hand of a clock makes one complete turn every hour. What type of angle is formed between the minute hand and the hour hand at 1:15?

This part of a concert or opera was usually spontaneous, although modern-day versions are often planned. With a name meaning "still" or "again" in French, it occurs at a performance's conclusion when the audience applauds. Give the word for this demand of a repeated song or the performance of additional material.
This president was a general in the army. One of his main accomplishments was the interstate road system. Who was the 34th president of the United States?

After receiving one of these objects from Madagascar, Charles Darwin correctly predicted the existence of a moth with footlong mouth parts. This plant structure includes a style and a stigma that may be fertilized by crosspollination thanks to animals like bees. Fruits and seeds are produced by what reproductive organ of plants, that is often surrounded by colorful petals?

Spelled one way, this word means "doing nothing" and can refer to a state in which an engine runs on low power. Spelled another way, it can signify a false god or a celebrity. State the shared pronunciation for these words.
Lisa needs to fill a ball with air. The ball has a radius of 3 inches. In terms of pi and in cubic inches, what is the volume of the ball that she needs to fill with air?
This substance primes rough wood or canvas for paint. It is a white paint mixture that combines glue with chalk or plaster. Identify this liquid, whose name is Italian for "gypsum."
John Roberts is the Chief Justice of this group. What group of nine justices includes four women and five men?

This phylum includes the largest number of organisms, hands down! This phylum is characterized by organisms with a segmented body, jointed appendages, and an exoskeleton. Name this phylum which includes insects and crustaceans.
How many words in the following sentence need to be capitalized? We took a field trip to the Capitol Building in Frankfort.
The probability of winning a candy bar at the snack stand is three-sevenths. What is the probability of NOT winning a candy bar?
questions.a: 4/7 (CHANCE OF NOT WINNING) (ACCEPT: 4 OVER 7, 4 OUT OF 7)

questions.q: To create this type of work, an artist sets tesserae [TESS-uh-ree] into mortar that hardens to keep them in place. Since ancient times, they have decorated walls, floors, and ceilings, as well as outdoor pavements. Name this artwork made of small pieces of stone, glass, or tile.
Every American citizen has this inalienable right. What right is the first right listed in the Declaration of Independence?

Animals of this type do not require as much food as others in order to survive, but they are more affected by fluctuating temperature. Give the scientific term for animals, like lizards, that cannot regulate their own body temperature.

This online site was founded by Pierre Omidyar in 1995 and is based in San Jose [ho-zay], California. It facilitates consumer to consumer and business to consumer sales through its website. What is this online auction site?

This heat transfer process is responsible for the Earth's system of plate tectonics, as it occurs in the mantle. It is contrasted with heat transfer by direct contact or through a vacuum. Identify this type of heat transfer, which takes place in namesake currents.

This ballerina starred in Gise//e and Sleeping Beauty for the Vic-Wells Ballet. She created roles for Frederick Ashton when that company became the Royal Ballet. Who was this prima ballerina and frequent co-star of Rudolf Nureyev [noo-REY-ef]?

This nursery rhyme ends with the refrain, "The cheese stands alone." The title refers to an occupation and a small, wooded valley. Give the title of this nursery rhyme where every stanza includes, "Heigh-ho the derry-o."

State your answer as a fraction. Marco has 13 jelly beans in his lunch bag. Eight of the jelly beans are orange and the rest are yellow. If Marco chooses one jelly bean randomly, what is the probability that Marco will choose a yellow jelly bean?

First and last name. This collaborator with New Balance on a sustainable tennis shoe also founded the luxury streetwear brand MSFTS. He donated Water Boxes to Flint, Michigan, and founded JUST Water to reduce single-use plastic and help the environment. Identify this actor and rapper, whose father Will once starred in The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air.

These mass transit systems from the 19th and 20th centuries were named for the long, strong wire! that pulled them along. Identify these public transportation systems, particularly associated with San Francisco.
This Greek root can follow "agora-" or "claustro-." Identify this root that can also be a standalone word for an irrational fear or hatred.

Although it may appear like a new moon, it occurs only on nights with a full moon. It occurs when the Earth blocks the path of sunlight to this object. What is this astronomical event, contrasted with the solar variety?

This character may have been a Brothers Grimm creation, or he may have descended from a Grim Reaper-like Irish legend. He may also have been inspired by a real Hessian soldier who lost a crucial body part to a cannonball during the Revolutionary War. Identify this spooky rider who terrifies Ichabod Crane in Washington Irving's story "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow."
Examples of this stage of development often look very similar to adult insects. It replaces the larva and pupa stage. Identify this stage, unique to incomplete metamorphosis.

This dance style melds the Lancashire clog and Irish jig with West African step dances. Soft shoe and buck and wing were early techniques gradually replaced by Broadway style. Dancers of what style, like Savion Glover and Gregory Hines, wear leather shoes with metal plates attached to the soles?

This is one of the four census regions of the United States Census Bureau, along with the Northeastern, Western, and Southern regions of the United States. Some states of this region include Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, and Nebraska. Name this region of the United States, between the Northeast and Great Plains.
Two-word answer required. What name is given to a triangle with one ninety-degree angle and exactly two equal sides?
What is the greatest common factor for 60 and 75?

This element of art is implied in drawings and most paintings but actual in sculptures. Like shape, it can be either organic or geometric. Identify this three-dimensional artistic element with length, width, and height.

The first part of this compound word is a natural force consisting of moving air. The second half names a hollow cylinder made of wood, metal, or some other material that lets liquids or gasses pass through it. Give this compound word, the less formal name for the trachea [TRAY-kee-uh].

This type of change occurs through, among other ways, phase changes or mixing. These do not change the chemical formula of materials involved. What is this type of change, contrasted with chemical change?

According to this Amendment, homeowner rights are different during times of peace than during times of war. What Constitutional amendment deals with whether or not the government can force a homeowner to give troops somewhere to stay?
What is the result when 4 and one-half is divided by one-half?
This instrument's original name was the sackbut. Glenn Miller and Tommy Dorsey played this brass instrument during the big band era. Name this instrument that changes pitch by way of a long slide.
Spelling required. The customer attempted to negotiate a fair price. Spell the word in the previous sentence that means, quote, "to deal or bargain with another."

The highest point in these mountains is called Spruce Knob. These mountains are bordered to the south by the Cumberland Mountains. Identify this division of the Appalachians, which stretches through parts of Pennsylvania, Maryland, West Virginia, and Virginia.
Contrary to a popular saying, these animals can see. They do use echolocation, and they are known for consuming blood from their prey. Name this group of flying mammals.
What is the sum, in degrees, of the exterior angles, taking one at each vertex, of a regular polygon?

This novel's protagonists are twins Sandy and Dennys Murry. Before unicorns help them return home, they help Noah build the ark to escape the Great Flood. What is this novel from Madeleine L'Engle's Time Quintet?

This theatrical experience is also called a walkdown or a final bow. Give the alliterative phrase for the time after a play or musical ends when the audience claps and the performers return to the stage.

They are also known as the vitellus, and animals that give live birth generally do not produce them. They are sometimes separated from the whites, to create lower calorie recipes. What is this nutrient rich part of an egg, which is usually yellow?

This is a type of air pollution caused by smoke from burning coal mixing with sulfur dioxide. This was a serious problem for the city of London, England in the late 19th through the mid-20th century. What is this term for a combination of fog and smoke?
What property of math explains that 2 times the sum of 3 and 4 is the same as 2 times 3 plus 2 times 4?

Many examples of this type of kinetic structure consist of flat colored shapes suspended from wires. This art form was invented by Alexander Calder. What is this artwork often is used to keep a baby entertained in a crib?

This type of scientist often works closely with chemists, astronomers, and mathematicians, and their work can be applied in engineering. They can specialize in the particle, astro-, and nuclear subtypes. What type of scientist studies the behavior of matter and energy, and has Stephen Hawking and Albert Einstein as examples?

This important military action was taking place in the west, at the same time as the Battle of, Gettysburg occurred in the east. This is considered a major victory for General Ulysses S. Grant. Name this Civil War conflict that took place in the summer of 1863, in Mississippi.

This book's title character is an elderly man who works at the zoo. When he catches a cold, his penguin, elephant, owl, rhinoceros, and tortoise friends visit him at home. Give the name of this Caldecott-winning book by Philip C. and Erin E. Stead.

During this musical period, new vocal forms like the cantata, oratorio, and opera developed. Music separated the bass and melody lines, and sometimes used counterpoint. The years 1600 to 1750 were the approximate dates of what era, during which Johann Sebastian Bach composed?
These subatomic particles are larger than particles in the surrounding cloud. Along with neutrons, they are nucleons. Name these positively charged subatomic particles.
This economist was credited with first explaining the Law of Supply and Demand. He is often referred to as the Father of Modern Capitalism. Name this economist known for his work Wealth of Nations.
This sound device uses words that mimic the sounds of the objects or actions they reference. "Woof," "slurp," and "pop" are examples of what literary device?
A convex polygon has ten sides. What is the specific name given to this shape?

From top to bottom, this instrument consists of a bell, bass, wing, and butt joint. A curved metal tube called the crook holds its double reed. Give the name of this lowest-pitched and largest woodwind instrument.
Their seeds are not protected by fruits or similar structures. Examples of these plants include the conifers and the ginkgo. Name these plants, contrasted with angiosperms.
This man was a Puritan minister, theologian, and author. He left Massachusetts Bay Colony over religious disagreements. Name this founder of Providence Plantations.

This novel's protagonist is C-average student Katie Takeshima [tah-kuh-SHEE-muh]. She vows to improve her grades because her sister Lynn, who dies of lymphoma, wanted her to. The Japanese word for "glittering" is the title of what Newbery winner by Cynthia Kadohata?
Anumber has a prime factorization of 2 cubed times three squared. What is this number?
This poet made a legendary Native American chief the hero of The Song of Hiawatha. Real colonial, people inspired The Courtship of Miles Standish. Name the poet of "Paul Revere's Ride."
This man served as the seventh vice president of the United States. He was a defender of slavery. Name this advocate for states rights and nullification, from South Carolina.

Japanese woodcuts inspired this Impressionist artist's print The Letter. A Woman and a Girl Driving, Lilacs in a Window, and The Boating Party were also her works. Name this artist of The Child's Bath. and Mother and Child.
His invention involved the repurposing of the cowpox virus. He is called the "the father of immunology." Name this developer of the smallpox vaccine.
A word game includes a die containing the first ten letters of the alphabet. What is the probability of rolling a consonant on this die?

This explorer was the founder of the city of Detroit, Michigan. He was also Governor of Louisiana between 1710 and 1716. Identify this French explorer, who lends his name to a luxury car brand manufactured by GM.

This art medium can decorate outdoor pavements or indoor walls, ceilings, or floors. Today, bits of metal and brick may be part of this artwork, but ancient examples from the Roman Empire still exist. Identify this work made of small pieces of glass, stone, or tile set in mortar.
State the following sentence's simple predicate: Before the pandemic, Abraham and his mother had planned a trip to France.
An equilateral triangle has a side with a length of 18 units. What is the perimeter, in units, of the triangle?
This bone joins to the tibia and to the pelvis. Name this largest bone in the human body.

This composer based his opera Don Giovanni on the Don Juan legend. He gave one of his string serenades a German title meaning "A Little Night Music." Give the name of this Classical composer, who left his work Requiem unfinished at his death.

The so-called "back" version of this punctuation mark is only used in coding. The forward variety can indicate a line break in poetry or plays, but it can also replace the word "or." Identify this punctuation mark used in dates and fractions.

This amendment protects people from self incrimination. It also provides protection against being tried twice for the same crime. Name this amendment, which protects an individual's right to remain silent.
It is a component of batholiths and is a hard rock with no visible crystal structure. It is an example of an intrusive igneous rock. Name this rock, often used to make countertops.
Consider the pattern of numbers that begins with the numbers 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, and 19. What is the next number in this pattern?

This method of tree removal usually pertains to areas of 20 acres or more. It can destroy an area's ecological integrity in several ways. Identify this process, where entire wooded areas are completely cut down.

This executive producer and judge of the World of Dance TV show co-founded a children's health charity with her sister. She is a singer, dancer, and actress who, in 2021, resumed her relationship with ex-fiancé Ben Affleck. Name this founder of the J. Lo clothing line.

This president adjusted one of his State of the Union Addresses to speak about the Challenger explosion. A year later, he spoke to a Soviet president in front of Berlin's Brandenburg Gate. Name this Republican leader, a former actor who, in 1987, said, "Mister Gorbachev, tear down this wall."
This type of energy can be converted to electrical energy in a battery, and is a form of potential energy. It usually involves compounds. What is this energy of molecular bonds?
Jason has 25 baseball cards and Rob has 75. What is the ratio of the number of Jason's cards to the number of Rob's cards?
Examples of these machines include the balance and the seesaw. One component of them is a rigid beam. Name these simple machines, which involve a fulcrum.
This document was ratified in June of 1788 and went into effect in March of 1789. It includes seven articles and 27 amendments. Name this document that sets forth the rules for U.S. government.
This formal kind of balance may be radial or bilateral. Identify this quality that a shape has if it is identical on both sides of an imaginary axis.
This suffix might follow "age," "end," or "use." Give this suffix that, as a standalone word, is the opposite of "more."
Jerry has 2 pairs of pants, 8 shirts and 2 pairs of shoes. Using just these items, how many different outfits can Jerry wear if each outfit consists of 1 pair of pants, 1 shirt, and 1 pair of shoes?

This Latin American dance combined elements of the danzén [dahn-SOHN] and mambo. It requires two slow forward-and-back steps followed by three quick side steps. Give the repetitive name of this Cuban dance.
These temporary cell extensions are often found in amoebae [uh-ME-bay]. They are often used for propulsion. Give this term, meaning "false foot."

This Kentucky region is shaped like an arc and wraps around the southern and eastern parts of the Bluegrass region. It is the smallest of Kentucky's geographic regions. Identify this hilly region of Kentucky.

This fable's moral is "Gratitude is the sign of a noble soul." It ends with the Roman emperor freeing both of the title characters, who have faced off in an arena. Name this Aesop fable about an escaped slave who removes a thorn from a large cat's paw.
Sheila is making a list of the positive factors of 18. How many numbers are on the list?

The first part of this compound word is a primary color whose complementary color is orange. The second part can mean "to publish a manuscript" or "a reproduction of an original artwork." Identify this compound word for a detailed plan that shows how a building will be constructed.

This type of symmetry is contrasted with the bilateral variety, which is seen in almost all animals. Pentagonal symmetry is often considered a subtype of it, which is exhibited in sea stars. Identify this form of symmetry that can be rotated about a central point.

This musical's songs include "Hopelessly Devoted to You," "Summer Nights," and "You're the One That I Want." Its characters, members of the T-Birds and the Pink Ladies, attend Rydell High School in 1959. Sandy and Danny fall in love in what musical named for a product that makes hair shiny?
This battle was also known as the Battle of Chaplin Hills. It was the biggest Civil War battle fought. in the state of Kentucky. What was this Civil War battle, fought in Boyle County, Kentucky?
Suppose it takes Jack 3 and one-half seconds to run a 10 meter dash. If he was able to maintain this speed for a 100-meter dash, how many seconds would it take Jack to run the 100-meter dash?

These animals are members of the group Cingulata and they are related to anteaters and sloths. Their name comes from the Spanish for "little armored one." Identify these scaly animals seen in Texas and elsewhere in the South.

This term is generally synonymous with the phrase "the Roaring Twenties." Musical stars of this period included Joe "King" Oliver, Louis Armstrong, and Duke Ellington. Identify this age of American history, named for a type of American music associated with New Orleans.
Spelling required. Rain falls in small quantities during a severe drought. Spell the word from the preceding sentence that names a period of dry weather.

This religious ceremony was once a staple of many Plains tribes. It occurred when the buffalo returned in late spring or early summer and required a large pole to be erected. What was this dance to honor the Great Spirit's manifestation as a celestial body?
The distance between the ground and the top of the torch on the Statue of Liberty is 93 meters. What is this distance in decimeters?

Multiple answers. They are three types of material traditionally plotted on a phase diagram. They, are all more commonly seen and discussed, versus plasmas, super-cooled materials, or other phases. Name the three primary phases of matter.

She earned degrees from Princeton University, Worcester College, and Harvard Law School. She served as Solicitor General of the United States from 2009 to 2010. Name this Supreme Court justice appointed by President Obama in 2010.

The total rainfall for three months was recorded by Mr. Smith's class. In October, it rained 1.5 inches; in November, it rained 3.2 inches; and in December, it rained 2.7 inches. What is the total amount of rainfall in inches for the three months?

This novel's title building is a former stop on the Underground Railroad. Thomas Small explores his new home's hidden passages and discovers that the neighbors are trying to steal hidden treasure. What is this Virginia Hamilton novel?

Though the date of this folk song is unknown, this gospel song was used as an anthem during the Civil Rights movement in America. In what song does the singer state they are going to let the title object shine?
This mountain is part of the Alaska Range. The first recorded ascent of this mountain took place in 1913. Identify this tallest mountain in the United States.
To draw this musical note, use a solid head, a stem, and two flags. In 4/4 time, four of them are barred together to make one beat. Name this note, which is half the value of an eighth note.

They can come from comets, asteroids, or a similarly named object. They are objects that make it to the Earth's surface intact. What are these space objects, that strike the Earth, contrasted with meteoroids?

This picture book's narrator is a mouse whose toy airplane gets stuck in a tree. The title character convinces many animals to stand on top of each other to rescue the toy. What is this Caldecott winning book by Eric Rohmann?
There are 1000 millimeters in a meter, so a millimeter is one-thousandth of a meter. What is one thousandth of a millimeter?

Works in this nonfiction genre were some of the earliest historical writings. Examples include Elizabeth Leads the Way: Elizabeth Cady Stanton and The Right to Vote and A Voice Named Aretha. Give the word for a story someone writes about another person's life.

He was the third American in space, and orbited around the planet three times in 1962. In addition to being an astronaut, he was also a politician, Marine, and engineer. Identify this first American to orbit the Earth.

This tax impacted buyers of Colonial era newspapers, as well as legal and commercial documents. A namesake Congress met in New York City to protest this tax. Identify this tax, which sparked revolutionary spirit in the American colonies.

A number pattern has a rule that you add 3 to the first number to get the second number, and then you double the second number to get the third number. For example, if the starting number was 7, the number pattern would be 7, 10, and 20. If the starting number is 15, what is the third number in the number pattern?
A museum dedicated to this composer's work stands in Milan's La Scala opera house. His operas include Rigo/etto and one about an Ethiopian princess in Egypt. Name the composer of Afda [eye-EE-duh].
It is usually measured in nanometers or meters and is inversely related to frequency. It can also be measured from trough to trough. Give this term for the distance from peak to peak in a wave.

This battle was fought on August 19, 1782. Daniel Boone led the efforts against the Loyalists in this battle. Identify this battle from the American Revolution, fought near what is now Robertson County, Kentucky.

This novel's supporting characters include red-headed Will, Magister Reese, and John and Jennet Dark. The title character, a young girl named Alyce, learns from Jane how to help women give birth safely. Name this winner of the Newbery Medal, written by Karen Cushman.
Male ballet dancers often perform this move on the ball of the foot, while ballerinas do it on their toes. Give the French word for this rapid turning of the body on one leg.
A square has a perimeter of 20 units. What is the area, in square units, of the square?.

Many ballads, including "Sweet Betsy from Pike" and "Waltzing Matilda," fit into this musical category. Today, many examples are written down, but for centuries, they were passed down orally. Give the name for music written and performed by a culture's ordinary people.
This type of poem may emphasize any letter from any part of a word. Typically, it uses the first letters of words to spell out another word or phrase. Give the name of this type of poem.

These weather events are caused each year by changes in latitude of the Intertropical Convergence Zone. This term can also refer to short-term heavy rains in local areas. Identify this term for the tropical season characterized by near constant rains, most common near the equator.

This river rises in Montana and flows south and east for over 2,000 miles. It empties into the Mississippi River at St. Louis, Missouri. What is this river, which joins with the Mississippi to form the longest river in North America?
A sweater that normally sells for $50 is on sale. If the sale advertised 20% off, what is the new price for the sweater?

Many members of this religious group originally belonged to the Quakers. They lived in segregated communities where they made simple furniture and refused marriage. Ann Lee founded what group that once had a village at Mercer County's Pleasant Hill?
questions.a: SHAKER(S) (Accept (THE) UNITED SOCIETY OF BELIEVERS IN CHRIST’S SECOND APPEARING)

questions.q: Ben needs several tablespoons of sugar for a recipe. Ben doesn't have a tablespoon but he has a quarter cup. How many tablespoons are in a quarter cup?

This amendment recognized citizenship rights for those who had formerly been slaves in the United States. It grants equal protection of the laws for all citizens of the United States. Name this amendment that protects citizenship rights for all those born or naturalized here.
This apparent force acts outward on a revolving object. It can be felt when you are on a spinning ride at a fair or theme park. Name this rotation force, which has a similarly named lab device.
What is the following sentence's complete subject? Al's piano lessons improve his playing.

This Amendment was the topic of cases like Schenck versus United States and Debs versus United States, It guarantees our rights of petition and assembly, and freedom of religion, speech, and the press. Identify this amendment that starts the U.S. Bill of Rights.
Components of this system include the thyroid, pituitary, and adrenal glands. It is highly interlinked with the nervous system. Name this organ system, important for hormone regulation.
Onsheet music, this dynamic marking is represented by two lowercase P's. What is this Italian word, which means a note should be played or sung very softly?
Which words need to be capitalized in the following sentence? On vacation, we visited the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco.
questions.a: ON, GOLDEN, GATE, BRIDGE, SAN, FRANCISCO (any order)

questions.q: Four students form a line for the gymnastics meet. In how many different ways can they arrange themselves?

This landform is sometimes called the "Niagara of the South". At certain times, it has a rare phenomenon called a moonbow, which is formed by the mist in the air from the falls. Identify this Kentucky waterfall.
This planet has large bluish regions at its poles, as seen during the Juno mission. It is known for a Great Red Spot and for having many large moons. Identify this largest planet in the solar system.
Jason bought a ticket to the movies and some snacks. The ticket cost $8.00 and the snacks cost $7.25. If Jason paid with a $20 bill, how much change will Jason receive?

This brass instrument, a relative of the cornet and filigelhorn [FLOO-gul-horn], was invented in 1843. Common in military and brass bands, it is pitched an octave below the trumpet in C or B-flat. What is this large instrument that resembles a tuba?

This symphonic fairy tale was the work of Russian composer Sergei Prokofiev [pro-KAH-fee-ufh]. It uses different instruments to represent the title child, his grandfather, a bird, a duck, a cat, and hunters. What is this story about a young boy who outsmarts a forest predator?

This colonial object traditionally showed the Lord's Prayer, the alphabet, and the ten digits. Those items were written on paper that was mounted on a wooden tablet. Identify this colonial teaching tool named for the thin membrane stretched over the paper to protect it.

This mining method occurs mainly in Kentucky, West Virginia, Virginia, and Tennessee. It involves deforesting, and causes air and water pollution. Identify this form of strip mining, in which entire hilltops may be destroyed to mine coal.
It consists of matter with free electrons. It is very hot and makes up much of stars. What is this fourth state of matter?
This word precedes "Trace" in the historic name of a group of central Kentucky counties. What is this word for an area with little or no human settlement?
Liz read one-fifth of her book on Monday. If her book contains 300 pages, how many pages did Liz read on Monday?

Scientists do this with their senses or with various tools. Making these is important for coming up with research questions and for testing a hypothesis. Give this term for watching and recording something in science.
Mark added three-eighths of a cup of milk to a bowl. Julie then added one-third of a cup of milk to the bowl. How many cups of milk are in the bowl?
This Doric temple once housed a massive statue of the goddess Athena. A replica of it stands in Centennial Park in Nashville. Name this temple, whose remains stand on the Acropolis in Athens, Greece.
This is the earth's largest mountain carving. It is located in the Black Hills of South Dakota. Name this unfinished sculpture of a famous Native American leader.

This legendary North American creature is sometimes called a sasquatch. It supposedly lives in the mountains of western Canada and the United States' Pacific Northwest. What is this large, hairy creature named for the size of a certain body part?
This cathedral caught fire in April 2019. It is the most famous of the Gothic cathedrals of the Middle Ages. Name this Paris landmark that was not completely destroyed.
These single-celled organisms can use almost any organic compound for food. Some cause diseases, but most are harmless, and even beneficial. What organisms live in enormous numbers, even in your gut?
Mrs. Vance asks Andrew to choose a number between 7 and 23. He wants to pick the number that's exactly in the middle. Which number should Andrew pick?

This founder of the Society of Spiritual Arts taught Doris Humphrey and Martha Graham. The so called "first lady of American dance," she created dances inspired by Egyptian, Indian, and Japanese sources. Who founded a modern dance school with her husband Ted Shawn?
This word can refer to, quote, "a metal plate or rim for the hoof of an animal." What is this word that, for humans, may refer to a sneaker or sandal?

This settlement was located at the southern tip of Manhattan Island in the 17th century. It served as the seat of the colonial government for New Netherland. Give this name for the early Dutch settlement in North America.

This scale for measuring a property of minerals uses talc as an example of number one. The highest ranking mineral on this scale is the diamond. Identify the scale that measures the ability of one mineral to scratch another.

This material makes a piece of pottery stain-resistant and, in some cases, food safe. It is transparent, but adding metals to it can produce a variety of colors. Name this glass coating that fuses to a ceramic surface during kiln firing.

Spelling required. Jazz music gives grandpa nostalgia for his adolescence and young adulthood., Spell the word in the preceding sentence meaning, quote, "a longing for a time or event that has passed."
State your answer as a fraction. Two fair six-sided dice are tossed. What is the probability of rolling a sum of 2?

This writer named the title character of The Trumpet of the Swan after jazz musician Louis Armstrong. He created a small, mouse-like boy in Stuart Little. Identify the creator of Templeton, Wilbur, Fern, and the title spider in Charlotte's Web.

This religious building's altar wall features a fresco of the Last Judgment. Its ceiling shows prophets, sibyls, and scenes from Genesis, including The Creation of Adam. Identify this Italian chapel painted by Michelangelo.

This word names both a city and a province in eastern Canada. The city sits on the Saint Lawrence River, and the province was first settled in 1535 by Jacques Cartier. Identify this largely French speaking region of Canada.

Examples of these plants include conifers, but also most trees in environments without frost. They are contrasted with deciduous plants. What are these plants that do not lose their leaves in the fall?
What is the name given to a pair of lines that do not lie in the same plane and never intersect?

The smallest known one of these was created using DNA, and other man-made ones were commonly seen on houses before the 21st century. They are sometimes called feelers, and are found naturally in arthropods. Name these structures on the heads of many insects, used for sensing the environment.

This theatrical form is related to a type of puppet theater called bunraku [boon-RAH-koo]. Dating from the 1600s, it relies on mime, singing, and dancing done by performers in full makeup. Only men perform what traditional Japanese drama?

This was the date of one of the worst terrorist attacks in United States history. This date each year is memorialized as "Patriot Day" in the United States. What was this date of the attacks on the World Trade Center and Pentagon?

This star of a wordless picture book is a white animal with black nose, ears, and tail. She plays with her favorite red toy until a brown dog pops it, but she soon learns to love its blue replacement. Who is this dog, who receives a ball in a Caldecott-winning Chris Raschka [ROSH-kuh] picture book?
What is the simplified expression when the quantity 2X squared, close quantity, is all raised to the third power?

This comet was the first whose return was predicted. It was also the first to be imaged by spacecraft, when it returned in 1986. Identify this comet that was named for the English astronomer who first predicted its return.

Born Nora Lum, this actress voiced Otto in The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run. She played Ming Fleetfoot in Jumanji: The Next Level and Katy in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings. Identify this voice of Sisu in Raya and the Last Dragon, whose stage name sounds like a brand of bottled water.
The strike note of this particular instrument which resides in Philadelphia is E-flat. It is known for being cracked and its symbolism of American freedom. Name this famous bell.

Her poems have included "Phenomenal Woman," "Alone," and "Still I Rise." Much of her work was inspired by her personal life and role in the Civil Rights movement. Who wrote J Know Why the Caged Bird Sings?
What is the greatest common factor for 14, 28, and 35?

One of these homophones appears in the titles of works about a scorpion's one, whereas the other appears in works about Genji and Two Cities. One of these terms refers to a character from the Sonic video game series, and the other is combined with the word "fairy" in a certain literary genre. Identify this homophone, which can refer to either a story, or a furry appendage that cats and dogs sometimes wag when excited.

Adult citizens have this obligation when summoned to do so. Doing it may require the citizen to be absent from work for a time. What civic duty is being performed when a citizen serves as a member of a group of people that decide an accused person's guilt or innocence?
This term describes a variety of ways in which water reaches the earth's surface. They might be liquid or temporarily solid. What do we call forms of water that include rain, snow, sleet and hail?
The "grosso" kind of this composition pairs a small group of soloists with a larger orchestra. Vivaldi's Four Seasons and Bach's Brandenburg are examples of what instrumental work?
Using the equation Y equals 8X, what is the value of X when Y equals 32?,

This vector quantity can be linear, translational, or angular. In a closed system not affected by external forces, this quantity is conserved. Explained in Newton's Second Law, what is the quantity defined as mass times velocity?

Under this plan of government, there was a legislature, but no executive branch and no judicial branch. Each state had one vote in Congress, and Congress did not have the power to tax. Identify this first governing document of the United States.
Two angles form a linear pair. One of the angles measures 115 degrees. What is the degree measure of the second angle?

This ballroom dance is slower than the quickstep, which it inspired. Done in 4/4 time, it uses side steps, walking steps, and quarter turns. What is this dance that combines an animal's name with a horse's gait between walking and running?
This element of a story is almost always surrounded by quotation marks. Give the word for a conversation between two or more characters.

Unlike memoirs, these written works are typically more comprehensive and fact-based. Famous ones were written by Nelson Mandela, Benjamin Franklin, and Malcolm X. Give this term for a story authors write of their own lives.
The recommended daily amount of milk is 3 cups. At lunch, a milk container is a half-pint. How many half-pints of milk would be equal to the recommended daily amount?

This composer's early operas included The Flying Dutchman and Tannhduser [TAHN-hoi-zur]. He based a series of four operas on a German legend about a magic golden object. Identify this composer of the Ring Cycle.
This river is a tributary of the Ohio River, and its mouth is at Catlettsburg, Kentucky. Name this river in eastern Kentucky, named for a certain substance found on beaches.

Unlike friction, this force increases as an object moves faster. Sports cars and airplanes are streamlined to minimize this force. What aerodynamic force tends to slow an object's forward motion through liquid or gas?

This state had more U.S. presidents born there than any other state. This state is one of four U.S. states that call themselves a commonwealth. Identify this state, home to the houses of former presidents like Jefferson and Washington.

In this type of circuit, the amount of current is different at different points. It is used anywhere it is vital to keep multiple devices working, even when one device burns out. What kind of circuit contains multiple pathways, or branches, with each device being on a separate branch?

This man starred in the ballets Agon and A Midsummer Night's Dream, which George Balanchine [BAL-un-sheen] choreographed for him. He was the first full-contract, full-time African-American dancer with the New York City Ballet. Who was this co-founder of the Dance Theatre of Harlem?
This giant-killing character encounters a magic harp and a hen that lays golden eggs after climbing a plant into the heavens. Give the name of this boy who traded a cow for some beans.
The population of a town has increased by 20% since last year. If the town's population last year was 10,000, what is the population of the town this year?

This member of the lute family descended from the dombra in the 18th century. Ranging in size from double bass to piccolo, it has three strings and a triangular body. Name this folk instrument from Central Asia and Russia.

This famous leader of the women's suffrage movement was arrested in 1872 for voting illegally. Four years later, she led a protest at the 1876 Centennial celebration, where she stated, "Men, their rights and nothing more; women, their rights, and nothing less." This planet gets its nickname because, to put it simply, its surface is rusty. If you could travel from the Sun toward the outer solar system, what planet would come next after Earth?

This performance technique can make it seem like music has been cut short and then started again. It changes a piece's regular metrical pattern. Identify this technique of stressing normally weak beats.

This membranous organelle, which consists of stacks of thin sacs, creates lysosomes. questions.a: GOLGI [GOAL-jee] APPARATUS (Accept GOLGI COMPLEX or GOLGI BODY)

These members of the class Anthozoa typically live in colonies of many polyps. They are in the same phylum as jellyfish and are often found along ocean coasts. Name these animals that collect in namesake reefs.

The term for this punctuation mark also refers to an aside made by a character to the audience or another third party. Rules for its use in punctuation are based on where letters are omitted or whether a word is singular or plural. Name this punctuation mark used to show possession and to create contractions.

When President Franklin Pierce signed this act into law, it repealed the Missouri Compromise and provided for the issue of slavery to be decided through popular sovereignty. Give the name of this act named for two U.S. states.
Anumber pattern starts with 97. The rule for the pattern is to subtract 12 to get the next term in the pattern. In this number pattern, what is the third number in the pattern?

This is the highest summit of the southern Front Range of the Rocky Mountains. It was named for. an American general and explorer whose first name was Zebulon. Name this mountain summit, which shares part of its name with an eastern Kentucky county.

This type of folk art is common in the Pennsylvania Dutch countryside. Many examples are murals of abstract moons, stars, and sunbursts. What are these barn decorations originally meant to ward off evil spirits?

This person served in the Crimean War, then founded a secular nursing school in London and revolutionized how nursing was taught. What nurse would check on patients at night, earning her the nickname "the lady with the lamp"?

This work from the last Impressionist exhibit inspired a critic to coin the term "Neo-Impressionism." It shows men, women, and children having a relaxing weekend on an island in the middle of the Seine. Give the name of this Pointillist painting by Georges Seurat [ZHAWRZH suh-RAH].
questions.a: (A) SUNDAY ON (THE ISLAND OF) LA GRANDE JATTE [GRAHND ZHAHT] (--1884)

questions.q: Young men who take part in this civic duty do not have to worry about serving, unless a large war breaks out. Name this responsibility that requires young men to serve in the military without being a volunteer.

questions.a: TO MEDITATE AFTER A STRESSFUL DAY

While these are sometimes contrasted with their Macintosh counterparts, Macs are technically in this group as well. Identify these devices, which are examples of hardware and are manufactured by ACIS, Dell, and HP.

The founder of this media organization was arrested in London in April 2019. He had sought asylum in the Ecuadoran Embassy in London. What is this organization founded by Julian Assange that has published thousands of private or classified documents?

While the independent kind of these are manipulated by the experimenter, the dependent kind are typically outcome measures. Identify these fundamental features of experiments, which could include quantities such as mass, sun exposure, growth in height, and IQ.

This graphic novel's protagonist, Jordan Banks, loves to draw cartoons. He encounters racism when his parents enroll him at the Riverdale Academy Day School. Identify this Newbery winner by Jerry Craft.
These numbers are types of real numbers. We use these numbers to count. What kind of numbers beginning with the letter "N" start with 1?

He led Kentucky's militia during the Battle of the Thames, an engagement of the War of 1812, which occurred while he served as Kentucky's fifth governor. Name this political leader who also served as Kentucky's first governor.

This piano style was sometimes called the "fast Western-style" or "Western rolling blues." Like ragtime before it, it was popular with honky-tonks, but its popularity declined after World War Two. Give the rhyming name for this music genre.

One example of this type of landform in the United States is Delmarva, where most of the state of Delaware sits. Other examples include upper and lower Michigan as well as Florida. Give the term for a piece of land that is surrounded by water on three of its sides.

questions.a: 30 TIMES 6 EQUALS X (ACCEPT: 6 TIMES 30 EQUALS X or X = 30 TIMES SIX)

This two-word measurement indicates atmospheric humidity. It is the temperature at which water vapor saturates the atmosphere. Give the term for the temperature at which water begins to condense from the air.

At his death in 1891, this artist's painting, The Circus, was unfinished. His first painting set at night was 1888's Circus Sideshow. Identify this man who co-founded Pointillism with Paul Signac [seen-YAHK].

Traditionally, men weave this cloth, and women sew the strips together. Once reserved for royalty and made of silk, it is now made of cotton and available to everyone. What is this brightly colored and patterned cloth native to Ghana?
Spelling required. Most herbs will freeze successfully. Spell the word from the preceding sentence, an antonym of "thaw."
There are two green balls, six red balls, one orange ball, and two yellow balls in a bag. If you choose a ball from the bag without looking, what is the probability that the ball will not be black?

This man was a naturalist on the HMS Beagle's expedition along South America's coasts. He scandalized Christians by suggesting that species gradually changed over hundreds of years. Who proposed evolution by natural selection in his book On the Origin of Species?

This member of the British royal family served as heir apparent for more than seven decades before he succeeded his mother, Queen Elizabeth the Second, to the throne in 2022. Give the name of this newly crowned British monarch.
This music element is a group of notes of different pitches played one after another. Identify this element that makes up a song's tune.

Despite being mortal, this novel's protagonist learns how to haunt people's dreams and make himself invisible. The Owenses raise Bod, who defeats the man Jack with the Sleer's help. A cemetery is the setting of which Neil Gaiman [GAY-mun] novel?
This question requires multiple answers. What four basic mathematical operations can be performed using real numbers?
This substance's states include plasma, gas, liquid, and solid. Everything in the universe, except for energy, consists of it. What is this substance made of atoms?

Kentucky's Knobs region roughly forms a horseshoe around this larger region, which includes the cities of Louisville and Lexington within it. Identify this region whose name references Kentucky's state nickname.
Happy Times Hotel has 14 floors with 20 rooms on each floor. If half of the rooms are reserved, how many rooms are left?

This book reassures readers that, despite automation, the title structure is "built to last forever." It follows the keeper's life as he marries, has a child, and saves a sunken ship's passengers from drowning. Identify this book, which earned a Caldecott Medal for Sophie Blackall.

In 2020, this sporting event was held in September, the first time since World War Two that it has not been held on the first Saturday in May. What sporting event, known as the "Run for the Roses," is held yearly at Churchill Downs?

This secular music style developed from enslaved people's praise songs, chants, and spirituals. The so-called Delta ones originated near the mouth of the Mississippi River. B. B. King performed what kind of music with repeating structures and sad lyrics?

Newton described this property in his First Law of Motion. It is an object's resistance to changing its velocity - that is, its speed and direction. Identify this tendency of an object to remain in motion or at rest unless acted on by an unbalanced force.

In this circuit type, the current amount differs at different points. Adding more light bulbs to this circuit won't cause any of the bulbs to dim. Name this kind of circuit that has a separate branch for each device.

This percussion instrument has curved corners, with one corner slightly open. Smaller ones are pitched higher than larger ones, but they all hang from a piece of leather or string. Identify this instrument named for the three-sided shape it resembles.
In this form of geographic measurement, the Equator is designated as 0 degrees. What measurement uses lines called parallels to describe the north-south position of a point on Earth?
One poem of this type is "The Mouse's Tale" from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland. Name this type of poem written in the shape of its subject.
A school day at Harper Elementary lasts 6 hours and 30 minutes. Convert this time to a mixed number of hours in reduced form.

This composer probably wrote Für Elise for one of his students, Therese. He titled his only opera, which premiered in 1805, Fidelio. Give this composer's name, whose Ninth Symphony contains the "Ode to Joy."

This author wrote of Louis, a mute bird, in The Trumpet of the Swan. His first children's book was inspired by a dream about a tiny boy who acted like a mouse. Give the name of the author of Stuart Little.
Paleontologists study these specific scientific remains. They may be true form, cast, trace, or mold. What are these remains of animals, plants, and other organisms often found in sedimentary rock?
Originating in Northern China, this language form is often called "Northern Chinese." Give the name for this form of Chinese, the country's most widely spoken.
A mosaic in the hallway has 6 red trapezoids for every 16 green triangles. What is the ratio of triangles to trapezoids?
questions.a: 8:3 (EIGHT TO THREE) (ACCEPT EIGHT OVER THREE OR EIGHT-THIRDS)

questions.q: This type of character usually fights against an antagonist. However, a character in this role doesn't have to be a so-called "good guy." What is this Greek-rooted name for a work's main character?

Though this settlement was burned by Native Americans in 1566, it was successfully relocated and remained the first permanently occupied European settlement in the New World. Give the name of this settlement, established in a coastal area of Florida by Spanish settlers.

This man's daughter Cosima married fellow composer Richard Wagner [RIKH-ahrt VAHG-nuhr]. He was a piano prodigy who composed Transcendental Etudes. Identify this Romantic Era composer of Hungarian Rhapsodies.
These clouds form from 13,000 to 66,000 feet above sea level. They form at high altitudes, usually before a weather change. Name these thin, wispy clouds made of ice crystals.
Give your answer as a decimal to the hundredth place. One thousand meters equals one kilometer. Convert 36,910 meters to kilometers.
This polygon can be drawn using a compass. What polygon contains 360 degrees around a central point?

This cryptid first gained widespread fame in 1933, thanks to an Inverness Courier article. Some believers argue it is a surviving plesiosaur [PLEE-see-uh-sawr], an extinct marine reptile. Identify this creature that supposedly inhabits a Scottish lake.

Multiple answers are required. The poet Ralph Waldo Emerson later referred to the shot that began these two battles as the "shot heard round the world." Give the name for the military engagements fought on April 19, 1775, which officially began the American Revolutionary War.

A 19th-century French acrobat created this costume, which gymnasts and circus performers originally wore. It eventually spread to ballet, where it transitioned from cotton to spandex. Identify this one-piece, skin-tight garment that covers the torso.

These celestial objects are also called planetoids. They are rocky bodies of metal and stone, and the largest examples are classified as dwarf planets. Name these objects that orbit the sun in a belt between Mars and Jupiter.

This part of a cell is found in archaea [ARK-ee-uh], bacteria, algae, fungi, and plant cells. Protozoans and animal cells don't have one. Give the name of this rigid structure that surrounds the cell membrane.

After being a soloist for the Kirov Ballet, this dancer defected to the West in 1961. After spending two decades with London's Royal Ballet, he was the Paris Opera Ballet's artistic director. Name this frequent duet partner of Dame Margot Fonteyn [MAR-go fawn-TAYN].

In his second inaugural address, this man called for unity and healing after the Civil War. He honored the Union soldiers who died at the Battle of Gettysburg two years earlier. Name this Kentucky-born man, the first U.S. president to be assassinated.

This warship was newly built when it took part in the first engagement between two ironclad warships at the Battle of Hampton Roads in March 1862. Give the name of the Union vessel which engaged in that influential naval battle with the rebuilt USS Merrimack.
Terry is buying a new carpet for her bedroom. Her room is 10 feet long and 12 feet wide. How many square feet of carpet will she need?

This musical is based on the memoir The Story of the Trapp Family Singers. Set in Austria, it follows Maria's transition from the nunnery to nannying 7 children. Name this final Rodgers and Hammerstein musical, whose songs include "Do-Re-Mi" and "My Favorite Things."
This Latin suffix can mean "process" or "act." Give this suffix that might follow "enjoy" or "state."
At the lunch counter, a customer can choose 4 different burgers, 3 salads, 2 desserts, and 2 drinks. A customer chooses only one item from the menu. How many possible choices does the customer have?

This vascular plant tissue consists of cells with rigid, thick walls. Its dead tissue forms hollow pipes that run from the roots through the stems and into the leaves. Name this tissue that transports water throughout a plant.

The Panic of 1873 occurred during the presidential administration of this man who had served as the U.S. Army's Commanding General during the American Civil War. What Union general would later become the United States' 18th president?
Spelled one way, this word names a part of the human foot. Spelled another way, it is a synonym of "mend." Give these words' shared pronunciation.

He served as Judge/Executive of Jefferson County, Kentucky, before he was elected a U.S. senator in 1984. Since 2021, he has served as the Senate's Minority Leader. Name Kentucky's senior U.S. senator.
Consider the expression 5x plus 3. What part of the expression is the variable?

Except for spiders and scorpions, almost all arthropods have these paired sensory appendages. Crustaceans have primary and secondary pairs on their first two head segments. Identify these jointed, movable appendages that help insects touch and smell the world.
Multiple answers are required. These 3 hues in art are the complementary colors of green, violet, and orange. State the three primary colors in the artist's color wheel.
Solve for S in the following equation. Twelve plus fifteen plus S equals forty. What is the value of S?

Along with the stabile [STAY-bile], Alexander Calder invented this type of art. It is a kinetic sculpture whose moving parts are driven by motors or wind. Identify this type of object that sometimes dangles above a baby's crib.
These respiratory organs are found in crustaceans, mollusks, and insects. Many amphibians and all fish also possess them. Identify this feathery tissue that allows aquatic animals to breathe.

The percentage of voters participating in this process is often called "turnout." What term refers to the formal process in which voters can cast their vote to accept or reject political propositions or select an individual to fill a public office?

Rarely, this punctuation mark can form the plurals of certain abbreviations, letters, or words. It can come before or after an S when forming a possessive. Identify this punctuation found in contractions.
Sally has $10.00 and wants to buy her mom four balloons. The balloons cost $2.25 each. How much money will she have left?

Subjects of the painting series by this artist included poplars, Rouen [roo-AN] Cathedral, and haystacks. He also painted the Japanese footbridge and the water lilies in his Giverny [zhee-vair-NEE] garden. Name the artist of Impression: Sunrise.

Its inventor is known by the pseudonym Satoshi Nakamoto. It is recognized by its logo featuring the capital letter B on an orange circle. Give the name for this most recognized and widely used form of cryptocurrency.
This soft, yellowish organ produces enzymes to help the body digest food. It also produces the hormones glucagon [GLOO-kuh-gon] and insulin. What is this organ whose malfunction can cause diabetes?
Identify the following sentence's indirect object: Bobby baked Benjamin a pan of brownies.
Identify the following sentence's noun clause: My mom encouraged me to remember who I was.

Despite its name, this scientific branch also studies plants, animals, and non-living things like sand and rocks. Seafloor geology, marine ecosystems, and current patterns are some of its focuses. Give the name for the study of Earth's saltwater bodies.

Baker Bob used 14 ounces of sugar to make cookies and 14 ounces to make brownies. Then he used 12 more ounces of sugar to make candy drops. As a mixed number, how many pounds of sugar did Baker Bob use?
A poster designed by J.M. Flagg helped popularize this character as a national symbol of patriotism. Name the character Flagg represented, pointing above the words, "I Want You For U.S. Army."

These folk art objects were originally carved using seashells, sharpened stones, bones, and beaver teeth. Six Pacific Northwest tribes traditionally made them for weddings, memorials, and myth remembrance. Identify these large wooden poles sculpted and painted to resemble animals.

This pastime first required an artist to remove a surface's imperfections with shark's skin or pumice. Then, he used a needle or pocket knife to carve a portrait or seascape. Name this art form in which sailors carved walrus tusks or whalebone.
Spelling required. The physical education teacher must gauge each student's activity level. Spell the word in the preceding sentence that means "to appraise, estimate, or judge."
A geometric sequence begins with 4, 16, 64. What is the next term in the sequence?

This inventor of one of the first smokeless powders combined guncotton and nitroglycerin to form blasting gelatin. He made his fortune by inventing dynamite. Identify this man who lent his name to global prizes for literature, economics, various sciences, and peace.

In 2018, the Supreme Court of this western U.S. state barred voters from deciding whether or not the state should be divided into three new states. What western U.S. state is the country's most populous?

This musical element consists of a piece's sequence of sounds and silences. It controls the length of time between a piece's accents--that is, its major beats. Give the name of this element, whose patterns can be clapped or tapped.

This novel begins in a Flint, Michigan, orphanage in 1936. The title boy leaves his foster home to search for the jazz musician Herman Calloway, who turns out to be his grandfather. Give the title of this Christopher Paul Curtis Newbery winner.
Adding a negative number to another number is the same as completing this basic operation. What operation is the same as adding negative four to positive five?

This mixture category includes aerosols, foams, emulsions, and gels. Examples include cream, fog, mayonnaise, and blood. Identify this mixture of two or more particles in which each substance retains its own properties.
This Kentucky city is home to the Muhammad Ali Center and Muhammed Ali International Airport. What city was the birthplace of Muhammad Ali and has Kentucky's largest population?
A basket of fruit costs $3.33. The store is selling the baskets for one-third off. How much will the baskets cost on sale?

In this picture book, a man takes the Number 5 bus to work each morning. When he wakes up with a cold, his zoo animal friends visit him at home. What is this Caldecott-winning collaboration of Philip C. and Erin E. Stead?

Led by their patriarch known as "Ole Ran’l," this Kentucky family is best remembered for their legendary feud with a family led by its patriarch known as "Devil Anse." Identify this Kentucky family, one half of a longstanding feud with the Hatfields of West Virginia.

Composers in this era loved polyphony [puh-LIF-uh-nee], a musical texture with multiple independent voices. The opera, cantata, and oratorio all developed during this period that lasted from about 1600 to 1750. Name this era, whose composers included Handel and J. S. Bach.
Free fall is a constant type of this physics vector. Newton's Second Law of Motion states it equals force divided by mass. Name this change in the rate of an object's velocity.
Be specific. This property is found in nickel, cobalt, and some rare-earth elements. Magnetite - sometimes called lodestone - and iron also have it. Name this strongest type of magnetism.

This instrument family's members can be pitched or unpitched. The maracas, steelpan, timpani, and cymbals all belong to it. Which family consists of instruments that can be struck, scraped, rubbed, or rattled?

This type of device typically contains a magnetic needle that aids navigation by aligning with the magnetic north pole. What do we call these instruments that typically display cardinal directions and are helpful when you're lost?

Two poems of this type are The Iliad and The Odyssey, both probably written by the ancient Greek Homer. They use heroic similes, typically beginning in the middle of the action, and often include gods and goddesses. Give the word for a long narrative poem about a hero's adventures.

Larry's math class ordered 2 and 1/2 pepperoni pizzas and 3 and 1/2 cheese pizzas. The pizza shop switched the orders, making 3 and 1/2 pepperoni pizzas and 2 and 1/2 cheese pizzas. How much less cheese pizza did they receive than they ordered?

This ballet's characters include the Bluebird and the Diamond and Lilac Fairies. At its conclusion, Prince Desiré weds Princess Aurora, whom he awakened with a kiss. Name this Tchaikovsky [chigh-KAWF-skee] ballet.

In this novel's opening scene, Thomas Small spends his 13th birthday moving to Ohio. His family helps Mr. Pluto and Mayhew trick the Darrows into abandoning the title man's treasure. This is the plot of which Virginia Hamilton novel?

Because this igneous rock fractures with sharp edges, ancient civilizations made cutting and piercing tools from it. It forms quickly from cooled lava that has minimal crystal growth. Identify this shiny black volcanic glass.

This term can follow the word "Pennsylvania" in a two-word name for a particular cultural group with German ancestry that settled in the state. What term most often refers to an individual of Germanic ethnic origin native to the Netherlands?
There are 23 sugar cookies and 15 chocolate chip cookies in a bowl. What is the ratio of sugar cookies to all the cookies?
questions.a: 23:38 (TWENTY-THREE TO THIRTY-EIGHT) (ACCEPT: TWENTY-THREE OVER THIRTY-EIGHT OR TWENTY-THREE THIRTY-EIGHTHS)

questions.q: When this story element is internal, it pits a character against him- or herself. External types include person versus nature, society, or person. Give the word for the struggle that drives a story's plot.

According to a famous story, this American upholsterer was responsible for convincing George Washington to use a 5-pointed star in the design of the American flag. Though her actual role has been questioned by historians, whose name is now synonymous with the creation of the first U.S. flag?
This type of folk dance is similar to tap dance. It evolved from the hornpipe, reel, and jig in England and Ireland. What is this dance that requires wooden shoes?

This atmospheric layer extends from 30 to 250 miles above Earth's surface. Like the mesosphere and thermosphere, it rests between the stratosphere and exosphere. Identify this region of electrically charged particles, which produces auroras and helps spread radio waves.
Jill's desktop measures 1,200 millimeters. How long is her desktop in centimeters?
This polygon contains four 90-degree angles. What polygon also has two pairs of opposite sides equal in length?

In one Aesop fable, this animal lies in a manger and prevents oxen from eating the hay there. In another, a wolf chooses freedom over this animal's life of a collar and chain. In yet another fable, which creature loses his bone while barking at his reflection in the water?

Born Araminta Ross, she was often called "Moses" by those she assisted on the Underground Railroad. Identify the influential American who escaped slavery herself before courageously leading hundreds of other enslaved people to their freedom.

In the "grand" one of these ballet movements, a dancer does a split in mid-air. The dancer throws her working leg forward while extending her supporting leg backward. Name this jump from one foot to the other.

This astronomer assisted Tycho Brahe and corresponded with Galileo about the telescope. His mathematical discoveries proved Copernicus's heliocentric theory. Who devised the three laws of planetary motion?

Like plastids, these organelles have their own DNA. They use cellular respiration to produce ATP and small amounts of carbon dioxide. What are these so-called "powerhouses of the cell" that produce energy?

This dancer studied at the American Ballet Theatre School under Merce Cunningham and Martha Graham. Mikhail Baryshnikov performed her choreography in the 1976 Push Comes to Shove premiere. Who is this choreographer of Deuce Coupe and Movin' Out?

This fairy tale ends with the title characters growing fat from grazing in a meadow. A troll threatens to eat each animal who passes over his bridge, but the largest animal eventually blinds and kills him. What is this fairy tale about a trio of livestock brothers?
He was a senator from Illinois before he was elected president by defeating John McCain in 2008. Name the United States' 44th president, for whom Joe Biden served as vice president.
A regular hexagon has sides of length 6 units. What is the perimeter in units of the hexagon?
