In Elizabethan times, this part of the stage got its name because it was tilted toward the ground. Which section of a proscenium stage is found closest to the audience?
In math, this Greek prefix can be found before "-gon." Identify this prefix meaning "many."

The card shop has 5 different birthday cards, 6 different get-well cards, and 2 all-occasion cards for sale. How many different combinations of cards, one from each category, can be made from the available card selection?

This word describes any vascular plant that reproduces using an ovule - that is, an exposed seed. Many of those seeds are in cones, meaning conifers belong to this group, along with ginkgos and cycads. Identify these opposites of angiosperms [AN-jee-oh-spermz].
This city, which last hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1984, will next host the games in 2028. Name this American city, the country's 2nd largest by population.
The first half of this compound word is what mammals use to nourish their young. The second half can be a verb meaning "tremble" or "jiggle." What is this compound word for an ice cream drink?

In the U.S. government, the holder of this office is second only to the president in authority over the U.S. military. What presidential cabinet member leads the executive department that oversees the U.S. Armed Forces?
The Fibonacci sequence is a special number pattern, with each number being the sum of the previous two numbers. What is the fifth term of a Fibonacci sequence that begins 0,1,1?
This invertebrate class is the largest in the phylum Mollusca [muh-LUS-kuh]. A few species, including conches and limpets, can be eaten. What is this class that also includes snails and slugs?

This artistic tool is usually wooden and comes in A-frame and H-frame varieties. Field ones are small and portable, while studio ones can support works weighing over 200 pounds. Identify this upright stand used to support a canvas.
A grocer placed 20 bags of apples on the display. He sold X bags of apples. In terms of X, how many bags of apples did he have left in the display?

During this period, artists branched out from religious work to depict ancient Greek and Roman subjects. Giotto and Donatello were two masters of its early period, while the so-called "High" part lasted from about 1475 to 1525. Name this era of rebirth during which Michelangelo and Leonardo also worked.

Be specific. This framework is found in sponges, starfish, and all vertebrates. It provides more structural support than the type invertebrates have. What is the word for bones that hold an animal from inside the body?

Also known as conscription, this process was last utilized in the United States during the Vietnam War. What term refers to how individuals may be selected to fill military vacancies, sometimes involuntarily?

In a series that already contains commas, this punctuation mark can separate the items in the series. More commonly, it comes between two independent clauses when they lack a coordinating conjunction. What is this punctuation that looks like a period vertically above a comma?
Juan had $312.00 in his savings account. He made two deposits of $5.00 each. How much money does he have in savings now?

This person was the only American-born artist to exhibit in Paris with the Impressionists. The Letter and The Child's Bath show the influence of Japanese prints. What is the name of this artist known for her portraits of mothers and children?

In economics, the law of this measurement states that as a product's price increases, fewer people will want to purchase that item. What is this economic measurement often discussed in terms of its relationship with a product's available supply?

Scientific name, please. This bone's head forms a ball-and-socket joint with the hip. At the other end, it connects to the knee. Identify this longest bone in the human body, informally called the thigh bone.
State the following sentence's appositive phrase: My favorite basketball team, the University of Kentucky, is not doing well this year.
Give the following sentence's adjective clause: People who are obedient follow the rules.

This branch of geophysics uses tools called geophones and hydrophones. Some of its scientists try to study volcanic interiors, while others locate gas and oil fields. Identify this science that studies artificial and natural vibrations, including earthquakes.
Haley was measuring angles with her protractor. One of the angles was 108 degrees. What type of angle is greater than 90 degrees and less than 180 degrees?

A poem closely associated with this sculpture states, "Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses." What sculpture, a gift given from France to the United States, can be seen raising its torch high above the harbor in New York City?

African instruments of this type include the bata, dundun, and djembe [JEM-bay]. Some tribes use the so-called "talking" kind to communicate over long distances. Name this percussion instrument whose membrane head the player strikes with a mallet or the hand.

This former Bizaardvark actress more recently portrayed Nini Salazar-Roberts on High School Musical: The Musical: The Series. Billboard's 2022 Woman of the Year, she embarked on the Sour Tour after releasing her debut studio album. Who is this singer-songwriter of "Deja Vu" and "Drivers License"?
Spelling required. It was ridiculous to excuse her suspicious behavior. Spell the word in the previous sentence that is a synonym of "absurd."

The academic coach was putting study materials into folders. He put 25 study sheets in the first folder, 31 sheets in the second folder, and 37 sheets in the third folder. How many sheets will he put in the fifth folder if he continues with this pattern?

This scientist established the New York Infirmary for Women and Children and, after moving back to England, the National Health Society. She studied at Geneva Medical College, opened a Women's Medical College, and was a professor at the London School of Medicine for Women. Name this first female doctor educated in the U.S.

Characters introduced in recent years on this long-running children's television program have included Lily, who has experienced homelessness, Julia, who is neurodivergent; and Ji-Young, the program's first Asian American Muppet. Name this television program that featured iconic characters such as Oscar the Grouch, Big Bird, and Elmo for decades.
This scale uses a pattern of whole, half, whole, whole, half, and whole steps. It usually gives the music a sad, serious quality. Name this opposite of a major scale.

In this novel, Mr. Spizz kills most of the title town's original residents to convince Miss Volker to marry him. Because 11-year-old Jack is grounded for the summer, he helps Miss Volker write obituaries for the local newspaper. Name this Newbery Medal-winning Jack Gantos novel.
Use the Distributive property to find the product. 3 times the quantity 6 plus 7 close quantity. What is the product?

In this state of matter, atoms diffuse to fill all the space in a container. It has a low density and can change directly into a solid through deposition. Name this state of matter, of which air is an example.

Kentucky's 425-mile-long shared border with this state differs from most of Kentucky's borders in that it is not created by a river boundary and is primarily a straight line. What state borders Kentucky to the south?
The school art show has 225 pictures on display. Twenty-five students entered pieces into the show. How many art pieces did each student enter if each student entered an equal number of pieces?

This book's text is a poem whose lines include, "Through the dark glows the moon" and "In that bird breathes a song..." It highlights yellow light sources both inside a home and in the nocturnal sky. Give the title of this Caldecott winner by Susan Marie Swanson.

Communities throughout Eastern Kentucky were devastated by this form of natural disaster in the summer of 2022. What is this type of natural disaster that involves typically dry land being submerged underwater, often due to vast amounts of rainfall or other extreme weather events?
This era's musicians favored program music - music that tells a story. It was a nationalistic period that focused on composers' emotions. Give the name of this era that spanned most of the 1800s.

This force is stronger in more massive objects than in less massive ones. It decreases with distance, and is why planets orbit around the sun and the moon orbits around Earth. Name this force that prevents you from floating off into space.
Any object that you can see does this to visible light. It occurs when light hits a surface and bounces off. What is this quality at which mirrors excel?
This instrument was once called the sackbut. Despite being classified as low brass, it has a higher range than the tuba. Name this instrument that changes pitch by using a U-shaped slide.

In geography, these divisions are created relative to the location on either side of the Equator or Prime Meridian. Give the term for any of the four examples of one half of Earth, typically referred to independently as northern, southern, eastern, and western.

This 19th-century poet wrote about a fictional Native American chief in The Song of Hiawatha. He also reimagined a colonial silversmith's midnight warnings from April 18, 1775. Who wrote "Paul Revere's Ride"?
Three bottles of dish soap held 3/8 liter, 1/2 liter, and 5/16 liter respectively. As a fraction, how many liters were in the three bottles?

This composer based The Marriage of Figaro on a sequel to The Barber of Seville. At the conclusion of his opera Don Giovanni, the title character is dragged down to Hell. Identify this Classical Era composer, whose final work was the unfinished Requiem.

In this novel, Kira moves into the Council Edifice to repair the Singer's robe. She refuses to leave with her blind father, Christopher, instead staying to weave her own vision for her community. Identify this second novel in Lois Lowry's Giver Quartet.
When this substance cools and hardens, igneous rock forms. Before it passes through a vent, it is called magma. Identify this molten rock that a volcano expels.

An important historical document was drafted and signed aboard this ship after it had crossed the Atlantic Ocean with a group of Puritan families in 1620. Give the name of the boat which brought the Plymouth Pilgrims to the New World.
Allison's class has 17 boys and 13 girls. What is the ratio of boys to girls in the class?
questions.a: 17:13 (SEVENTEEN TO THIRTEEN) (ACCEPT: SEVENTEEN OVER THIRTEEN OR SEVENTEEN-THIRTEENTHS)

questions.q: An example of this figure of speech is, "The moon smiled down on us." Which figure of speech gives human characteristics to animals, objects, or ideas?

This American Founding Father served as the first United States Minister to France and the first Postmaster General. Which of the Founding Fathers, known for publishing Poor Richard's Almanack, is often recognized today as the face on the $100 bill?
This Lindy Hop relative can be performed solo or with a partner. It features a walking step with the toes in and heels out. Identify this 1920s jazz dance named for a South Carolina port city.

In the Southern Hemisphere, this season lasts from late September to late December. In the Northern Hemisphere, it begins with the vernal equinox. Identify this season that falls between winter and summer.
Sharon ran 600,000 centimeters; Lisa ran 6,000 meters; and Thomas ran 6 kilometers. Which runner ran the farthest?
questions.a: ALL RAN THE SAME DISTANCE (ACCEPT SIMILAR RESPONSES)

questions.q: This quadrilateral has opposite angles of equal measure. What polygon also has two pairs of parallel sides?

The Himalayan black bear may have made this legendary creature's footprints. Like its North American counterpart, it is a large, hairy, apelike organism. What is this cryptid that supposedly lives at the snow line near Mount Everest?

In keeping with the name of this system, so-called "passengers" were led by "conductors" to various "stations" along their route to freedom. Give the two-word name for the secret network of routes used by enslaved individuals to escape to freedom in northern states.

Like Isadora Duncan, this dancer rejected graceful ballet steps, instead creating forceful, emotionally expressive moves. A student at the Denishawn School, she later formed her own modern dance company in New York City. Give the name of this choreographer of Appalachian Spring.
This planet's four Galilean moons are Callisto, Europa, Ganymede, and Io. It contains a storm, the Great Red Spot, that is twice as wide as Earth. Name this largest of our solar system's planets.
Certain antibiotics, like penicillin, come from organisms in this kingdom. Yeasts, truffles, mildew, and molds are all types of it. Identify this kingdom that also includes mushrooms.

This woman choreographed The Cobra, The Incense, and Radha after studying Hinduism. Her other works included Egypta and O-Mika. Identify this teacher of Martha Graham, who co-founded a dance school with her husband, Ted Shawn.
This nursery rhyme character calls for his pipe, bowl, and a trio of fiddlers. Name this fictional ruler, whom his rhyme characterizes as, quote, "a merry old soul."

A significant moment at the beginning of this event was "Black Thursday," a day in which the Wall Street stock market crashed to historic lows. Give the name for this long period of poor economic conditions, which affected much of the world from 1929 to 1939.
An isosceles triangle has two sides measuring 12 units and a third side measuring 10 units. What is the measure in units of the perimeter of the triangle?

This Meredith Willson musical is set in River City, Iowa. In it, Harold Hill stops conning people after falling in love with Marian, the librarian. In what musical does a children's band play the song "Seventy-Six Trombones"?
This word contains Greek roots meaning "one" and "ruler." It refers to a hereditary sovereign, usually a king or queen. Give this word that also names a butterfly species.
Your password combination must be three numbers. Each number must be chosen from the digits 0 to 9. How many combinations of numbers can you choose for your password?

This plant part can be fibrous or tap. It stores a plant's food, absorbs water and nutrients from the soil, and anchors it to the ground. Identify these plant parts that are typically hidden underground.

Among the individuals to hold this elected office as of January 2023 are Craig Greenberg in Louisville, Kentucky, and Linda Gorton in Lexington, Kentucky. What elected official generally holds the highest-ranking position within a city government?
As a verb, this word can mean "to be alertly on the lookout." As a noun, it names a timepiece worn on the wrist. What is the shared pronunciation of these homonyms?

Among the president's cabinet secretaries, this position is first in the line of presidential succession. The holder of this Cabinet position is responsible for representing the United States when meeting with leaders of foreign countries. What position is held, as of January 2023, by Antony Blinken?
The first three numbers in a sequence are 42, 48, and 54. What is the sixth term in the sequence?
This invertebrate with a central disk can regrow an appendage it loses. They move by using their tube feet, which resemble suction cups. Name these marine animals that can have from 5 to 50 arms.

Like rhythm, this principle of design shares its name with an element of music. It is similar to unity and counterbalances variety. Which principle stresses how separate but related parts of a piece work together?
Solve for X in this equation. 30 divided by X equals 6. What is the value of X?

This art form can create both two- and three-dimensional objects with geometric or organic forms. Some of its modern artists use tweezers, paper clips, and rulers in addition to their hands. What is this Japanese art of paper folding?

These mammals use echolocation to find insects to eat and also to avoid colliding with objects. They have large ears, fur ranging from gray to brown and black, and thin skin layers stretching from their arms to their legs. Name these nocturnal animals, the only true flying mammals.

Though it falls on April 18 in 2023, this day is typically observed in most years on April 15. Give the name for this sometimes-dreaded day of the year in which certain prepared reports must be submitted to the IRS.
How many words in the following sentence should be capitalized? My favorite book is The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe.
Mrs. Hanson planted sixty flowers in her garden. Of the flowers she planted, only three-fourths of them grew. How many flowers grew in Mrs. Hanson's garden?

Painted between May and June 1937, this large mural uses only black, white, and shades of grey. It was the centerpiece of Spain's pavilion at the Paris World's Fair. What was this critique of a Basque town's bombing, painted by Picasso?

Critics have recently accused Ticketmaster of possessing this type of leverage within the ticket sales market. Give the term for a market in which one company has little to no competition, a name shared with a popular board game.

It's not the nose, but some vertebrates use this organ to collect scents in the air. Others use it to clean themselves or to catch insects and other small animals to eat. Name this organ that, in humans, contains some of the taste buds.
What is the following sentence's simple predicate? The class will go on a field trip to the zoo.
What is the following sentence's gerund phrase? Everyone in my family loves playing chess.

This scientific tool's two main categories are refracting and reflecting. Galileo used one for astronomy. Name this optical instrument for making distant objects, such as stars and planets, appear larger and closer.
This geometric shape has 12 angles. It also has 12 vertices. What regular polygon has 12 sides?

Built from 1930 to 1931, this building was the world's tallest for nearly four decades. Today, it remains one of the most recognizable buildings on the skyline of New York City. Give the name of this iconic skyscraper, a name that references the state nickname of New York.

This plant was a staple of colonial Florida's, Georgia's, and South Carolina's economies. It was used in cosmetics and wound cleaning but mainly as a blue dye for textiles. What is this crop that shares its name with a color of the rainbow?

This singer competed alone on UK's X Factor before being brought back to join a boy band. During that band's hiatus, he released three solo albums, including 2019's Fine Line. Identify this former One Direction member, whose singles include "Adore You" and "Watermelon Sugar."
Spelling required. Last December, my cousin was a contestant on Jeopardy! Spell the word in the preceding sentence that is a synonym of "competitor."
The square root of X equals 10. What is the value of X?

This scientist used a prism to discover that white light is actually a mixture of colors. He explained forces' effects on objects in his Three Laws of Motion. Name this man who also developed the Law of Universal Gravitation.

In a Tweet posted in March 2022, he said, "my place is still on the field and not in the stands." His Tweet read, "I'm coming back for my 23rd season in Tampa." Which longtime NFL Quarterback retired in early 2022, only to unretire a few weeks later?
Italian name, please. This musical symbol means a note should be held longer than usual. It consists of a dot with a downward curving arc above it. Identify this symbol nicknamed a "birdseye."

Set during the Great Depression, this novel consists of 110 free verse poems. Its protagonist, Billie Jo Kelby, reconciles with her father after the accidental deaths of her mother and baby brother. What is this Newbery-winning novel by Karen Hesse [HESS]?
An equation is stated as 28 + 0 = 28. What property of addition is illustrated by the previous equation?
Examples of this change include mixing sand with water, shredding paper, and chopping wood. What kind of change affects a substance's form but not what makes up the substance?

Extending from southern Florida to Michigan near the Canadian border, this north-south interstate passes through the Kentucky cities of London, Richmond, and Lexington before continuing north into Cincinnati, Ohio. Identify this interstate, the second longest north-south interstate in the U.S.
The storage closet contains 10 boxes of 7 erasers each. How many erasers will be left over if 8 boxes of erasers are used?

This wordless picture book begins and ends with a child finding a camera at the beach. The camera's photos show the animals, plants, and cities that exist under the waves. Name this book, which earned David Wiesner [WEEZ-nur] his third Caldecott Medal.

During the American Civil War, this state was the birthplace of both the president of the Confederate States and the president of the United States. What state was the birthplace of both Jefferson Davis and Abraham Lincoln?

Originally, this word applied to any musical piece played and not sung. Eventually, it referred to a multi-movement work for one or two instruments. Identify this kind of piece, one which Beethoven nicknamed "Moonlight."
This simple machine is the part of a flagpole that raises and lowers the flag. Give the name of a wheel and rope that can change a force's direction.
This quantity measures the average kinetic energy of a substance's particles. It increases as the particles move at higher rates. Identify this measure of an object's warmth or coolness.

Despite the name, instruments in this family can also be made of metal or plastic. Some require one or two reeds, while others don't need any. Give the name of this family that includes the clarinet and flute.

In geography, this term refers to a large geographical region typically consisting of a large landmass or a significant portion of a vast landmass. Give the term for these regions, of which Africa, Europe, and Asia are examples.
It's not the haiku, but this poem shares similarities with the Japanese tanka. Identify this poetic form, whose 5 lines consist of 2, 4, 6, 8, and 2 syllables.
Leo ran 2 and 2/7 miles on Monday and 3 and 1/49 miles on Tuesday. How much farther did he run on Tuesday than on Monday?

One of this opera's title characters is a disabled street beggar. The other title character, his love interest, is dating Crown and buying drugs from Sportin' Life. Charleston's Catfish Row is the setting for what work by Dubose Heyward, George, and Ira Gershwin?

This author wrote of Cedric Errol's unexpected inheritance in Little Lord Fauntleroy. A similar windfall happens to Sara Crewe in her novel A Little Princess. Name this creator of Mary Lennox in The Secret Garden.
Unlike erosion, this natural process occurs in one place. It can be biological, chemical, or mechanical. What is this breaking down of exposed rock?

From 1616 to 1699, this settlement within the Colony of Virginia served as the capital of colonial America. What English settlement is recognized as the first permanent English settlement in the New World?
Coco had eight pups, and three were white. Four of the pups were black, and the rest were brown. What is the ratio of brown puppies to the total number of Coco's pups?
questions.a: 1:8 (ONE TO EIGHT) (ACCEPT ONE OVER EIGHT OR ONE-EIGHTH)

questions.q: This sound device is a staple of comics. Examples include "pow," "boom," and "whoosh." Identify these words that resemble the sounds they represent.

This historical event, which occurred on December 16, 1773, was an act of protest organized by the Sons of Liberty. Give the name of this event where participants protested "taxation without representation" by dumping shipments of a specific good into a harbor.
One legend says the goddess Pele first performed this dance to celebrate her escape from her sister. It uses arm and hip movements to describe a place or tell a story. Name this Hawaiian folk dance.

Many of these weather phenomena form from cumulonimbus [kyoom-yoo-loh-NIM-bus] clouds. It features Earth's strongest winds, reaching up to 300 miles per hour. What is this rotating column of air that reaches from a cloud to the ground?
George has 128 ounces of water in a container. He wants to fill 1/8 gallon water bottles. How many water bottles will he be able to fill?
This geometric shape contains 180 degrees. It is one-half of a circle. What geometric shape looks like a slice of an orange?

In this fable, a runaway slave removes a thorn from a large cat's paw. Later, that animal refuses to eat him in a Roman arena. Name this Aesop fable that teaches, quote, "Gratitude is the sign of a noble soul."

Delivered at the dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery on November 19, 1863, this brief speech began with the words "Four score and seven years ago." Give the name of this iconic speech delivered during the American Civil War by President Abraham Lincoln.

This musician incorporated kicks, toe stands, and an anti-gravity lean into his performances. His signature move was a popping step in which he traveled backward while appearing to move forward. Identify this late "King of Pop," the perfecter of the moonwalk.
This subject of the Mariner and Messenger spacecrafts orbits the sun in 88 Earth days. It has no moons and is less than half Earth's size. Identify the closest planet to our sun.

These unicellular organisms can be shaped like rods, spheres, or spirals. Many reproduce through binary fission and can be killed by antibiotics. Give the name of these microscopic organisms that cause illnesses like strep throat.

This musical is based on a 1920s comic strip created by Harold Gray. Among its characters are Miss Hannigan, wealthy Daddy Warbucks, and Sandy, the dog. Name this musical, whose red-headed protagonist sings about the sun coming out tomorrow.

This man delivered his best-known speech to Williamsburg's Peyton Randolph, president of the Second Virginia Convention. In it, he urged the colony to raise and establish a militia to fight in the American Revolution. Identify this man who ended his speech, "Give me liberty, or give me death!"

This war has been referred to as the "Great War" and the "War to End All Wars." In 1917, the United States joined what global military conflict that concluded a year later with a victory by the Allies?
Mr. Rogers is covering his flower bed with mulch one inch thick. The flower bed measures 60 inches long and 5 inches wide. How many cubic inches of mulch will he need to cover the flower bed?
Another name for this set-up is the theater in the round. It often features tiered seating in a large auditorium. Give the word for a stage that the audience surrounds on all sides.
This word is sometimes a synonym of "commonplace." It contains the Latin root for "foot." What is this word for someone who walks?
A spinner is divided into 12 equal sectors. Each sector is a different color. What is the probability of spinning a specific color in a single spin?
This plant part causes hay fever in people allergic to it. A plant's stamens form these grains, which contain sperm cells. Name these tiny yellow spores that fertilize a plant's egg cells.

First and last names are required. From 2016 to 2019, he served as Attorney General of Kentucky. Name this politician who defeated Governor Matt Bevin in an election in 2019, becoming the sixty-third governor of Kentucky.
The first part of this compound word is a natural substance that can be petrified. The second part is a nickname for "Charles." Identify this other name for a groundhog.

This amendment to the U.S. Constitution includes a Self-Incrimination Clause which protects an individual's right to decline to answer questions that could be used to make them appear guilty of a crime. Individuals, who refuse to answer such questions typically "plead" which amendment to the U.S. Constitution?
A number pattern is formed by subtracting 3 from the previous number. The first term of this pattern is 100. What is the seventh term of the pattern?

These insects are related to both wasps and ants. They feed on nectar and pollen and live in either large colonies or small hives. Identify these black and yellow insects that, in some cases, make wax and honey.
This word applies to shapes with a curving, flowing appearance. They are often asymmetrical and based on shapes found in nature. State this opposite of geometric shapes.
Solve for X in this equation. X equals Y minus 2 when Y equals 10. What is the value of X?
Paintings in this genre include Frederic Edwin Church's The Icebergs and Winslow Homer's The Gulf Stream. Give the word for a painting of the ocean.

In rare cases, the Bengal one of these mammals may have white fur. The Sumatran, Malayan, Indochinese, and Siberian species are all endangered. Identify this large cat with orange fur and black stripes.

The Fifth amendment to the U.S. Constitution states that without this two-word term, one shall not be "deprived of life, liberty, or property." Give the two-word term which refers to a citizen's right to be treated fairly and lawfully in legal matters.

This punctuation mark can divide a word at the end of a line of text. It also separates parts of compound words like "merry-go-round" and "sister-in-law." Give the name of this punctuation mark, which is sometimes confused with the dash.
The local fruit stand sold 6 bags of apples on Monday. On Tuesday, it sold five-sixths as many bags. How many bags of apples did the fruit stand sell on Monday and Tuesday combined?

Because the artist used oil-based paints on plaster, this mural has been restored numerous times since its 1498 completion. It decorates a wall in a convent in Milan, Italy. Identify this depiction of Jesus's final meal with his disciples, painted by Leonardo da Vinci.
Gutzon Borglum is best remembered for designing this massive sculpture within the Black Hills of South Dakota. Name this national memorial that features the carved faces of four U.S. presidents.

Cirrhosis scars this organ, which hepatitis can also damage. As the body's largest and heaviest internal organ, it breaks down toxins and stores sugars, vitamins, and minerals. What is this organ that produces bile to help digest fats?

This part of speech accounts for the English language's most common word. It contains only three words, with two being indefinite and one being definite. Give the part of speech of "a," "an," and "the."
An example of this sentence structure is, "Wherever you go, you can always find hope." What kind of sentence consists of one independent clause and at least one dependent clause?

Like airplanes, this type of craft moves by jet propulsion. However, it carries its oxygen supply, which means it can work in space. Give the name of this device that can launch missiles, fireworks, and spacecraft.
The radius of a circle is 15 centimeters. What is the diameter of the circle in centimeters?

Rooms within this residence include the East Room, the Treaty Room, Lincoln Bedroom, and the Oval Office. Give the name of the presidential residence located at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington, D.C.

In Eastern Woodlands music, this technique happens when a leader sings a short melody that dancers echo in unison. Its African origins made this style a staple of early American gospel music. Identify this compositional style that resembles a conversation.
questions.a: CALL AND RESPONSE (Accept CALL AND ANSWER)

questions.q: This seven-time men's World Player of the Year moved to Barcelona at age 13. Since 2021, he has played professionally for the Paris Saint-Germain F. C. Name this soccer star who led Argentina's national team to the 2022 World Cup championship.
Spelling required. The student's grades made him ineligible to participate in extracurriculars. Spell the word from the previous sentence that is a synonym of "disqualified."
The temperature was 32 degrees. By noon it increased by X degrees. What is the value of X if it was 50 degrees at noon?
This man received a Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect. He also developed the special theory of relativity. Which scientist's name is now a nickname for any very smart person?

Initially becoming popular in the American Pacific Northwest, this athletic activity skyrocketed during the COVID-19 pandemic and has recently been described as the United States’ fastest-growing sport. Give the somewhat unusual name of this racket sport, often described as combining badminton, ping-pong, and tennis.

This element of music increases when a player or singer sees "accelerando" [aht-chel-uh-RAHN-doh] and decreases when they see "ritardando" [ree-tar-DAHN-doh]. Largo, allegro, and presto are all words related to it. Give the term for how fast or slow a piece of music is performed.

This novel's title refers to Luna, whom Xan [ZAN], the witch rescued as a baby. As Luna's magic powers grow near her 13th birthday, Xan nears her own death. What is this Newbery Medal-winning Kelly Barnhill novel?
This question requires two answers in the correct order. Both addition and multiplication have identity elements. What are the identity elements for addition and multiplication?
questions.a: ZERO, ONE (MUST BE IN THIS ORDER)

questions.q: Like the Kelvin scale, this temperature scale uses SI metric measurements. A Swedish astronomer devised it, but he reversed water's boiling and freezing points as we know them today. Identify this scale at which water boils at 100 degrees and freezes at 0 degrees.

A museum dedicated to this iconic businessman is located in Corbin, Kentucky, at the site of a café where he developed his world-renowned "secret recipe" for fried chicken. Name the founder of Kentucky Fried Chicken.
At the football game, 7.5 rows of bleachers were filled. Six fans can sit in each complete row. How many fans attended the football game?

This Caldecott-winning picture book is based on a Brothers Grimm fairy tale. In it, Paul O. Zelinsky describes the title character's birth, childhood, and imprisonment by a witch. Identify this book about a prince who rescues a young woman from a tower by climbing her long hair.

Two U.S. vice presidents, Richard M. Johnson and John C. Breckinridge, both graduated from this school, the first university opened west of the Allegheny Mountains. Identify this university established in 1780 and located in Lexington, Kentucky.
Two-word answer, please. This element of music is why instruments and voices each have unique sounds. What is this element, also called tone color?

This simple machine comes in three classes based on the position of its fulcrum, load, and effort. Crowbars and seesaws are examples of this simple machine that uses a rigid bar that pivots around a point. What is this simple machine?

These waves are the longest in the electromagnetic spectrum. Radar uses them, as do communication and broadcasting satellites, cell phones, and computers. What are these waves with AM and FM varieties your car's antenna can detect?
This musical piece has an Italian name that means "playing together" or "agreeing." An example is The Four Seasons by Antonio Vivaldi. What do we call this music piece for a soloist and an orchestra?

An example of this map feature might indicate that every centimeter on the map is equivalent to 10 kilometers of real space. What feature of a map details how distance on the map corresponds to distance in the physical world?

This poet once compared hope to, quote, "the thing with feathers-- / That perches in the soul--" The speaker celebrates anonymity in her poem "I'm Nobody! Who are you?" Identify this reclusive 19th-century poet nicknamed "The Belle of Amherst."
One liter of water equals approximately 33.8 ounces. How many liters of water are equivalent to 135.2 ounces?

This instrument's greatest living player is probably Yo-Yo Ma. It is the lowest-pitched member of the standard string quartet. Identify this string instrument that is larger than a viola but smaller than a double bass.

This author wrote about an orphaned girl in Eight Cousins and its sequel Rose in Bloom. Her masterpiece was initially published in two parts, with the second half being called Good Wives. Who wrote Little Women?

Scientists characterize this part of the ground as the O horizon. It can be an inch thick and contains microorganisms and organic matter called humus [HYOO-mus]. Give the name for this uppermost layer of soil.

It became the second permanent English colony in the New World and the first permanent English colony in New England when it was settled in 1620. Name this colony originally settled by separatists brought to the New World aboard the Mayflower.
A quilt pattern contains fourteen pink squares and eighteen purple squares. What is the ratio of purple squares to pink squares?
questions.a: 9:7 (NINE TO SEVEN) (ACCEPT: NINE OVER SEVEN OR NINE-SEVENTHS)

questions.q: This broad literary category includes encyclopedia entries, movie reviews, and histories. Newspaper articles, travel guides, and biographies also fall under this heading. What is this type of prose that deals with facts and reality?
Because this state ratified the U.S. Constitution five days before Pennsylvania in 1787, it is known as the "First State." Name the first state admitted to the Union, which has its capital at Dover.

This ballet's five segments include "Buckaroo Holiday" and "Hoe-Down." Set at Burnt Ranch, it follows a cowgirl's attempts to woo the head wrangler. Give the one-word title of this Aaron Copland work.
Sometimes, this word is used interchangeably with "glaze" to refer to clear ice on objects. Other times, it names a mixture of snow and rain. Name these ice pellets that are smaller than hail.
Janice rides her bike 2,000 meters to school and back daily. How many kilometers does she ride in five days?
Stop signs are examples of this geometric shape. It has eight angles and eight vertices. What geometric shape contains eight sides?

This tall tale man created the Grand Canyon by dragging his axe behind him. Other stories tell how he built the Big Rock Candy Mountain and created the Great Lakes as watering holes for his pet. Name this lumberjack owner of Babe, the Blue Ox.

In December 1860, this southern state became the first to secede from the Union. Identify this state, which in April 1861, was the site of the Battle of Fort Sumter and the official beginning of the American Civil War.
This element of dance controls a dancer's focus and pathway. It also determines the level, size, and direction of movements. Identify this element, which can be general or personal.

This planet's largest moon, Titan, is the only moon in the solar system confirmed to have clouds. The Cassini spacecraft sampled the atmosphere of this second-largest planet in our solar system. Give the name of this gas giant known for its rings.

This acid is shaped like a double helix, resembling a twisting ladder. It is made of genes and stored in chromosomes in a cell's nucleus. Name this complex molecule that determines an organism's physical traits.

This performer began her career on Broadway in Top Speed and Girl Crazy. She soon moved to Hollywood, where she co-starred in Flying Down to Rio and Top Hat. Who was this frequent onscreen co-star of Fred Astaire?

This nursery rhyme's title contains a phrase meaning, quote, "a disfavored or disreputable member of a group." In it, the title animal claims he has three bags of wool for his master, his dame, and the little boy who lives down the lane. Identify this rhyme about a dark-colored lamb.

In one famous story concerning this American city, a cow belonging to resident Mrs. O'Leary was responsible for starting the "Great Fire" that destroyed many of its buildings and homes in 1871. Name this city in Illinois, today America's third largest by population.
To find the volume of a rectangular prism, you must know three measurements. Besides length and width, what other measurement must you know?

To date, this is the highest-grossing Broadway musical, having earned over $1.6 billion. It mixes live performers with puppets in numbers like "Can You Feel the Love Tonight" and "The Circle of Life." What is this musical about Timon, Pumbaa, Nala, and Simba?
As a prefix, it can precede "time," "flow," or "come." It is an Anglo-Saxon prefix meaning "above" or "too much." What is this antonym of "under"?
The probability of getting heads or tails is 1/2 when flipping a quarter. What is the probability of getting heads after 100 flips of the coin?

This part of a plant contains stomata [sto-MAH-tuh], pores that open and close to exchange gases with the atmosphere. Deciduous plants shed them, while evergreens keep them all year long. Identify this thin, flat plant organ that houses chlorophyll for photosynthesis.

Kevin McCarthy took over this federal government role in January 2023, succeeding Nancy Pelosi. The holder of what congressional leadership position is second in the U.S. presidential line of succession?
questions.a: SPEAKER OF THE (UNITED STATES) HOUSE (OF REPRESENTATIVES)

questions.q: As a noun, this word is a synonym of "type" or "variety." Give this word that, as an adjective, is a synonym of "nice."

While President Ulysses S. Grant signed the law officially designated it a federal holiday, Abraham Lincoln chose for the day to be observed on a Thursday in November. Give the name of this national holiday often associated with the Plymouth Pilgrims.
The first four numbers of a number pattern are 69, 58, 47, and 36. What is the rule for finding the next number in the pattern?

Insects of this type have hard forewings that cover their thin, membranous flight wings. They make up about 1/4 of Earth's known animal species. What is this category that includes weevils, scarabs, and ladybugs?
This type of line implies that a landscape continues beyond an artwork's edges. It can suggest relaxation and rest. What is this counterpart of the vertical and diagonal lines?
Use the equation Y equals X plus 45. What is the value of Y when X equals 45?

Also called poster paint, this substance can form a base for pastels, crayons, or watercolors. It dries quickly and is made of pigment, gum arabic, and additives like chalk. What is the French word for this opaque watercolor?

The ladybug fits into this dietary category because it feeds on aphids. Snakes, sharks, and large and small cats are also part of it. Give the word for an animal that primarily or exclusively eats meat.

Abraham Lincoln issued a proclamation officially known as Proclamation 95 issuing this form of freedom on January 1, 1863. Give the term beginning with "E," which refers to freeing an individual or group from previous social, legal, or political restraint.
How many words should be capitalized in the following sentence? I have playdates every Saturday and Sunday in June.
There are 32 students in the math class. 25% of the students were absent. How many students were absent?

This painting technique has a name meaning "light-dark" in Italian. Caravaggio [kar-uh-VAH-jee-oh], Rembrandt, and Leonardo da Vinci all mastered it. Identify this art technique that arranges light and shadow to define three-dimensional objects.

A portion of Leviticus 25:10 is cast into the metal comprising this American symbol once located in the steeple of Independence Hall in Philadelphia. Give the popular name for this physical American Independence symbol most easily recognized by a large crack on its surface.

These particles are made of nucleic acid surrounded by protein. Fevers can kill them, antibodies attack them, and vaccines sometimes prevent them from infecting people. Name these particles that cause the flu, the common cold, and COVID.
Give the following sentence's complete predicate: The basketball team's injured player scored the winning basket.
How many prepositional phrases appear in the following sentence? From what she said, she aced the test without trying.

This scientific tool's first wide-scale use was in supermarket checkouts. Some printers use them, and they sometimes replace knives and scalpels in surgeries. Identify this focused beam of light that escapes from a tube.
One side of a stop sign measures 10 units. What is the perimeter of the stop sign in units?

First and last names are required. Following a third-round loss at the 2022 U.S. Open, this 23-time Grand Slam champion confirmed her plans to step away from competitive tennis. Name this champion athlete who rose to the top of women's tennis alongside her sister, Venus.

Unlike other Impressionists, this artist rejected that label and painted in a studio rather than outdoors. He set some of his paintings at racetracks and cafes, but over half of his works depict ballerinas. Who sculpted Little Dancer of Fourteen Years?
This musical rest is a black box placed under the staff's fourth line. In 4/4 time, which rest is worth 4 beats?
These whole numbers are not divisible by two. Adding 57 and 32 will equal this type of number. What type of whole numbers are 29 and 97?

In this novel, deaf Valencia narrates her portions from a first-person perspective. An omniscient [ahm-NISH-unt] narrator speaks for bully Chet, shy Virgil, and psychic Kaori. Identify this Newbery Medal-winning novel by Erin Entrada Kelly.

A national recreation area lying between this lake and Kentucky Lake is known as Land Between the Lakes. Name this lake which extends from Livingston, Lyon, and Trigg counties in Kentucky into Middle Tennessee.
This type of substance is either ionic or covalent. It occurs when two or more elements are chemically joined. Water and table salt are examples of what?
Cameron needs 750 beads to make 50 necklaces for the craft fair. Each necklace will have the same number of beads. How many beads will be in each necklace?

This book earned its author-illustrator the second of his three Caldecott Medals. Its title characters rescue dragons from being slain and lure the cat and the fiddle out of their nursery rhyme. In which David Wiesner [WEEZ-ner] book does the trio of protagonists outsmart the Big Bad Wolf?

A Kentucky parkway once known as Daniel Boone Parkway was renamed for this congressman who began serving his 22nd term in congress in 2023. Identify this congressman who, as of 2022, is the longest serving member of the U.S. House of Representatives for Kentucky.
This rhythmic choice is vital to jazz, ragtime, and reggae music. Identify this technique of shifting a piece's normal accent to typically unaccented beats.

Sometimes, this simple machine works like a lever by multiplying force. Part of it consists of a cylindrical drum with ropes applied to it. Identify this simple machine, whose examples include a door knob and car tires.

Full name, please. The human skin uses this type of radiation to produce Vitamin D. However, too much of it can cause a sunburn and, in some cases, skin cancer. What are these rays, whose name is abbreviated to UV?

This first modern jazz form rose to popularity in the mid-1940s. It featured fast, improvised chords and took its name from syllables used in scat singing. Name this style pioneered by Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker.

One well-known example of this type of island is named Castaway, a popular cruise line stop owned by the Walt Disney company. Give the name for a type of tiny, sandy island that forms upon a coral reef.

This author-illustrator's early books include And to Think That I Saw It on Mulberry Street and The 500 Hats of Bartholomew Cubbins. He later created the Lorax, Yertle the Turtle, and Horton the Elephant. Name this creator of The Cat in the Hat.
There are 12 forks in the drawer and 1/6 of the forks are plastic and the rest are metal. How many metal forks are there in the drawer?

This woodwind has a curved bocal [BO-call] and a pear-shaped bell. Despite its name, it probably didn't originate in Great Britain. What is this double reed woodwind that plays a fifth lower than the oboe?

As this novel opens, the title characters await their chaplain father's return home from the Civil War. By the book's end, one of the sisters has died, while the other three have grown and married. Name this story of Meg, Jo, Beth, and Amy by Louisa May Alcott.

This hollow mineral body is found in limestone and certain shales. It has a chalcedony [kal-SED-uh-nee] layer and forms when a fluid-filled cavity expands. What is this rock filled with colorful crystals?

In terms of generational populations, individuals considered part of this generation are second only to millennials in terms of total numbers. Give the name for the generation of Americans, born between approximately 1946 and 1964, who were born amid a significant increase in births following World War Two.
Caesar's Pizzeria sells fifteen cheese pizzas to every three pepperoni pizzas. On Super Bowl Sunday, they sold 30 pepperoni pizzas. How many cheese pizzas did they sell?
This literary technique is essential to allegory. Name this technique in which a word, image, character, or other literary element represents a larger idea.

The name of this state capital comes from a French explorer who named it after a red stick he found on its lands. The French translation of “red stick” provides the name for what capital of a southern U.S. state?

A chorale from one of this man's cantatas inspired the hymn "Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring." Four of his six sons, including Carl Philipp Emanuel and Johann Christian, also became composers. Which Baroque composer wrote The Well-Tempered Clavier [kluh-VEER]?
This type of two-word weather event has winds that range from 39 to 73 miles per hour. Name this kind of cyclone that has less than hurricane force winds.
Harry prepared six gallons of his famous chili for the Chili Cook-off. He divided the chili into quart containers. How many quarts of chili did Harry make?
One inch equals 2.54 centimeters. How many inches are equal to 7.62 centimeters?

In this fable, a young shepherd devises a new way to amuse himself. Because he deceives local villagers on several occasions, they refuse to help him when a real predator attacks his flock. Which Aesop fable illustrates that, quote, "Nobody believes a liar, even when he tells the truth"?

Despite being the last of the original 13 colonies, it became the fourth state added to the Union. James Oglethorpe founded this colony in hopes it could become home to individuals who had been imprisoned in England for owing debt. Name this Southern colony.

Like second position, this ballet step has an en l'air [AHN LAIR] equivalent. The dancer turns both feet out and divides her weight equally between them. In which position does one foot rest approximately 12 inches in front of the other?

Twelve of these astronomical groupings lie in a band called the zodiac. Other non-zodiac groupings include Orion and Ursa Major. Give the word for these 88 star clusters that resemble people, objects, or animals from mythology.

These organelles are much larger in plant cells than in animal cells. They are lined with a membrane and filled with fluid rather than cytoplasm. Name these cellular bubbles that store nutrients and waste.

This ballet dancer retired at age 29 after a schizophrenic breakdown. He could perform en pointe and starred in Petrushka [puh-TROOSH-kuh] and The Firebird for the Ballets Russes [bal-EY ROOS]. Who also choreographed The Afternoon of a Faun and The Rite of Spring?

This nursery rhyme's last stanza includes the lines, quote, "Then the traveler in the dark / Thanks you for your tiny spark..." Its better-known first verse describes the title body as, quote, "Up above the world so high, / Like a diamond in the sky." Name this rhyme about an object you see when the night sky is cloudless.

Multiple answers required. The poet Ralph Waldo Emerson later referred to the shot that began these two battles as the “shot heard round the world”. Give the name for the military engagements fought on April 19, 1775 which officially began the American Revolutionary War.
Two ninety-degree angles are defined by this term. Also two angles with measures of 80 degrees and 100 degrees are classified as these angles. What is any pair of angles with a sum of 180 degrees?

Before this theater burned in 1613, it could house about 3,000 people in its yard and galleries. A replica opened in 1997 on the Banks of the Thames [TEMZ] in London. What was this theater where many of Shakespeare's plays premiered?
This Latin prefix can mean either "not" or "opposite of." What is this prefix that might come before "trust," "like," or "honest"?
A cube measures 2 units on each side. What is the volume of the cube in cubic units?
This part of a flower consists of one or more carpels. Its individual sections are the stigma, style, and ovary. Give the name for a flower's female reproductive organ.

This transaction, totaling about $15 million, was authorized by the administration of President Thomas Jefferson in 1803. Give the two-word name for this transaction in which the United States acquired more than 800,000 square miles of additional land from France.

The first half of this compound word means, quote, "a round frame that turns on the axle." The second half of the word is a piece of furniture you can sit on. What is this compound word for a mobility aid for people who can't walk?

President Lyndon B. Johnson was aboard an aircraft known by this name when he was sworn into office in Dallas, Texas in 1963. Give the three-word name for an airplane used to fly the president of the United States.
You toss a fair coin exactly three times. What is the probability that the coin will show three heads?

This relative of the sea anemone [uh-NEM-uh-nee] has a polyp body whose mouth contains tentacles. It can lay eggs or bud and, as it grows, attach to surfaces where it remains for the rest of its life. Name this animal that can form large colonies, including Australia's Great Barrier Reef.
Multiple answer required. Primary colors cannot be mixed from other colors. What are the three primary colors of art?
A number pattern is created by adding 6 to the previous term. The pattern begins with 14. What is the fifth term?

This national landmark is made of an iron framework covered with thin copper sheets. Over the years, exposure to oxygen has turned the copper green. Identify this large sculpture of a woman holding a torch and a book, which stands in New York Harbor.

Unlike bone, this substance contains neither nerves nor blood vessels. It is the only component of sharks' skeletons and, in mammalian embryos, forms the skeleton before bones develop. What is this tissue that makes up the human ears and the tip of the nose?

Kentucky’s constitution requires this position which is responsible for financial oversight of the state government. Since 2016, Mike Harmon has served in what elected role whose duties include examining financial records of the state government and all state agencies?
How many words in the following sentence should be capitalized? "Big Ben is a large clock tower that stands in London, England."
You are working to find the least common multiple of two numbers. One of the numbers is 10 and the second number is 4. What is the least common multiple of 10 and 4?

Today, this process creates many mass-produced print and graphic items, including books, maps, posters, and newspapers. The artist uses a greasy oil or fat to divide a smooth surface into regions that absorb and repel ink. What is this printmaking process, whose name indicates it once required a stone?

The U.S. State Department issues this type of document which is generally valid for ten years for those over 16, and five years for those younger. What type of travel document is generally required for an American citizen to travel internationally?

Also called hydrophobia, this disease can cause throat spasms, delirium, and seizures. Bites from infected animals like dogs, cats, and raccoons can spread it to humans. Name this virus that is fatal if not treated before symptoms appear.

Like adjectives, words belonging to this part of speech can be in the positive, comparative, or superlative degree. Many of these words end in -ly. Give the part of speech of "happily" and "most slowly."
This type of clause is missing from simple and compound sentences. It is, however, found in complex and compound-complex sentences. Identify this kind of clause that can't stand alone.
Branches of this science include horticulture, agronomy, and forestry. Name this science, which is sometimes called plant biology.
Give your answer as a decimal number. The top of the desk is 25 inches wide and the desk pad on the desk is 14.5 inches wide. How many inches of the desktop in width will not be covered by the pad?
questions.a: 10.5 (TEN AND 5 TENTHS INCHES) (ACCEPT: TEN POINT FIVE OR SIMILAR RESPONSE)

questions.q: Examples of this economic principle might include federal funds used to produce a new vaccine or a company needing to pay its workers overtime to rush a new product to market. What economics term can be defined as the total amount of money or other capital spent in order to provide a service or to produce a good?

For the Medici family, this Renaissance artist painted Adoration of the Magi. He included Roman goddesses in an allegory of spring titled La Primavera [pree-muh-VAIR-uh]. Who was this artist of The Birth of Venus? (SANDRO) BOTTICELLI 61-AH. This Christian sect's worship services once featured spontaneous and, later, choreographed dancing. Members lived in isolated farm communities where men and women were separated and made wooden furniture. Mother Ann Lee founded what group, who once had a village at Mercer County's Pleasant Hill? (THE) SHAKER(S) 62-LA. Spelling required. She received a scholarship for her visual art." Spell the word in the previous sentence that means "relating to sight." V-I-S-U-A-L 63-MA. The spinner for a board game is divided into 8 equal sectors. Four of the sectors are blue; 2 are white; and the remaining sectors are black. What is the probability that the spinner will NOT land on black? 3/4 (THREE-FOURTHS) (ACCEPT: 75 PERCENT) 64-SC. In 1977, this scientist founded her namesake Institute for Wildlife Research, Education, and Conservation. For decades, she studied a certain primate species in Kenya and Tanzania [tan-zuh-NEE-uh]. Give the name of this primatologist, who conducted pioneering research on chimpanzees. (JANE) GOODALL 65-SS. The name of this act, enacted in 1787 by the Congress of the Confederation, references direction of new territory in relation to the Ohio River. Give the name of this important legislation that organized territory within the United States that would eventually become such states as Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, and Michigan.
This musical concept is closely related to register. Give the word for the full spectrum of notes a voice or instrument can produce, from lowest to highest.
Think about the number 77,777 (seventy-seven thousand, seven hundred seventy-seven). The 7 in hundreds place is how many times greater than the number in ones place?

Among this picture book's characters are a heavily tattooed man and a guitar player on a city bus. After church one Sunday, CJ and Nana take that bus to volunteer at a local soup kitchen. What is this Newbery-winning book by Matt de la Peña [PAIN-yuh]?

The two-word, alliterative name of this Kentucky community is synonymous with an annual picnic held there by the St. Jerome Catholic Church. Name the community home to this picnic which welcomes Kentucky politicians to give often fiery speeches before loud and passionate crowds.

This state of matter is so hot that electrons are ripped from their atoms. About 99 percent of the visible universe, including stars, nebulas, and auroras, is made of it. Identify this so-called "fourth state of matter."
A baker's dozen includes 13 donuts. How many donuts will be in 12 baker's dozens?

In this book, a crab confesses the crime he witnessed. At its conclusion, a large fish enters tall grass and exits with the small blue bowler another fish had stolen from him. Identify this Caldecott-winning book by Jon Klassen [KLAH-sin].

A bronze statue of this American racehorse stands at the entrance to Churchill Downs where the horses ashes were interred following his death in 2007. Give the name of the champion Thoroughbred who convincingly won the 2006 Kentucky Derby before suffering an ultimately fatal injury in his very next race.

This singing technique was once a way for animal herders to communicate over mountainous distances. Some country singers adopted this technique of rapidly alternating high and low pitches. What type of singing has an international competition every 3 years in Switzerland?

This vector quantity has a standard unit of measure in meters per second. To find it, divide the change in an object's distance by the time it took to travel that distance. Which physics quantity is an object's speed plus its direction?

This method of heat transfer can be natural or forced. Currents that cause winds and thunderstorms operate by this process, which moves liquids and gases. Name this counterpart of radiation and conduction.

This music genre originated when 19th-century slaves satirized unpopular leaders during Lent. It uses ballad meter and syncopation and is sometimes accompanied by steel bands made of tuned oil drums. Give the name of this Caribbean genre that originated in Trinidad and Tobago.

This line of latitude is located in the Northern Hemisphere and is the line above which the sun is directly overhead on the summer solstice. Name this latitude which has a counterpart in the Southern Hemisphere known as the Tropic of Capricorn.

This poet won his first of four Pulitzer Prizes for a volume he set in New Hampshire. He wrote of rural life in "The Death of the Hired Man" and "Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening." Identify this poet of "The Road Not Taken."
There were 2 and 2/3 dozen paper plates left after the party. How many paper plates were left?

This instrument is traditionally made from a eucalyptus limb or trunk that termites have hollowed out. The player vibrates their lips and uses circular breathing to produce a droning sound. Identify this folk instrument of Aboriginal Australians.
This author named Sophie from The BFG after his granddaughter. He also wrote Fantastic Mr. Fox and Charlie and the Great Glass Elevator. Who was this author of James and the Giant Peach?

About 10 to 20 percent of the sedimentary rocks in Earth's crust are this type. The arkose kind mixes feldspar and quartz grains, while the wacke type has a clay matrix. Give the name of this sedimentary rock second only in abundance to shale.

Once one of the United State’s four largest cities, this city has experienced a decades-long decline in population due to the loss of many of the automobile manufacturing jobs that had earned it the nickname, “The Motor City”. What city, also known as “Motown”, is Michigan’s largest?

At the swap meet, there were 8 vendors selling fishing supplies, 7 vendors selling boating supplies, and 5 vendors selling concessions. What is the ratio of the concession vendors to the number of fishing vendors?
questions.a: 5:8 (FIVE TO EIGHT) (ACCEPT: FIVE OVER EIGHT OR FIVE-EIGHTHS)

questions.q: In plays, this element isn't usually enclosed by quotation marks. In many poems and fiction, however, it appears in quotes. Give the term for the words exchanged between a work's characters.

The conquistador Don Pedro de Peralta settled this future state capital around 1609. The oldest European settlement west of the Mississippi, it was once the most important city north of the Rio Grande to the Spanish Empire. Identify the Spanish settlement that is today the capital of New Mexico.

The fourteen works in this composer's Swan Song were published posthumously. A post-Classical composer, he studied under Salieri [sal-ee-AIR-ee] and once sang with the Vienna Boys' Choir. Identify this man, whose Ninth Symphony was nicknamed "The Great C Major."

This process is responsible for about 10% of the water in the atmosphere. It is a subset of evaporation and begins with water passing through a plant's roots and into its vascular tissue. Identify this process by which water vapor passes through a leaf's stomata and into the air.
The Candy Shop sells candy in four-ounce packages. Enrico bought 12 packages of candy. How many pounds of candy did he buy?
This figure is a quadrilateral. It has four equal sides and four equal angles. What quadrilateral has four 90 degree angles and four sides that equal 5 inches?

This tall tale man was based on a real Kentucky native who made a so-called "whippoorwill call" on an engine's whistle. After his 1900 death in Mississippi, his co-worker Wallace Saunders wrote a ballad about him. Name this heroic railroad engineer who sacrificed his own life to save his passengers.

This historic home was once known as Little Hunting Creek Plantation before it was owned by an American Founding Father. What landmark mansion, built on the Potomac River, served as the private family home of the United States’ first president, George Washington?

In one of this country's folk dances, the troika [TROY-kuh], a man dances with two women. It also houses the Bolshoi and Mariinsky [muh-RIN-skee]--formerly Kirov--Ballet companies. Identify this country that spawned the Ballets Russes [bal-EY ROOS].

This astronomical event can happen when an old star runs out of gas to burn. It can also occur in binary star systems when a white dwarf gathers too much matter from a red giant. What are these explosions that can produce light up to 600 billion times brighter than the sun?

These protozoans can cause dysentery [DIS-in-tair-ee], a bowel infection with diarrhea. Some are parasites, while others live in fresh or saltwater. Identify these unicellular organisms that move and eat using pseudopods [SOO-duh-podz].

As a child, this man performed with his dancer brother and musician father at Harlem's Apollo Theater. He starred with Mikhail Baryshnikov [mik-EYL buh-RISH-ni-kawf] in White Nights and with Sammy Davis Jr. in Tap. Identify this actor, singer, and dancer, who also performed in the Broadway musicals Eubie! and Jelly's Last Jam.

A dance teacher wrote this nursery rhyme to help his students master the waltz clog tap routine. Its accompanying dance requires you to place one hand on your hip, hold your other arm straight, and bend at the waist. What is this nursery rhyme that ends, quote, "Tip me over and pour me out"?

Born Araminta Ross, she was often called “Moses” by those she assisted on the Underground Railroad. Identify the influential American who escaped slavery herself before courageously leading hundreds of other slaves to their own freedom.
Two angles of a triangle measure 60 degrees and 30 degrees. What is the measure in degrees of the third angle in the triangle?

This musical is based on a Gregory Maguire novel that was itself inspired by an L. Frank Baum book. Its protagonist, Elphaba, befriends Glinda and falls in love with Fiyero [fee-YAIR-oh] while learning to embrace her green skin. "Defying Gravity" ends Act One of what musical set in Oz?
Correct the following sentence, if needed: "These recipes is good for beginning bakers."
A rectangular flower box is 2 units tall by 2 units wide by 9 units long. How many cubic units of soil will fill the box?
These vascular plants reproduce via spores rather than seeds. They lack flowers and grow in warm, moist, shady places. Identify these plants recognizable by their feather-shaped fronds.

He had been a decorated officer in the Revolutionary War and given command of West Point before it was discovered he planned to surrender his fort to the British. Identify this military officer whose decision to defect to, and lead British forces against, the Americans led to his name becoming synonymous with traitors and betrayal.

One definition of this word is, quote, "of average or acceptable quality." Additionally, it can refer to bright, sunny weather. Identify this word that may also follow "county" or "book" in the names of festivals.

During America’s Prohibition Era, he gained fame as leader of the Chicago Outfit. Give the name of this man, often known as “Scarface”, whose bootlegging and other criminal activities led to his being listed as “Public Enemy Number One”.
In a game, you must roll 2 dice. If you roll a sum of 12, you can move 5 spaces. What is the probability of rolling a sum of 12 with one roll of the dice?

The house one of these insects lives in North American and European buildings. Most other types live outside in the tropics, where they use poisonous claws to hunt their prey at night. Identify these arthropods that, despite their name, can have between 14 and 177 pairs of legs.

This specific art element includes a work's subject, like a landscape's trees or a still life's vase of flowers. It doesn't include the background and areas that surround those subjects. State this opposite of negative space.
Consider the numerical expression 3 X squared. What is the exponent in the expression?

This word once named a full-scale drawing an artist did to prepare for painting a fresco. Today, the political kind satirizes the government. Name this kind of drawing found in comic strips and animated movies and TV shows.

Unlike the scaly lizard, this amphibian has smooth, shiny skin. It can regrow its tail if it breaks off and defend itself by secreting a painful or bad-tasting poison. Give the name of this slender, four-legged animal, whose subspecies include the mud puppy and newt.

In late 2022, Kyrsten Sinema became the third, current member of the U.S. Senate to list this term as their political party. What term, also used by Senator Bernie Sanders, confirms that an individual is not affiliated with or represents any existing political party, and is usually represented by the letter “I”?
With an exclamation point, this punctuation mark is half of an interrobang [in-TAIR-oh-bang]. Identify this punctuation that always ends an interrogative sentence.
Use X to represent the time in hours Tony spends on homework. He works on homework X hours a day, six days each week. How many hours does Tony spend on homework each week?

This artist explored the human body's proportions in his drawing Vitruvian [vih-TROO-vee-un] Man. He also invented an aerial screw that was an ancestor of the modern helicopter. Name this Renaissance artist of Lady with an Ermine and Madonna of the Rocks.
questions.a: LEONARDO DA VINCI (Accept first, last, or both)

questions.q: One of the freedoms protected by the First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, this freedom protects organizations like the Wall Street Journal and New York Times when investigating or criticizing the government. What Constitutional freedom prevents the government from interfering with legal reporting in magazines, newspapers, and television news shows?

Four teeth in this category are nicknamed "wisdom teeth." For adult teeth, the first and second sets typically erupt around ages 6 and 12, respectively. Identify these large, flat teeth used for grinding and located at the back of the jaw.
Identify the following sentence's verb tense: "At recess, I will go down the slide and then play kickball."
How many prepositional phrases are part of the following sentence? "The store at the corner sells sandwiches with mustard on the side."

In a science experiment, this type of variable isn't influenced by any of the experiment's other factors. However, it can cause changes to other variables in the experiment. Give the term for the variable the experimenter changes in order to prove or disprove her hypothesis.
The recipe for chocolate cookies requires two-thirds cup of cocoa. You need to triple the recipe. How many cups of cocoa will you need?

This company reported in 2022 that it expected to lose more than $200 million after terminating its relationship with a controversial hip hop star. Name the sportswear company that ended production of the Yeezy fashion line due the actions and statements of its former partner, Kanye West.

This man illustrated scenes from Dante's Inferno with his sculpture The Gates of Hell. Among his other sculptures are The Kiss and The Burghers of Calais [kah-LAY]. Name this artist of The Thinker. (AUGUSTE) RODIN [aw-GYOOST roh-DAN] 61-AH. Amish and Mennonites reject this type of folk art, which they say springs from pagan superstition. Other American settlers painted them directly on their barns and, later, on circular discs they attached to their buildings. Identify these colorful geometric signs favored by the Pennsylvania Dutch. HEX (SIGN(S)) 62-LA. Spelling required. When combined, oil and water immediately separate. Spell the word from the previous sentence that is a synonym of "divide." S-E-P-A-R-A-T-E 63-MA. Use M to represent the money that Sally spent on lunch. Sally had $10.00 in her purse. What expression shows how much money she had left after buying lunch? $10 - M (TEN DOLLARS MINUS M) (ACCEPT: TEN MINUS M) 64-SC. This biologist's first three books were called Under the Sea-Wind, The Sea Around Us, and The Edge of the Sea. Her masterpiece eventually convinced the U.S. government to ban the pesticide DDT. Name the author of Silent Spring. (RACHEL) CARSON 65-SS. The project to construct this monument has been in progress since 1948, though as of 2023, it is still likely decades from being finished. What memorial, under construction in the Black Hills near Mount Rushmore, is designed to honor a Lakota warrior?

This symbol is also called the G clef because it wraps around a staff's second line. It means the staff's lines are, from bottom to top, E, G, B, D, F and its spaces are F, A, C, and E. What is this clef, whose notes a pianist plays with the right hand?
Three real numbers, A, B, and C are on a number line. Number B is between A and C and to the left of C. Which number is the largest of the three numbers?

This novel's title comes from the Twelve-Step meetings the protagonist overhears. Set in tiny Hard Pan, California, it includes a motherless girl's mistaken belief that her guardian Brigitte is moving back to France. Name this Newbery winner by Susan Patron [puh-TROHN].
This river is formed when the Levisa Fork meets the Tug Fork in northeastern Kentucky. Give the name of the river that forms a boundary between Kentucky and West Virginia.

This heterogeneous [het-uh-roh-JEE-nee-us] mixture has solid particles that are dispersed, but not dissolved, in a liquid. If left alone, the solid particles will separate and settle over time. What kind of mixture is water and sand?
Happy the Clown needs 45 balloons to make the balloon animals for the party. Balloons come in packages of eight. How many whole packages must Happy buy for the party?

In this picture book, a poem uses the words of Gwendolyn Brooks, Langston Hughes, and Martin Luther King, Jr. It covers slavery's horrors, the Civil Rights movement, and African-Americans' resilience today. Name this Caldecott winner with art by Kadir [kuh-DEER] Nelson and words by Kwame [KWA-mee] Alexander.

This Confederate general was commander of the Army of Mississippi and later the Army of Tennessee and played an important role in one of Kentucky’s most important Civil War battles. Name the Confederate general who was forced to retreat from Kentucky to Tennessee following the Battle of Perryville?

In this kind of work, a singer's solos are called arias. An orchestra accompanies performers who sing, act, and sometimes dance. Identify this genre of Beethoven's Fidelio and Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro.

This force is what propels a flying machine in the direction of motion. Engines usually generate this force, which is how a craft maneuvers in outer space. Identify this counterpart of weight, drag, and lift.
This rock is a member of the spinel [spuh-NEL] group. Early compasses used it because it naturally pointed north. Identify this rock, whose natural polarity attracts iron.

This oldest brass instrument only had piston valves added around 1820. Its thin tubing gives it a bright sound, and its most popular versions are pitched in B-flat and C. Identify this smallest and highest-pitched brass instrument in a standard orchestra.

Director Taika Waititi created an acclaimed television series about teenagers growing up on this type of land which stars D’Pharaoh Woon-A-Tai, Devery Jacobs, and other fully indigenous actors. What is the name for an area of land that is set aside to be inhabited and self-governed by Native American populations?
One poem in this unstructured form is Walt Whitman's "Song of Myself." Give the two-word phrase for a poem that lacks both meter and rhyme.
Give your answer as a mixed number in lowest terms. Carson finished a book by reading the same number of pages every day for 8 days. If the book had 76 pages, how many pages did he read each day?

This ancestor of the classical guitar descended from the Middle Eastern oud [OOD]. The sitar is a type of this instrument, whose popularity was highest during the Renaissance. Name this stringed instrument with a hollow, pear-shaped body.

This author's works combine Christianity with fantasy and elements of modern science. She created the Austin family in the Chronos series and the Murry and O'Keefe families in the Kairos chronicles. Identify this writer of A Wrinkle in Time.
This mineral ranks a 4 on the Mohs hardness scale. It naturally grows in cubic crystals that can be colorless, purple, yellow, blue, or green. Name this mineral that glows under a blacklight.

Workers are often referred to by this term when they perform jobs in manual labor such as mining, construction, and manufacturing. Give the colorful name for this type of worker or job which is often contrasted with those considered “white-collar”.
There are 12 empty seats on a plane and 40 occupied seats. What is the ratio of occupied seats to the total number of seats on the plane?
questions.a: 10:13 (TEN TO THIRTEEN) (ACCEPT: TEN OVER THIRTEEN OR TEN-THIRTEENTHS)

questions.q: This literary element is also called atmosphere. The writer uses a piece's diction, setting, and tone to create it. What do we call the emotions a written piece evokes in the reader?

The cultivation of this cash crop was an important source of revenue for the early settlers in the Colony of Virginia. Name this crop, often credited as introduced in Virginia by John Rolfe, which would later be important to the economies of such U.S. states as North Carolina and Kentucky.

The composer later included this 3-minute work in his Third Symphony, which he published in 1946. The Cincinnati Symphony commissioned this work, which the composer dedicated to everyday Americans sacrificing for the war effort. Give the title of this percussion and brass composition by Aaron Copland [COPE-lund].

This part of the hydrosphere is what people hit when they dig a well. Its highest level is the water table, which gets pumped to the surface. Give the word for this underground reservoir inside rocks.
Each art group uses 3 pints of tempera to complete their projects. The class used 1.5 gallons of tempera. How many pints of tempera did the class use?
A triangle has three angles measuring 60 degrees each. What type of triangle has three equal angles?

Some tall tales claim this man had a son with his wife Polly Ann. He sang, played the banjo, and worked in the Allegheny Mountains for the Chesapeake and Ohio Railroad. Who was this former slave who died after defeating a steam drill in a race?
