A 22-year-old George Washington led an ambush on rival soldiers during this war’s Battle of Jumonville Glen. What war, fought from 1754 to 1763, saw various Native American tribes choose to fight alongside either British or French colonists?

This dance originated in lower-class ballrooms in Paris's Montparnasse [mohn-par-NASS] neighborhood. By the 1890s, it had spread to music halls, where a female chorus line wearing skirts, petticoats, and black stockings performed it. Give the repetitive name of this high-kicking dance.
Currently, this part of Canis Major is the sky's brightest appearing star. Give the name of this body nicknamed the "dog star."

This protozoan has a deep oral groove in its oval body and is slipper shaped. It lives in fresh or brackish water and moves using small hairs that beat in rhythmic waves. Give the name of this ciliate [SILL-ee-ut].

For the Vic-Wells Ballet, this woman danced Aurora in a 1939 revival of The Sleeping Beauty. She created roles in Frederick Ashton-choreographed works and performed for 15 years opposite a Russian dancer who had defected. Name this Royal Ballet prima ballerina, who co-starred in Romeo and Juliet with Rudolf Nureyev [noo-REY-ef].

In the Brothers Grimm version of this fairy tale, a woodcutter saves the title character and her grandmother. In the Charles Perrault [puh-ROW] version, a predator successfully eats both the protagonist and her grandma. Give the title of this fairy tale about a young girl who meets a wolf in the woods.

In keeping with the name of this system, so-called “passengers” were led by “conductors” to various “stations” along their route to freedom. Give the two-word name for the secret network of routes used by enslaved individuals to escape to the freedom in northern states.
Mr. Jones wants to fence his hexagon-shaped garden. Each side of the garden is 12 feet. What is the perimeter in feet of his garden?

In this musical, the protagonist's father Alfred sings "Get Me to the Church on Time." It follows phonetics Professor Henry Higgins's attempts to turn Cockney flower seller Eliza Doolittle into a lady. Identify this Lerner and Loewe musical based on George Bernard Shaw's Pygmalion [pig-MALE-ee-un].
In general, this word means "very hot and humid." What is this adjective that technically applies to the parts of the globe nearest the Equator?
A box of apple juice has a square base with an area of 25 square units. The height of the box is 12 units. What is the volume of the juice box in cubic units?

This science word can follow "thigmo-" [THIG-mo], "gravi-," "hydro-," "chemo-," "thermo-," and "photo-." It is the directional movement that a plant exhibits in response to a certain stimulus. What is this instinctual behavior that can be triggered by light, heat, or water?

The name for this period of American history comes from the Latin for “before the war”. Give the name for this period, coinciding roughly with the years between the War of 1812 and the American Civil War, in which the southern economy was based on plantations and the widespread use of slavery.
Spelled one way, this word is a synonym of "odor" or "smell." Spelled another way, it names 1/100 of a dollar. Give these words' shared pronunciation.
Having served as Speaker of the House from 2007 to 2011, this Californian returned to the office in 2019 and served until 2023. Name the first woman ever elected Speaker of the House.
A twelve-sided die has the numbers 1 through 12. What is the probability of rolling a number divisible by 3?
Ancient Egyptians associated this insect with the god who rolled the sun across the sky. What is this beetle that lays its eggs in balls of dung that it rolls?

By definition, frescoes are this type of painting. Some people confuse graffiti, a type of street art, with it. Give the word for a painting executed directly on a large permanent surface, like a wall or ceiling.
The first three terms in a pattern are 5, 15, and 45. What is the rule to find the next term in the pattern?

Artistic movements that originated in this country include the Barbizon School, Fauvism [FO-viz-um], and Rococo. It was also the home of Neoclassicism and Impressionism. Which European nation's museums include the Musée d'Orsay [MEW-zay DOR-say] and the Louvre [LOOV]?

This is the only entirely carnivorous primate species. They leap between trees and live only in Southeast Asia, especially the Philippines. Identify these large-eyed animals named for their long ankle bones.

In early 2023, Senator Patty Murray began serving in this role which is the U.S. Senate’s second-highest-ranking position. What U.S. Senate leadership position is typically held by a longtime-serving senator who presides over the body in the vice-president’s absence?
questions.a: PRESIDENT PRO TEM(PORE) (OF THE UNITED STATES SENATE)

questions.q: Which words should be capitalized in the following sentence? "In the United States, Thanksgiving always falls on the fourth Thursday in November."
questions.a: IN, UNITED, STATES, THANKSGIVING, THURSDAY, (AND) NOVEMBER (any order)

questions.q: Solve for X in this equation. 14X equals 28. What is the value of X?

This artist ignored perspective and Western ideas of beauty in his group portrait Les Demoiselles d'Avignon [luh dem-wah-ZEL dah-veen-YAWN]. Some of his oil paintings resemble collages, including two works titled The Three Musicians. Who was this Cubist artist with African, Rose, and Blue Periods?
This economic condition exists when supply is greater than demand. What term refers to the excess amounts of a good possessed by a retailer or manufacturer after all demand has been accounted for?

Early signs of this disease include fatigue, headache, fever, and a rash that resembles a bull's eye. Humans contract it when ticks harboring certain bacteria bite them. What is this disease named for the Connecticut town where it was first diagnosed?
State the following sentence's complete predicate: "The opera star finished her last song."
This kind of sentence can end with either a period or an exclamation point. What type of sentence gives a command?

Full name, please. This type of semiconductor device gives off infrared or visible light when an electric current charges it. They are used in newer cars' brake lights, as indicator lights on electronics, and sometimes as home light bulbs. Identify this device, whose name is usually shortened to L.E.D.
Add the mixed numbers: 4 and 1/3 plus 5 and 1/6. What is the sum as a mixed number in lowest terms?

The United States is generally said to have this type of economy because, while much of its economy operates as a free market, some control and regulation is maintained by the government. Name this type of economy which can most easily be defined as a blending of other existing economic systems.

The Cherokee used this dance to remove evil spirits from the earth. Some tribes wore feathers and turquoise during it to represent wind and precipitation. What kind of ceremonial dance did many Native American tribes perform in hopes of keeping their crops watered? RAIN (DANCE) 61-AH. These objects were carved of cottonwood and presented to a tribe's girls by its men. They featured masks, feathers, and colors to teach children about a tribe's ancestral and divine spirits. Give the name of these dolls created by the Hopi. KACHINA [kuh-CHEE-nuh] (DOLL) 62-LA. Spelling required. "Traffic jams are frustrating for all the parties involved." Spell the word in the preceding sentence that is a synonym of "annoying." F-R-U-S-T-R-A-T-I-N-G 63-MA. Let X equal the number of bananas in each bunch. There are 16 bunches of bananas. How many bananas are there in all? 16X (SIXTEEN X) (ACCEPT: SIXTEEN TIMES X) 64-SC. This member of the Mercury Seven later became a U. S. Senator from Ohio. At age 77, he took part in a nine-day mission aboard Discovery, making him the oldest person at that point to have gone to space. In 1962, which astronaut became the first American to orbit Earth? (JOHN) GLENN 65-SS. First and last name required. A memorial to this U.S. president in Washington D.C., features a sculpture of the president seated next to his dog, Fala. In 2001, a sculpture was added to the memorial depicting this president in a wheelchair. Identify this president who won re-election to the office three times.

This musical element is influenced by how many instruments are playing and how many different vocal or instrumental parts are in a piece. It might be described as thick or thin and shares its name with an element of art. Name this element concerned with the relationships between a musical piece's layers.
Identify this number by its definition. This integer is a real number and a whole number larger than negative one. What is this integer that is not a natural or counting number?

This fantasy novel is set in the Kingdom of Dor, which is ruled by Princess Pea's father. At its conclusion, the princess, Miggery Sow, Roscuro [ro-SKYOOR-oh] the rat, and the title mouse all reach their own happy endings. Give the title of this Newbery-winning novel by Kate DiCamillo [dee-kuh-MILL-oh].

The universities of Brescia and Kentucky Wesleyan are located in this city, Kentucky’s fourth-largest by population. Identify this Kentucky city bordering Indiana which was the birthplace and childhood home of actor Johnny Depp.

When this chemical reaction happens very quickly, an explosion can result. It begins when a substance reaches its ignition point, usually by being struck by a spark, exposed to strong light, or heated. Fire is the most common type of what chemical reaction that produces heat and light?
The vendor had 72 keychains for sale. He sold all of the keychains. If each customer bought 3 keychains, how many customers bought the keychains?

This Caldecott-winning book's last update included George W. Bush. Its subjects are the first 42 leaders of the United States. Give the title of this book written by Judith St. George and illustrated by David Small.
questions.a: SO YOU WANT TO BE PRESIDENT?

questions.q: One of the most important political figures in Kentucky history, he served as both Speaker of the House and Secretary of State. He was also an influential U.S. senator, multi-time candidate for president, and a leading member of the Whig party. Who was this political figure often referred to as the “Great Compromiser”?
Originally, this term referred to hymns that celebrated the birth of Jesus. Later, it spread to songs about snow and Santa Claus. What do we call these seasonal Christmas songs?

Confusingly, this force isn't really a force, but instead is the result of inertia [ih-NUR-shuh]. A tetherball exhibits it, as does a person riding a merry-go-round. Name this force, which is the energy of an object trying to move in a straight line when it's actually moving in a circle.

This phenomenon occurs when a light, sound, or other wave encounters a small object in its path. It also happens when the wave is forced through a small opening. Which physics process happens when a wave remains in the same medium but bends around an object?

In both World Wars, this instrument accompanied the Highland Regiment into battle. It has a drone and a chanter attached to a sack that, in earlier centuries, was made of animal skin. Name this traditional Scottish wind instrument.

This type of water body is generally larger than a bay, but typically features a narrower opening. Give the name for these large bodies of water, an example of which borders Florida to the west and the states of Mississippi, Louisiana, and Alabama to the south.
Besides rhyme, this sound device is also part of the sentence, "It's true--I do like you!" What is the name for this repetition of vowel sounds?
The garden path is 15 feet long. The path is covered with 20 equal-sized stones. As a fraction in lowest terms and in feet, how big is each stone?

In 2012, Max Richter released a so-called "recomposed" version of this Baroque violin suite. The original works were published with accompanying poems that the composer may or may not have written. What is the collective title for this Antonio Vivaldi work consisting of "Spring," "Summer," "Autumn," and "Winter"?

This author's first novel, A Summer to Die, was based on the loss of her sister. She also created the fictional siblings Anastasia and Sam Krupnik. Give the name of this author of the Gooney Bird Greene series.
This part of soil helps form pores and keeps the soil loose and soft. It also provides the nutrients that plants need. Identify this organic matter made from decaying plants and animals.

Three-word answer required. An American family’s communication by way of this language formed the plot of the 2022 Oscar winner for Best Picture, CODA. This visual-based, natural language is the primary form of language for hundreds of thousands of Americans within the Deaf communities. Identify this form of language often abbreviated ASL.
Seventy-five percent of the theater seats were filled. There are 200 seats in the theater. How many seats were filled?

Essentially, this literary technique is the opposite of a flashback. In it, an author may point out objects that will prove important or describe an event similar to what will happen. Identify this type of spoiler that hints at what will occur later in a work.

Some researchers have suggested the single letter within the name of this generational group could stand for “zoomers”. Give the name for the generation of individuals, now roughly between the ages of 10 and 25, which directly followed a generation known as the Millennials.

This composer designed the Bayreuth [by-ROIT] Festival Theater in Bavaria to house his operas. Those works include The Flying Dutchman, Parsifal [PAR-sif-uhl], and Lohengrin [LO-hen-grin]. Whose masterpiece was the four-opera Ring Cycle?
This atmospheric layer extends to about 30 miles above Earth's surface. It lies above the troposphere [TRO-pus-feer] and below the mesosphere [MEZ-uh-sfeer]. What is this home of the ozone layer?

The gym teacher set up an obstacle course at school. Students have to bounce a ball for the first 6 feet, then run 12 feet to the end of the field, and finally hop back to the beginning of the course. How many yards must the students hop?
A regular pentagon has five equal interior angles. What is the measure of an interior angle of a regular pentagon in degrees?

This fable ends with a group of insects dismissing another insect's request for food. The starving bug spent the summer playing music while his neighbors stored grain for winter. Identify this Aesop fable teaching that, quote, "There's a time for work and a time for play."

Residents of Ohio are often referred to by this term which is also the mascot for The Ohio State University. Give this term, which can describe a type of peanut butter candy dipped in chocolate, found in Ohio’s state nickname.

This 19th-century social dance possibly originated in Germany before spreading to France and England. It required a couple to perform a slide, close, slide step in 2/4 time. What was this dance, whose name sounds like a horse's run?

Scientists first discovered these so-called "light clocks" in 1967 and, to date, have found about 2,000. These rapidly spinning neutron stars can emit radio waves, visible light, x-rays, or gamma rays. Identify these stars named for the regular bursts of energy they emit.

Like the endoplasmic reticulum [in-doh-PLAZ-mik ruh-TIK-yuh-lum], this organelle resembles a stack of pancakes. It absorbs transport vesicles from the E.R. and forms lysosomes [LIE-suh-zomes]. Identify this organelle that packages proteins for transport in vesicles.
questions.a: GOLGI [GOAL-jee] APPARATUS (Accept GOLGI BODY, GOLGI COMPLEX)

questions.q: This man won Emmy Awards for directing and choreographing the TV special Liza with a Z. His record eight Best Choreography Tonys came for musicals like Pippin, Sweet Charity, and The Pajama Game. Who directed and co-wrote the semi-autobiographical movie All That Jazz?

This fairy tale inspired the title of a 1941 A. A. Milne play. Since its publication, that title has become a saying for, quote, "an unattractive or unpromising child who becomes a beautiful or much-admired adult." Identify this Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale about an unloved young bird who becomes a beautiful swan.

Three-word answer required. Playwright Arthur Miller famously depicted these events in his Tony Award-winning play, The Crucible. Some 200 residents of colonial Massachusetts were accused of witchcraft in what controversial series of prosecutions during the late 1600's?
Give your answer in terms of pi. The diameter of a circle is 6 units. What is the circumference of the circle in units?
This theatrical form originated in 17th-century Kyoto. Like noh, it requires performers to act, sing, and dance. Heavy make-up and all-male casts are features of which type of Japanese drama?

This suffix meaning "condition of" or "skill" often means a word is a noun. It may follow "relation," "leader," "friend," or "champion." Identify this suffix that, as a standalone word, names a large boat.
A spinner is divided such that one-sixth of the sectors are red, one-half of the sectors are green, and one-third of the sectors are white. On which color is the spinner least likely to land?
These plant parts protect and enclose a bud as it develops into a flower. What are these outermost flower organs that resemble small leaves?

Delivered at the dedication of the Soldiers’ National Cemetery on November 19, 1863, this brief speech began with the words “Four score and seven years ago”. Give the name of this iconic speech delivered during the American Civil War by President Abraham Lincoln.
This word can be a synonym of "student." Identify this word that also names the black, central portion of the eye.

From 1817 to 1825, he served as the United States’ fifth president. Which early American president is best remembered today for his “doctrine” warning European powers against taking any further action in the Western Hemisphere?

You want to make as many different outfits as possible from the clothes in your closet. You have 6 shirts, 5 bow ties, and 2 pairs of pants in the closet. How many outfits can you make from these different clothes?

Organisms with this type of symmetry don't have left or right sides but do have fronts and backs. They can repeat a body part 4, 5, 6, or 8 times around a central axis. Identify this symmetry exhibited by the sea anemone [uh-NEM-uh-nee] and the starfish.

Ancient artists created this type of art with colored pebbles. Its pieces are called tesserae [TESS-uh-ree], which means "dice" or "cubes" in Latin. Identify this long-lasting art form that consists of small glass, ceramic, or stone pieces embedded in plaster.
A geometric sequence begins with 14, 28, and 56. What is the fifth term in the sequence?

This art style believed in letting the viewer's eye mix colors instead of having an artist mix them on a palette or canvas. Its pioneers were the French painters Paul Signac [seen-YAK] and Georges Seurat [ZHWARZH suh-RAH]. Identify this movement named for the small dots of color it favored over brushstrokes.

In high temperatures, this animal's short-beaked variety cools itself by blowing mucus bubbles that burst and evaporate. Also called the spiny anteater, it resembles--but is unrelated to--the hedgehog. Give the name of this species that, with the platypus, is Australia's only monotreme.

A major road within Lexington, Kentucky is named for this legendary racehorse who won 20 of the 21 races run during his career. Fittingly, this thoroughbred’s only loss came to a horse named Upset. Give the name of this animal widely often considered the horse racing’s all-time greatest champion.

These paired punctuation marks may enclose a side comment or side sentence. They show that the information between them is a non-essential clause. Name these punctuation marks that look like curved brackets.
Let D represent the number of dogs in the pet store. Let C represent the number of cats in the store. What equation shows that there are a total of 16 dogs and cats in the store?
questions.a: D + C = 16 (D PLUS C EQUALS 16) (ACCEPT: C + D = 16)

questions.q: This group of about 30 paintings was the artist's first series dedicated to a single subject. Completed in 1890 and '91, it examined seasonal light changes on piles of a feed crop for horses and cattle. Identify this Monet series.

This three-word title is among those held by the president of the United States and refers to the president’s power within the U.S. Armed Forces. What title gives the president absolute control and authority of the military?

This body system's major organs include the thymus, spleen, appendix, and tonsils. A relative of the circulatory and immune systems, it is the reason bone marrow produces white blood cells. What is this system named for a yellowish fluid that small vessels transfer from the body's tissues to the bloodstream?
What is the following sentence's direct object? "For my 11th birthday, my dad built me a clubhouse."
Identify the following sentence's appositive phrase: "A record-setting runner, Shakira practically lived at the track."
This type of data is either discrete or continuous. Those words mean the data is either countable or measurable. State this opposite of qualitative data.
Sharon painted 22 roses and 6 daisies on the mural. What is the ratio of daisies to the total number of flowers that Sharon painted?
questions.a: 3:14 (THREE TO FOURTEEN) (ACCEPT: 3/14 OR THREE OVER FOURTEEN)

questions.q: Economists often use a graph to determine the existence of this economic situation by pinpointing the moment that an item’s supply and demand meet. Give the name for this moment in a market in which the available supply of a good or service is perfectly balanced with the current demand for it.

In the mid-1800's, women sometimes held so-called "bees" to complete this type of folk art. It has a layer of insulating batting tucked between two pieces of cloth. Name this kind of blanket that can be pieced or patchwork. QUILT(S) 61-AH. This United Nations Messenger of Peace was arrested for refusing to fight in the Vietnam War. He earned an Olympic gold medal at age 18 and was the first boxer to win the world heavyweight championship three times. Name this Louisville native, who claimed he could, quote, "float like a butterfly, sting like a bee." (MUHAMMAD) ALI 62-LA. Spelling required. "He hopes to duplicate his overseas success domestically." Spell the word in the preceding sentence meaning, quote, "to produce something equal to." D-U-P-L-I-C-A-T-E 63-MA. A bag contains 3 red cubes, 4 blue cubes, and 7 orange cubes. What is the probability of choosing an orange cube on the first draw? 1/2 (ONE-HALF) (ACCEPT: 50 PERCENT) 64-SC. This physician used hypnosis to help his patients speak freely about their lives. He divided the human mind into the id, ego, and superego and wrote The Interpretation of Dreams. Identify this Viennese man nicknamed the "father of psychoanalysis." (SIGMUND) FREUD [FROYD] 65-SS. In a popular musical parody concerning this type of digital asset, rapper Jack Harlow explains, “its unique, there can only be one”. In December 2022, former president Donald Trump announced he was selling a line of them featuring artistic portraits of himself. Identify these blockchain-based assets, often produced in the form of photos or videos, that are often bought and sold under a three-letter abbreviation.

In music, this Italian word is a synonym of diminuendo [dih-MIN-yoo-IN-doh]. It resembles a "greater than" sign in math. Identify this symbol that tells a musician to gradually play or sing more softly.
You learn that 7 times 8 is 56. You also learn that 8 times 7 is 56. What property of multiplication states that the product is the same regardless of the order of the numbers multiplied?

As this novel opens, the title character runs away from his uncle and aunt's home and arrives in segregated Two Mills, Pennsylvania. He befriends Amanda Beale, former baseball player Earl Grayson, and eventually, his rival Mars Bar Thompson. Identify this Newbery-winning Jerry Spinelli novel.

This city began experiencing rapid population growth in the mid 1980's when it was selected as the site of the Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky factory. Name this Kentucky city, the county seat of Scott County.

Ernest Rutherford discovered these subatomic particles in 1920. The number of them present in an atom's nucleus indicates what element the atom belongs to. Name these positively charged subatomic particles.
This question requires multiple responses in correct order. List the following numbers in order from least to greatest: 17, 70, 5, and 32.

This book ends with its author realizing he loves two places: Japan and California. Most of the story occurs in the late 1800's, when the author's ancestor immigrated from East Asia to the United States. What is this autobiographical Caldecott winner by Allen Say?

This Kentucky-native had served as Secretary of War under President Franklin Pierce before being chosen to serve as the president of a breakaway republic in 1861. Who served as president of the Confederate States of America during the American Civil War?
In the Middle Ages and the Renaissance, this was one of Western music's two primary genres. Today, it encompasses genres like rock, jazz, and hip-hop. Give the word for non-religious music.

The fastest one of these in the universe belongs to light and is represented in an equation by the letter C. It is a scalar quantity that, like velocity, is often measured in meters per second. What is this measure of how fast an object moves relative to a reference point?
Diamond is a good one of these for heat but a bad one for electricity. To varying degrees, all metals are this for both electricity and heat. What is this opposite of an insulator?

Types of this instrument include suspended, finger, and crash. They are part of a drum kit but can also be heard in orchestras. Identify these thin metal disks that are struck with a mallet or hit against each other.

Individuals involved in this practice use such tools as scale and projection to create specific representations of the Earth or lands within it. Give the name for the science and practice of making maps.
This poetic form has both Italian and English versions whose rhyme schemes differ. One poem of this type is "How Do I Love Thee?" by Elizabeth Barrett Browning. Name this kind of 14-line lyric poem.
This multiple of nine has factors of one and two. It also has factors of three and four. What number equals 12 when it is divided by nine?

The composer hid many Freemason symbols in this 1791 opera. Pamina [puh-MEE-nuh] and Tamino [tuh-MEE-no] join forces with Sarastro [suh-RAH-stroh] to defeat the Queen of the Night. Give the title of this final Mozart opera.

In this novel, a 12-year-old boy becomes apprenticed to his community's Receiver of Memory. However, he escapes that village with the infant Gabriel, who is scheduled to be killed the next day. Identify this prequel of Gathering Blue, Messenger, and Son, all written by Lois Lowry.

Soil of this type has smaller particles than sand or silt. It is plastic when wet, meaning it can be rolled, pinched, or sculpted into a variety of forms. Name this substance that can produce long-lasting bricks, pipes, or flowerpots after it dries and hardens.

Communities organized by members of this religious group form a popular tourist destination in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. Give the name for this group and related lifestyle generally characterized by plain clothing and the rejection of modern technology.

The waitress at Joe's Drive-In is filling salt shakers from a 3 pound box of salt. The waitress divides the salt equally between 15 shakers. As a fraction in lowest terms, how many pounds of salt will go in each salt shaker?

Like legends, these ancient stories often featured gods or fantasy creatures. Part of the oral tradition, they usually tried to explain natural phenomena like the world's creation. Name these fictional stories found in cultures from Greece and Rome to China, Mexico, and Peru.

Illegal immigrants who entered the United States before adulthood may be referred to by this name which comes from an acronym for the Development, Relief, and Education for Alien Minors Act. Give this name, most often used in reference to undocumented students and children, that might also describe a group of sleeping individuals.

This folk dance incorporates steps from the quadrille, English Country Dance, and Morris Dance. Those steps include the promenade, allemande, and do si do [DOE SEE DOE]. What is this dance for four couples, whose name indicates the shape they make on the floor?

Unlike its white counterpart, the black type of this weather phenomenon is invisible and more damaging. Farmers adjust their growing season to occur between the last one in the spring and the first one in the fall. When water condenses and freezes out of the air, what thin white coating results?
Harper receives a 20 percent tip for each dollar she earns. She earned $55.00 on Tuesday. How much did she receive in tips on Tuesday?
A certain bridge will support vehicles that weigh 5 tons. An empty truck and driver weigh 6,550 pounds. How many pounds of cargo can the truck carry across the bridge?

Some translations of this fable paint the title characters as cousins, while others say they're only friends. The animals eat simple food at a rural home but, when they try to eat a rich meal in the city, two large dogs interrupt their feast. Which Aesop fable teaches, quote, "Better beans and bacon in peace than cakes and ale in fear"?
questions.a: (THE) TOWN MOUSE AND THE COUNTRY MOUSE

questions.q: A war named for this Native American leader, fought from 1675 to 1676, is considered one of the bloodiest conflicts in American history. Name this son of Massasoit who waged war against New England’s colonists.

This dance's traditional form resembles Cuba's rumba and Puerto Rico's bomba. Percussion instruments provide a beat in 2/4 time as dancers shift their weight from one leg to the other. Give the name of this national dance of Brazil.

Spots on this celestial body's surface appear and disappear in 11-year cycles. Its so-called "wind" consists of particles ejected from its outer layer, the corona. Name this center of our solar system.

This organelle is only found in eukaryotic [yoo-kare-ee-AH-tik] cells. It consists of a porous envelope, chromatin [KRO-muh-tin], and a nucleolus [noo-klee-OH-lus]. What is this organelle that directs a cell's reproduction, growth, and metabolism?

This man choreographed and appeared in one of the first dance films, 1912's Dances of the Ages. The school and company he co-founded with his wife trained modern dancers like Martha Graham. Identify this founder of Jacob's Pillow and husband of Ruth St. Denis.

This Nobel Peace Prize winner titled his final speech "I've Been to the Mountaintop." He wrote "Letter from Birmingham Jail" after being imprisoned for demonstrating against Alabama segregation. Which civil rights leader, during the 1963 March on Washington, delivered his "I Have a Dream" speech?

This document was signed on November 21, 1620 aboard a ship anchored in a Massachusetts harbor. Name this document on how to govern Plymouth Colony, agreed to by the Pilgrims and named for the ship which brought them to the New World.
The angles of an equilateral triangle are congruent. What is the measure in degrees of an interior angle in any equilateral triangle?

In theater, a soliloquy [suh-LIL-uh-kwee] is a special type of this. Acting schools, agents, and casting directors often require a performer to deliver one or more of them. Give the word for a theatrical speech by a single character.
In a certain saying, being "put out to" this place means a person, animal, or thing is past its prime. State this word beginning with P for grassland used for grazing livestock.
A rectangular box is 12 inches long by 9 inches wide. How many inches of ribbon will be needed to go around the box?

In narrow leaves, these structures lie parallel to each other, but they are net-like in broader leaves. They provide a skeleton of sorts and also carry food and water to and from the leaves. What are these plant parts that share their name with a type of human blood vessel?

In December 1860, this southern state became the first to secede from the Union. Identify this state, which in April 1861 was the site of the Battle of Fort Sumter and the official beginning of the American Civil War.

One word with this pronunciation names a small room in a prison or an organism's basic structural unit. Another word pronounced this way is the opposite of "purchase." Give the shared pronunciation of these words.
Before he was elected president, he served as secretary of state in the administration of his predecessor, Andrew Jackson. Who was elected in 1836 as the United States’ eighth president?
There are 6 orange marbles and 5 blue marbles in a bag. What is the probability of picking a blue marble from the bag without looking?

Long mistaken for plants, these animals help build and maintain coral reefs. A skeleton supports its soft mass of cells, while spongy skin lets water flow inside. Name these members of the phylum Porifera [puh-RIF-uh-ruh], which are full of holes.
Be specific. This structure can be used to dry wood, melt metal, or heat limestone. Name this furnace or oven also used for baking bricks and firing pottery.
Adding an even integer and nonzero non-even integer will result in this type of integer. What type of integer will result when adding two even integers and one nonzero non-even integer?

This kind of artwork may be group, singular, or self-. Today's iPhone cameras have a mode called this, which puts the subject in focus and blurs the background. Give the word for a painting, drawing, or photograph of one or more people.

Only one species of this bird lives near the Equator--specifically, in the Galápagos [guh-LAH-puh-gohs] Islands. The rest reside in the far Southern Hemisphere, where they eat krill and use their flippers to swim, but not fly. What are these black-and-white swimming birds found partly in Antarctica?
In 2020, this American city’s NFL team retired its previous name and logo due to potential insensitivity towards Native Americans. What city’s NFL team is now known as the Commanders?
How many words in the following sentence need to be capitalized? Chloe asked, "Will you watch The Little Mermaid with me?"
The first basket has 36 eggs; the second basket has 24 eggs and the third basket has 12 eggs. Following this arithmetic pattern, how many eggs will be in the fourth basket?

This artist's 1884 painting Children Playing on the Beach shows the influence of Japanese printmaking. Among her other works are Lilacs in a Window, The Cup of Tea, and Girl Arranging Her Hair. Which Impressionist painted Nurse Reading to a Little Girl?
Doug Emhoff became the first American to fill this title when his wife, Kamala Harris, became vice-president. Give the title for the husband of a vice-president of the United States.

In humans, this body system is divided into the axial and appendicular [ap-in-DIK-yoo-lur] sections. Adult ones typically have 206 components, including the vertebral column, rib cage, and skull. Name this system made of the bones that protect softer organs.
Identify the following sentence's predicate nominative: "Melinda is a guitarist in a local rock band."
State the following sentence's noun clause: "They have a surprise for whoever wins the competition."

Scientists often prefer these pieces of lab equipment to beakers when they need to handle or store multiple small samples. Made of Pyrex--heat-resistant glass--they allow for easy heating of samples. Name this thin cylinder with a U-shaped bottom and an open top.
Solve for N in the following equation. Seventeen minus N equals negative one. What is the value of N?
A basic definition for this economic term is “a person cannot have everything they want.” What term do economists use to explain that not all resources can be available to all people all of the time?

One California tribe made this craft out of planks, while the Chippewa and Ojibwe [oh-JIB-way] created birch bark ones. In the Pacific Northwest, tribes carved dugout ones from cedar trunks. Identify these narrow, open boats that were propelled by paddles or, in a few cases, sails. CANOE(S) 61-AH. At age 22, this man entered the Jesuit order, but didn't take his final vows until 1973. He was archbishop of Buenos Aires and then a cardinal before succeeding Benedict the Sixteenth in his current role. As of February 2023, who is this Roman Catholic pope? (POPE) FRANCIS (THE FIRST) 62-LA. Spelling required. "The detectives undertook a thorough investigation." Spell the word from the preceding sentence that means, quote, "extremely attentive to accuracy and detail." T-H-O-R-O-U-G-H 63-MA. Kelly rode her bike for one-half mile. If there are 1,760 yards in one mile, how many yards did Kelly ride? 880 (EIGHT HUNDRED EIGHTY YARDS) 64-SC. This scientist investigated gravity by dropping items off the top of the Leaning Tower of Pisa. He built his own telescope and made discoveries that proved Copernicus's [kuh-PER-nick-us] heliocentric theory. Which Italian scientist discovered Jupiter's four largest moons? GALILEO (GALILEI) 65-SS. After this document was approved by the Second Continental Congress on November 15, 1777, it was ratified by all states and went into effect on March 1, 1781. What document served as the United States’ first framing document until it was replaced eight years later by the U.S. Constitution?

Technically, this musical element applies to any notes that are played at the same time. Typically, these notes are combined into chords. What is this element of music that is closely related to melody?

This math property is illustrated by the following example. This property applies when adding and multiplying the quantity 6 plus 3 quantity closed times 4. Using what property allows you to multiply 6 times 4 and add it to the product of 3 times 4?

In this novel, 12-year-old Miranda receives notes from a homeless stranger known only as the Laughing Man. She discovers that the Laughing Man is a grown-up version of Marcus, who travels back in time to save Sal's life. What is this Newbery winner by Rebecca Stead?

In Kentucky geography, this word names a river in southeastern Kentucky, as well as a waterfall on that river referred to as “Niagara of the South”. What word also names the “gap” through which Daniel Boone journeyed into present day Kentucky?

This state of matter has a definite volume but takes the shape of its container. Its particles are attracted to each other but are still free to move over each other. Identify this phase that can freeze into a solid or evaporate into a gas.
Each level of a game has 35 questions and there are 12 levels in the game. Kerry only finishes 4 levels of the game. How many questions did he answer?

This nonfiction free verse book is set in the summer of 1869. Among its characters are the workers, builders, and passengers on the United States' first transcontinental railroad. Identify this Caldecott Medal winner by Brian Floca [FLOW-kuh].

This legendary college basketball coach won 876 games across his 41-seasons as head coach of the University of Kentucky. Identify the basketball coach for whom an arena in Lexington, Kentucky is named.

Music historians credit John Field with popularizing this composition type in the 1800's. Chopin [shoh-PAN] wrote over 20 of these works, which are often solo piano pieces. What composition's name comes from its suitability for nighttime performance?

Any object that undertakes this type of motion is a satellite. It is a repeating, regular path one object takes around a center of gravity. Identify this movement that the moon does around Earth and Earth does around the sun.

This part of a circuit may come in oil, mercury, or knife varieties. Under normal load conditions, it opens or closes an electrical circuit. Identify this device that you flip to turn on or off a light.

This free-reed wind instrument first gained popularity in 19th-century Austria and Germany. It uses bellows to move air, and buttons and keys to produce notes. What is this folk instrument often heard in polka music?

The travel form of this collection of geographic references was frequently required for long-distance travel prior to the introduction of GPS devices. Give the name for a collection of charts or maps.

This man's poem "A Dream Deferred" inspired the title for the play A Raisin in the Sun. In another poem he mused, quote, "Hold fast to dreams / For if dreams die / Life is a broken-winged bird / That cannot fly." Identify this Harlem Renaissance poet of "Mother to Son."
There are 15 bike racks in the park. Each rack will hold 5 bikes. If every rack is full, how many bikes are parked in the racks?

This ballet based on a short story originally featured choreography by Marius Petipa [MAIR-ee-us puh-tee-PAH]. It includes the "Waltz of the Flowers" and "Waltz of the Snowflakes," as well as the "Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy." Identify this Christmas ballet by Pyotr Tchaikovsky [PEET-ur chigh-KAWF-skee].

This author's first published novel was the American Library Association Notable Book Zeely. Later, she won the National Book Award for the same novel that made her the first African-American Newbery Medalist. Name the author of M. C. Higgins, the Great.

This class of rock can be foliated or non-foliated. Gneiss [NICE], soapstone, schist, quartzite, and marble are all examples. Which rock class forms when high temperatures and pressure alter a rock's chemical and physical properties?

Methods of extracting this natural resource include surface mining, strip mining, and mountaintop removal. Name this combustible resource that has historically been important to the economy of eastern Kentucky.

On Valentine's Day, Diego gave his mom a box of candy. The box had 3/5 pound of caramel, 3/5 pound of chocolate cherries, 3/5 pound of turtles, and 3/5 pound of milk chocolate pieces. As a mixed number, how many pounds of candy was in the box?
This element of a story can be limited or omniscient [ahm-NISH-unt]. It is always in the first, second, or third person. Give the three-word phrase for the perspective from which a story is told.

In communities undergoing this process, property values often rise at the cost of forcing out longtime residents who can no longer afford to live there. What term, beginning with “G”, names this process in which large numbers of wealthier individuals move into a formerly poorer neighborhood and transform its buildings and businesses?

This type of movement occurs in general, as opposed to personal, space. Examples include crawling, skipping, and hopping. Give the term for these movements that take the body from one place to another.

This natural phenomenon results from temperature changes in air, water, and land. It can bring dust, sand, snow, or rain, as Asia's monsoons do. Give the word for the movement of air near Earth's surface.
Sales tax is 6 percent on each dollar amount sold in Kentucky. How much sales tax would be charged on a sale of $6.00?
The fence around Kelly's pool is 120 feet long. How many yards long is the fence?

This folk character once brought his wife and children to steal the harvest from a goober pea patch. In other tales, he fell down a well, fooled Sis Cow, and got temporarily stuck to a tar baby. Give the name of this enemy of Br'er Fox in the Uncle Remus stories.

Minimum two-word answer required. John Winthrop was the first governor of this colony which was settled in 1630 by around 1,000 Puritans. Give the name of this colony in New England that chose Boston as its capital.

This man co-starred with his sister Adele in the Gershwin musical Funny Face. He included elements of ballroom, tap, and ballet in his dances for the movies Flying Down to Rio and Top Hat. Identify this onscreen partner of Ginger Rogers.

This terrestrial planet has two small, rocky moons: Phobos and Deimos. It contains the solar system's largest known volcano, Olympus Mons. Which one of Earth's neighbors is nicknamed the "red planet"?

These eukaryotes [yoo-KARE-ee-oats] resemble plants but are actually protists. They can be uni- or multicellular and live in water, on land, and even on animals. Seaweed is an example of what organism that comes in blue, green, red, and brown varieties?

In 1911, this ballerina founded a dance company that was the first to tour the globe. Before that, she attended the Imperial Ballet School and performed with the Ballets Russes [bal-AY ROOS]. Who was this dancer remembered for her solo The Dying Swan?
When this nursery rhyme first appeared, it mentioned a form of sport and fortune telling. In which nursery rhyme does the quick title character jump over a candlestick?

As a military commander, he is best remembered for leading a major failure at the Battle of the Monongahela in 1755. Name the British Major-General whose death in that battle ended his short time as the first commander-in-chief of the colonial forces during the French and Indian War.
Identify the type of angle by its properties. This angle is greater than zero degrees. What angle's measure is also less than 90 degrees?

In this type of stage, the area in front of the curtain is called the apron. Traditionally, it includes an arch that makes the stage look like a framed picture. What is this stage that the audience faces directly on only one side?
The Greek root "therm" is found in words like "thermometer" and "thermal." What is its English meaning?
A right triangle has two legs of length 12 units each. What is the area of this triangle in square units?
Along with oxygen, this is one of the byproducts of photosynthesis. Name this sugar that plants use for energy and to make cellulose and starch.

The Battle of Queenston Heights was the first major engagement of this war, and resulted in a British victory. Name this war fought between Great Britain and the United States which featured the burning of the U.S. capital.
The first part of this compound word is a synonym of "soil" or "dirt." The second part is a large swine. What is this animal that, on February 2nd, does or doesn't see its shadow?

A film, adapted from this man’s 1853 book, won the Oscar for Best Picture in 2014. Name the freeborn African American whose experience being kidnapped and sold into slavery was detailed in his memoir, 12 Years A Slave.
There are 5 black balls, 1 red ball, and 6 green balls in a bag. If you choose a red ball from the bag, you will win the game. What is the probability of choosing a red ball from the bag?
A French dish made with these mollusks is called escargot [es-kar-GO]. Their eyes sit at the end of stalks and they move by gliding on a slimy foot. Identify these shelled creatures similar to slugs.
This artistic element is three-dimensional, meaning it has length, width, and depth. What is this relative of shape?
A number sequence contains the fractions 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32, and so on. What is the sixth term in the sequence?

This art movement originated in New York City after World War Two. Action painting and color field painting were both part of this movement, whose artists included Mark Rothko and Jasper Johns. Name this movement that also produced Jackson Pollock's drip paintings.

These mammals give birth standing up and, as herbivores, mostly eat acacia [uh-KAY-shuh] leaves and twigs. They roam the African savanna in groups called towers and use their good eyesight to watch for hyenas and lions. What are these spotted creatures with exceptionally long necks?

This military campaign occurred during the early 1990's in response to an invasion in the nation of Kuwait. What was this campaign in response to an Iraq invasion under Saddam Hussein with his aim of acquiring oil reserves in Kuwait?

In certain situations, this punctuation mark can substitute for a comma, a semicolon, or--when paired--parentheses. Its em and en types are slightly different lengths. Identify this punctuation that closely resembles a hyphen.
Solve for X in the following inequality. X is greater than the sum of 1 plus 9. What is the solution for X?

On the right side of this fresco, angels surround a grey-bearded God. Located on the Sistine Chapel ceiling, it dramatizes the story from Genesis about the first man's origins. Give the title of this Michelangelo painting.

For the first time since this process began in 1790, participants engaging in the process in 2020 had the option to do so online or by phone. What process, conducted every 10-years, attempts to gain an accurate count of all individuals living within the United States?
This human organ is the only one that can float on water. Tuberculosis and pneumonia infect them, while emphysema can fatally impair them. What are these paired organs that allow you to breathe?

This part of speech may be reflexive, intensive, or demonstrative [duh-MON-struh-tiv]. Examples can also be indefinite, relative, or personal. What is this of part of speech of "she," "itself," and "anyone"?
Identify the adjective clause in the following sentence: "There is the tree that we are going to climb."
questions.a: THAT WE ARE GOING TO CLIMB

questions.q: Categories for this piece of equipment include probe, electron, and optical. Its simplest type includes an eyepiece, focusing knobs, and a slide that holds the specimen to be examined. What is this scientific tool for inspecting objects too small to be seen clearly by the naked eye?
Use the equation Y equals 10 times X. What is the value of Y when X equals one-half?

This company, which merged with Live Nation in 2010, has recently been heavily criticized for its handling of instances in which demand exceeds supply. Name this company who has been sued by fans and criticized directly by Taylor Swift following a disastrous pre-sale of the singer’s upcoming world tour.

Legend has it this goddess lives in the crater of Mount Kilauea [kill-uh-WAY-uh]. She presides over dancing, fire, and volcanoes. In another myth, which goddess created the Hawaiian Islands? PELE [PAY-lay] 61-AH. In 2022, this singer-songwriter temporarily broke Ticketmaster when the service tried to sell tickets for her Eras Tour. The year before, her ninth studio album, Folklore, won the Album of the Year Grammy. Who is this singer of "Anti-Hero" from her latest album, Midnights? (TAYLOR) SWIFT 62-LA. Spelling required. "The government made seat belt usage mandatory for all drivers and passengers." Spell the word in the previous sentence that is a synonym of "required." M-A-N-D-A-T-O-R-Y 63-MA. A regular polygon has interior angles that equal a total of 720 degrees. Each interior angle equals 120 degrees. How many sides does this polygon have? 6 (SIX SIDES) 64-SC. This man was likely the first person to use "battery," "charge," "positive," and "negative" in an electrical context. He invented a stove, bifocals, and the lightning rod. Identify this Philadelphia man, who also helped write the Declaration of Independence. (BENJAMIN) FRANKLIN 65-SS. Specific two-word answer required. The Seal of the President of the United States depicts one of these creatures holding an olive branch and 13 arrows in its talons. What bird of prey was chosen by the United States’ founders as the country’s national bird?
This word applies to the top line of choir music. It also describes the highest-pitched models of a particular instrument, such as the saxophone. Give this word for the highest singing voice.
Adding two nonzero non-negative numbers will always equal this type of number. What type of number has a value larger than zero?

In this novel, Lady Furnival orders John Aycliffe to murder the title 13-year-old. That orphan travels with Bear the wandering jester and, at the novel's conclusion, abandons the lead cross that proves his high parentage. Medieval England is the setting for what Newbery-winning Avi novel?

Murray State University is in this area of the extreme western part of Kentucky. The area is bounded partly by the Mississippi River, the Ohio River, and the Tennessee River. Identify this region of Kentucky named for the United State’s 7th president.

Occasionally, this temperature for a substance is not the same temperature as its freezing point. For water, it is 32 degrees Fahrenheit or 0 degrees Celsius. What is this point at which a solid turns into a liquid?
There are 20 students in art class. Each student created 45 paintings. How many paintings did the class complete?

This Caldecott winner advises the reader, quote, "Never leave a thumbtack where you might sit on it." Its title characters are a Napville policeman and his canine partner, who give safety tips to schoolchildren. Give the title of this Peggy Rathmann book.

This network of television stations was founded in Kentucky in 1968 and is today the largest such network of the Public Broadcast System, or PBS. Give the name of this educational television network which airs PBS television throughout Kentucky as well as coverage of local news and issues.

This type of entertainment began in Japan when a band failed to appear for a gig at a bar. James Corden used to host a "carpool" version of it. Give the word for an amateur singing to recorded instrumental accompaniment.

A spiral staircase is a large example of this simple machine. It consists of an inclined plane wrapped around a central rod. Name this simple machine, which can also be a metal fastener that is rotated into wood.

In the U.S., this type of current's frequency is 60 Hertz. Nikola Tesla preferred this kind of current, which a transformer can convert from the electricity in power lines. Which type of electricity constantly switches directions?

This string instrument originated in Africa, came to America with slaves, and was later exported to Europe. Its body looks like a large tambourine, while its five metal strings pass over a fretted neck. Name this instrument popular with bluegrass musicians.

Examples of this form of geographic grouping in the United States include Alaska’s Aleutians, the Florida Keys, and the islands that form the state of Hawaii. Give the term for a group or chain of islands.
An example of this figure of speech is, "I'm so hungry I could eat a hippo." Identify this type of exaggeration that is often funny and isn't meant to be taken literally.

Fernando fills a fruit platter with strawberries, bananas, and blackberries. One-sixth of the plate has bananas and one-half of the plate has strawberries. In lowest terms, what part of the plate contains blackberries?

Subtitled A Tone Poem for Orchestra, this work premiered in Carnegie Hall in 1928. The composer called it a "rhapsodic ballet," and it inspired a 1951 movie musical starring Gene Kelly. The French capital's name appears in the title of which George Gershwin work?

This novel's characters include Louise the Larger, a black garden snake, and a dragon called Proginoskes [prog-ih-NO-skeez]. Meg Murry travels inside her brother Charles Wallace's mitochondria in order to save him from a deadly disease. This is the plot of which fantasy novel from Madeleine L'Engle's Time Quintet?
Rocks in this class are either extrusive or intrusive. Gabbro, granite, and basalt all belong to this category. Give the name for rocks that form when magma or lava cools and solidifies.

Due to its reputation for producing a certain beverage, a region of this U.S. state is often called “Wine Country”. Name the western state whose "Wine Country" is centered around the Napa Valley near San Francisco.
A restaurant prepared 5 bacon quiches for lunch. Only 2 and 2/3 of the quiche was served at lunch. How much of the quiche was not served?
This part of a plot may begin after the story's inciting incident. On Freytag's Pyramid, the left slanting side represents it. Which part of a story occurs between the exposition and climax?

An important figure in England’s Elizabethan age, he was responsible for sending settlers to the New World to establish Roanoke Colony, the so-called “Lost Colony”. Give the name of this English statesman for whom the capital of North Carolina is named.

This dance style's pioneers include Bill "Bojangles" Robinson and Savion [SAY-vee-ahn] Glover. Among its basic steps are the spank, brush, flap, and shuffle. Identify this percussive dance that requires shoes with metal plates on the soles.

In the Köppen classification system, this is the only category that isn't entirely based on temperature. It applies to the semi-arid steppe and the arid desert and includes Earth's hottest spots. What is this climate named for the small amount of annual precipitation it receives?
Kevin answered 90 percent of the questions correctly on his science test. He answered 45 questions correctly. How many questions were on the test?
Samson buys a four pound bag of soil to use in eight flowerpots. If he divides the soil equally, how many ounces of soil will he put in each pot?
This tall tale man worked alongside a small donkey he named Tamarack. He once cleared 100 acres of forest using an axe he borrowed from his brother. Who was this miniature sibling of Paul Bunyan?

In Spanish colonial America, individuals with this heritage were generally not allowed to become leaders in the church or government. Individuals were generally considered as being of this heritage if they were of European or African descent but born in the West Indies. Give the name for this ethnic group that is sometimes confused with the Cajun ethnicity due to both groups’ large populations in southern Louisiana.

Before Martha Graham, this woman also explored freer movement than ballet provided. She often danced barefoot in loose tunics to mimic the Greek and Roman sculptures she admired. Name this so-called "mother of modern dance," who died when her scarf was caught in a car tire.

After the telescope's invention, this was the first planet to be discovered. Voyager 2 flew by this gas giant, whose methane gives it a blue-green appearance. What is this seventh planet from the sun?
This five syllable adjective applies to all bacteria and archaea [AHR-kee-uh], as well as many protists. Give this adjective for organisms that consist of a single cell.

This ancient civilization celebrated the City Dionysia [die-uh-NIZH-ee-uh] festival, where masked actors performed. Aristophanes [air-uh-STOFF-uh-neez] wrote its most lasting comedies, while Aeschylus [ES-kuh-luhs], Sophocles [SOF-uh-kleez], and Euripides [yuh-RIP-uh-deez] wrote many of its tragedies. In what present-day country can you see theatrical ruins in Athens?

This activist was fined $100 for casting a ballot in the 1872 U.S. presidential election. In response, she gave a speech saying, quote, "It was we, the people; not we, the white male citizens...who formed the Union." Name this suffragette who, in 1979, became the first woman to appear on a circulating U.S. coin.

Henry Wadsworth Longfellow wrote a poem about this Plymouth colony resident’s unrequited love for Priscilla Mullins. Name the subject of this poem who served as the Plymouth Colony’s military advisor.
The measurement of angle A is 30 degrees and the measure of angle B is 60 degrees. What term defines the relationship between angles A and B?

This 15th-century theatrical form featured masked actors portraying stock characters. Slapstick comedy and improvisation were hallmarks of this style, which inspired England's Punch and Judy shows. Identify this genre, whose name is Italian for "comedy of art."

In legal terms, this word names an object or document that is shown in court and referenced in written evidence. It derives from a Latin word meaning "to hold forth" or "to have." Give this word that means "to present for inspection."
The bases of a trapezoid are 6 units and 10 units. Its height is 18 units. What is the area of the trapezoid in square units?
Like spores, this part of a plant can be distributed by wind, water, or animals. It consists of a coat, endosperm, and embryo. Name this fertilized ovule that germinates into a new plant.

Forces led by William Henry Harrison defeated the brother of this Shawnee leader at the Battle of Tippecanoe. He was later himself killed by Harrison’s forces at the Battle of the Thames [temz]. Give the name of this Shawnee chief who joined forces with the British to capture Detroit during the War of 1812.

One of this word's definitions is, quote, "a dishonest scheme, trick, business, or activity." Another is, quote, "a loud noise or clamor." Identify this word that names equipment used in squash, badminton, and tennis.

An often-quoted military order from this battle is, “Don’t fire until you see the whites of their eyes.” This battle was fought on June 17, 1775 in Charlestown, Massachusetts during the Siege of Boston. Identify this early, major battle of the American Revolution which, though won by the British, provided much needed optimism to American forces for the fighting ahead.
A spinner is divided into three equal sectors. Two of the sectors are purple and one sector is orange. What is the probability of the spinner NOT landing on purple?

In the nests or hills these insects make, they divide themselves into males, workers, soldiers, and a queen. They can be yellow, brown, red, or black and use their two sets of jaws for eating, fighting, and carrying materials. What are these insects, whose varieties include carpenter and fire?
This substance mixes glue with chalk, plaster, or gypsum. Give the Italian name of this paint used to prime wood or canvas.
Use a division sign in your answer. Harry had 27 cookies and he put the same number of cookies into each of three bags. What numerical expression would show how many cookies are in each bag?

This type of religious artwork's most frequent subjects include angels, saints, and the Virgin Mary. Traditionally, they are painted with egg tempera on wooden surfaces. What are these sacred artworks in Orthodox Christianity, which share their name with a clickable picture on a computer?

This large mammal's eight species include spectacled, sun, and sloth. Most of its species hibernate and are omnivorous, but they all belong to the family Ursidae [OOR-see-day]. Name this group that also includes the grizzly and giant panda.

The holder of this local government position typically provides security within courts, serves legal documents, and helps to police and enforce laws in certain areas. Give the title of this locally elected official and sworn law enforcement officer.
Which words need to be capitalized in the following sentence? "At the North Pole, you can see reindeer, polar bears, and Arctic foxes."
Solve for X. Nineteen cupcakes have strawberry icing and X cupcakes have chocolate icing. If these add up to 24 cupcakes altogether, how many cupcakes have chocolate icing?

This artist depicted a popular Parisian entertainment in his 1890 painting The Can-Can. Critics classify his Bathers at Asnières [ahn-YAIR] as both Post-Impressionist and Neo-Impressionist. Name this Pointillist painter of Young Woman Powdering Herself.

The U.S. Constitution's fifth amendment features a clause known by this two-word term which protects individuals from being punished multiple times for the same offense. The term also refers to the right to not be prosecuted a second time after being acquitted or convicted through trial. Identify this protection which shares its name with the second round of a popular trivia game show.

When this body part's tiny glands become infected, a stye forms. Technically called cilia [SILL-ee-uh], they are made of keratin and grow from follicles. Identify these small hairs that prevent dust and other foreign matter from entering the eye.
State the antecedent [ant-uh-SEE-dent] of the pronoun in the following sentence: "Natalie received an A on her presentation."
One of these phrases is part of the sentence, "I asked the children to pick up their toys." Name this kind of phrase that consists of "to" and a verb.

Even though people use them interchangeably, this concept is different from the world wide web. It links governmental, educational, and commercial networks that use the same communication protocols. Identify this system for connecting millions of computers around the world.
Three real numbers are ordered so the second number is twice the first number and the third number is three times the second number. If the first number is 4, what is the third number?

First issued in 1999, this form of currency is the world’s second-most traded form of currency, second only to the U.S. Dollar. Give the name of the official currency of most members of the European Union.

Various Native American cultures have traditionally played the hand, foot, water, and powwow kinds of this instrument. West Africans created the djembe [JEM-bay] and the talking one of these percussion instruments, which they used to communicate over long distances. Name this instrument with a wooden body and a membrane head that can be struck by the hands or sticks. DRUM(S) 61-AH. This player recently broke Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's NBA record for most career points scored. After graduating from high school, he joined the Cleveland Cavaliers, whom he led to an NBA Championship in 2016. Identify this athlete, who also helped win championships for the Miami Heat and the Los Angeles Lakers. (LEBRON) JAMES 62-LA. Spelling required. "A community pool is situated adjacent to the recreational center." Spell the word from the previous sentence that means "next to." A-D-J-A-C-E-N-T 63-MA. A circular rug has a circumference of 14 pi units. What is the rug's radius in units? 7 (SEVEN UNITS) 64-SC. This physicist investigated the explosions of the space shuttles Challenger and Columbia. Before the Challenger's explosion, she had taken two trips aboard it in 1983 and 1984. Who was this first American woman in space? (SALLY) RIDE 65-SS. These three words are included on the Seal of Kentucky above a picture of two men shaking hands. What three words precede the words “Divided We Fall” in a popular American slogan?

Rarely, this part of sheet music contains one or more natural symbols. It can appear after a barline, but is normally found immediately after the clef. Name this set of sharps or flats that tells whether a piece is in, for example, D minor or A major.
This number is 10 times as large as 60. What number is equal to 60 times 10?

In this novel, Uncle Ob views Cletus Underwood as his so-called "afterlife antenna." With Summer, they travel to Putnam County, West Virginia, to ask a medium for help in contacting the deceased title character. Give the name of this Newbery Medal-winning Cynthia Rylant novel.

The only place in which this distinct type of weather-related phenomenon regularly occurs in the Western Hemisphere is at the Cumberland Falls in southeastern Kentucky. What is this type of phenomenon which is similar to a rainbow but is produced by a different light source?
This word describes objects that allow some, but not all, light to pass through them. What is this quality between transparent and opaque?
It takes 10 tiles to go across the room. Each tile is 12 inches long. How many inches long is the room?

Like its protagonist, this book's author is a member of the Turtle Mountain Band of Ojibwe [oh-JIB-way]. In the story, her tribe fights the so-called "black snake" of an oil pipeline that threatens a natural resource. What is this recent Caldecott Medal Winner, written by Carole Lindstrom?
Since 1981, this two-door luxury sports car has been produced in Bowling Green, Kentucky, home of a museum dedicated to it. Give the name of this iconic sports car manufactured by Chevrolet.

Musicians from this city include Aretha Franklin and Eminem. In 1959, Berry Gordy founded a record company there that successfully blended white and African-American popular music. Identify this Midwestern birthplace of Motown.
This simple machine lets heavy objects be slid, rather than lifted, to a higher point. Slides and ramps are both examples of what simple machine--a flat surface with one end higher than the other?

Every magnet is called a "di-" one of these because it has two of them. Like ones repel each other, while opposite ones attract each other. Identify these ends of a magnet that respectively point north and south.

This woodwind pitched in B-flat or A has 17 keys, including an octave key to reach higher notes. Its solo opens George Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue, and it represents the cat in Prokofiev's [pro-KAH-fee-evz] Peter and the Wolf. Give the name of this single-reed woodwind.

The six U.S. states generally said to comprise this region are Rhode Island, Massachusetts, Connecticut, New Hampshire, Maine, and Vermont. Give the two-word name for a region in the American Northeast which is also used by a professional football franchise known as the Patriots.
Among this man's poems for youngsters are "The Lamplighter" and "My Shadow." Both appear in his 1885 volume A Child's Garden of Verses. Identify this author of the novel Treasure Island.
The baker cuts a cherry pie into 12 equal pieces. He sells 3 pieces of the cherry pie. In lowest terms, what fraction of the cherry pie was left?

This composer nicknamed his Sixth Symphony Pastoral. He originally dedicated his Third Symphony to Napoleon, but later named it Eroica [uh-ROW-ick-uh]. Name this Classical and Romantic Era composer, who also wrote a Choral Symphony.

In this novel, homeless Buddy Clark belongs to a city-wide network called the "Tomorrow Billys." He helps the protagonist, a 300-pound musical prodigy, escape his overprotective mother. What is this Virginia Hamilton novel?
This type of fossil can be internal or external. When one fills in, a cast fossil forms. Identify this negative image of an organism that makes an impression in substrate.

Roughly half of the worldwide supply of this type of plant has been bred by a single ranch based in California, the Paul Ecke Ranch. Recognized by its green and brilliant red foliage, this plant accounts for around one in every 4 potted plants purchased annually in the United States, with much of those purchases made in the later part of the year. Name this plant, popularly displayed at Christmastime.

Eighteen students played basketball, six students played volleyball, and five students played softball at recess. What is the ratio of the students playing basketball to the total students playing volleyball and softball?
questions.a: 18:11 (EIGHTEEN TO ELEVEN) (ACCEPT: EIGHTEEN OVER 11 OR EIGHTEEN-ELEVENTHS)

questions.q: This reference work's name derives from the Greek for "well-rounded education." Like the dictionary, it once consisted of many large books whose entries on a wide variety of topics were arranged alphabetically. Name this reference work still produced by Britannica.

The name of this mythical location can now refer to any supposedly miraculous cure against aging. Name this mythical spring for which Juan Ponce de Leon was searching in 1513 when he landed in modern-day Florida.

The ballroom version of this dance comes in both American and International Styles. Its slow, slow, quick, quick, slow steps stretch over 8 beats. What is this dance claimed by both Uruguay and Argentina?
In general, these clouds pop up on sunny days to indicate fair weather. They are low clouds that grow vertically from flat bottoms. Give the name of these clouds that resemble puffy cotton balls.
Every question on the math test is worth 5 percent of the total. How many questions comprise the complete test?
In the United States, one metric ton equals 1,016.05 (SAY: One thousand sixteen point zero five) kilograms. How many kilograms are equivalent to 3 metric tons?

One tall tale explains that this man once splashed a frog with water and a thunderstorm resulted. In other stories, he overcomes blizzards, cyclones, and grasshoppers and witnesses nature creating popcorn balls. Identify this fictional Swedish-born Nebraska farmer.

Though this 47-page work was published anonymously when it was first printed in January 1776, its author was Thomas Paine. Give the name of Paine’s pamphlet which became a best-selling sensation in colonial America and helped strengthen support for declaring independence from Great Britain.

This choreographer's first dance for a ballet company was 1944's Fancy Free. He was both choreographer and director for the musicals Gypsy and Fiddler on the Roof. Give the name of this West Side Story choreographer.

This astronomical body can originate when a large star's gravity pulls it inward on itself. The object's gravity also pulls in any matter that approaches. Identify these incredibly dense bodies from which no electromagnetic radiation, including light, can escape.
This part of a cell mostly consists of proteins and phospholipids [FOSS-fo-lip-idz]. What is this porous barrier that separates a cell's interior from the outside environment?

This musical's songs include "Human Again," "If I Can't Love Her," and "A Change in Me." Like the movie on which it's based, it features the personified objects Lumière [loo-mee-AIR], Cogsworth, Babette, Chip, and Mrs. Potts. Name this Disney musical about Belle and a disguised prince.

In this fairy tale, a young man's older brothers inherit their father's mill and donkey. However, the youngest son marries a princess because his pet kills an ogre and brings the king gifts. Identify this fairy tale about a shoe-wearing cat.
This revolt against Colonial Governor William Berkeley resulted in the burning of the Jamestown settlement. Give the name of this first popular revolt to occur in the English colonies.
The sum of the interior angles of this regular polygon equals 1,260 degrees. Each interior angle of this geometric figure measures 140 degrees. What regular polygon has nine sides?
This closely woven white cloth is tightly wrapped around a wooden structure. Artists often prepare it with gesso [JESS-oh]. Name this hemp, linen, or cotton fabric that artists paint on.
Correct the following sentence, if necessary: When he's finished playing with the ball, he'll give it to you or me.
A parallelogram has a height of 8 units and a base of 10 units. What is the area of the parallelogram in square units?

Forests filled with this type of tree exist in northeastern Asia, western Eurasia, and eastern North America. Chestnuts, birches, beeches, elms, oaks, and maples are all examples. What do we call trees that shed their leaves?

This warship was newly built when it took part in the first engagement between two ironclad warships at the Battle of Hampton Roads in March 1862. Give the name of the Union vessel which engaged in that influential naval battle with the rebuilt USS Merrimack.
The first half of this compound word is an animal that runs in the Kentucky Derby. The second half is an antonym of "work." State this compound word that refers to a rough, rowdy type of fun.

Along with a navigator, Fred Noonan, this aviator mysteriously disappeared over the Pacific Ocean in 1937. Identify the iconic aviator who, in 1932, became the first woman to complete a solo flight across the Atlantic Ocean.
Hot Dog Haven is offering a special menu with four different buns, eight different toppings, and two different hot dog lengths. How many different hot dogs can be ordered from this special menu?

Two-word name, please. This mollusk is most likely either the largest or second-largest living invertebrate. Its massive eye is more than 10 inches in diameter, while its whole body can weigh up to 2,000 pounds. Identify this marine animal with 2 large fins, 2 long tentacles, and 8 arms.

This type of paint is more vibrant and less expensive than oil paint. Commercially available since the 1950's, it is fast-drying and water-based. Name this alternative to watercolor and tempera paint.
The first four numbers in a sequence are 16, 32, 64, and 128. What is the fifth term in the sequence?

This ancient Greek architectural order is found on Rome's Pantheon and the Temple of Olympian Zeus in Athens. Its thin columns have vertical grooves and capitals sculpted to resemble acanthus [uh-KAN-thus] leaves. Identify this most elaborate Greek architectural order.

For certain amphibian species, this is the name for their aquatic larval stage. Typically lasting from 1 to 3 months, it includes the transformation of gills into lungs, the tail's resorption, and the growth of hind limbs. Identify this stage between egg and froglet or toadlet.

Since 2005, the title of this highest ranking official within the U.S. government’s judicial branch has been held by John Roberts. What judicial position is typically viewed as being the most influential member of the U.S. Supreme Court?

If this punctuation is found at the end of a sentence, it contains an extra dot. It shows that one or more words has been omitted from a sentence. Name this punctuation mark that usually looks like three periods.
Tommy is stacking red and white blocks into identical stacks. He has 4 red blocks and 14 white blocks. What is the greatest number of stacks he can make without having any blocks left over?

This artist completed portraits of Elizabeth Taylor, Marilyn Monroe, and Elvis Presley. He silk-screened wooden crates to resemble Brillo boxes and painted a series of Coca-Cola themed works. Identify this Pop artist of Campbell's Soup Cans.

This amendment was added to the U.S. Constitution in 1795 and deals with an issue known as state sovereign immunity. Which Constitutional amendment, which protects states from being sued by citizens of other states, was the first amendment added after the Bill of Rights?

Early in her career, this woman cared for sick and wounded Crimean War servicemen in Turkey. She revolutionized hospitals by insisting on sanitary conditions and good diets for patients. Who was this woman who made nursing a respectable female career?
This type of phrase is part of the sentence, "Running with scissors is a dangerous activity." In it, a verb acts as a noun. Name this type of phrase containing a verb that ends in -ing.
What is the following sentence's grammatical structure? "I passed the test, but I would've gotten an A if I had studied harder."
Scientists working in this branch of zoology may study beetles, caterpillars, or bees. What do we call the study of insects?
A Lego set costs $15.99. Harold buys two sets. Discounting tax, how much money did he spend?
Prior to collapsing, FTX was a leading company concerned with the exchange of this form of currency of which Bitcoin is an example. Give the name for this form of digital currency.

This country's tribes include the Ewe [AY-way], Fante, and Ashanti [uh-SHAHN-tee]. For 150 years, it was the center of Britain's African slave trade, with about half a million of its people being transported to the American colonies. Which West African country gave us the colorful kente [KEN-tay] cloth?
